AffineMap.mk'.comment:
Construct an affine map by verifying the relation between the map and its linear part at one
base point. Namely, this function takes a map `f : P₁ → P₂`, a linear map `f' : V₁ →ₗ[k] V₂`, and
a point `p` such that for any other point `p'` we have `f p' = f' (p' -ᵥ p) +ᵥ f p`.

explanatories.AffineMap.toFun: This defines a function that takes an affine map between two affine spaces and returns the corresponding point-to-point mapping between those spaces.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.
explanatories.AffineMap.linear: This defines a method to extract the linear part of an affine map between two affine spaces, resulting in a linear transformation between their corresponding vector spaces.
explanatories.AffineMap.map_vadd': This theorem asserts that an affine map satisfies a compatibility condition with vector addition, relating the image of the sum of a point and a vector to the sum of the image of the point and the linear transformation of the vector.
explanatories.vadd_vsub_assoc: This theorem asserts that in an additive torsor, adding a group element to one point and then subtracting another point yields the same result as first subtracting the two points and then adding the group element.
explanatories.vadd_vadd: This theorem demonstrates that the addition of two vectors in an additive action distributes over vector addition with a third vector, maintaining the structure of vector addition.

AffineMap.mk'.fullDefinition: def mk' (f : P1 → P2) (f' : V1 →ₗ[k] V2) (p : P1) (h : ∀ p' : P1, f p' = f' (p' -ᵥ p) +ᵥ f p) :     P1 →ᵃ[k] P2 where   toFun := f   linear := f'   map_vadd' p' v := by rw [h, h p', vadd_vsub_assoc, f'.map_add, vadd_vadd]
AffineMap.mk'.description: This definition constructs an affine map by establishing the relationship between a given function, its linear component, and a reference point.

AffineMap.pi.comment:
`pi` construction for affine maps. From a family of affine maps it produces an affine
map into a family of affine spaces.

This is the affine version of `LinearMap.pi`.

AffineMap.pi.fullDefinition: def pi (f : (i : ι) → (P1 →ᵃ[k] φp i)) : P1 →ᵃ[k] ((i : ι) → φp i) where   toFun m a := f a m   linear := LinearMap.pi (fun a ↦ (f a).linear)   map_vadd' _ _ := funext fun _ ↦ map_vadd _ _ _
AffineMap.pi.description: This definition outlines a construction that generates a single affine map from a collection of affine maps, resulting in a mapping from an affine space to a family of affine spaces.

  f = g
AffineMap.pi_ext_zero.comment:
Two affine maps from a Pi-tyoe of modules `(i : ι) → φv i` are equal if they are equal in their
operation on `Pi.single` and at zero. Analogous to `LinearMap.pi_ext`. See also `pi_ext_nonempty`,
which instead of agrement at zero requires `Nonempty ι`.

AffineMap.pi_ext_zero.description: This theorem asserts that two affine maps from a product of modules are equal if they agree on single elements of the product and also at the zero vector.

slope.code:
slope.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {PE : Type u_3} [Field k] [AddCommGroup E] [Module k E]
  [AddTorsor E PE] (f : k → PE) (a b : k) : E
slope.comment:
`slope f a b = (b - a)⁻¹ • (f b -ᵥ f a)` is the slope of a function `f` on the interval
`[a, b]`. Note that `slope f a a = 0`, not the derivative of `f` at `a`.
slope.fullDefinition: def slope (f : k → PE) (a b : k) : E :=   (b - a)⁻¹ • (f b -ᵥ f a)
slope.description: This defines the slope of a function over a specified interval as the ratio of the change in the function's outputs to the change in its inputs.

slope_fun_def.code:
slope_fun_def.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {PE : Type u_3} [Field k] [AddCommGroup E] [Module k E]
  [AddTorsor E PE] (f : k → PE) : slope f = fun a b => (b - a)⁻¹ • (f b -ᵥ f a)
slope_fun_def.description: This theorem establishes that the slope function defined for a given function is equivalent to a specific formula expressing the slope in terms of the function's values at two points.

slope_def_field.code: slope_def_field.{u_1} {k : Type u_1} [Field k] (f : k → k) (a b : k) : slope f a b = (f b - f a) / (b - a)
slope_def_field.description: This theorem states that the slope of a function defined over a field can be expressed as the ratio of the difference in the function's values at two points to the difference in the points themselves.

slope_fun_def_field.code: slope_fun_def_field.{u_1} {k : Type u_1} [Field k] (f : k → k) (a : k) : slope f a = fun b => (f b - f a) / (b - a)
slope_fun_def_field.description: This theorem asserts that the slope of a function at a specific point can be expressed as a function that measures the change in the function's value relative to a reference point.

slope.eq_1.code:
slope.eq_1.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {PE : Type u_3} [Field k] [AddCommGroup E] [Module k E]
  [AddTorsor E PE] (f : k → PE) (a b : k) : slope f a b = (b - a)⁻¹ • (f b -ᵥ f a)
slope.eq_1.description: This theorem confirms that the calculated slope of a function over an interval is equal to a specific expression involving the changes in the function's values and the interval's endpoints.

slope_same.code:
slope_same.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {PE : Type u_3} [Field k] [AddCommGroup E] [Module k E]
  [AddTorsor E PE] (f : k → PE) (a : k) : slope f a a = 0
slope_same.description: This theorem asserts that the slope of a function at a single point is zero.

slope_def_module.code:
slope_def_module.{u_1, u_2} {k : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Field k] [AddCommGroup E] [Module k E] (f : k → E)
  (a b : k) : slope f a b = (b - a)⁻¹ • (f b - f a)
slope_def_module.description: This theorem defines the slope of a function between two points as the scaled difference in the function's values over the difference in the input points.

sub_smul_slope.code:
sub_smul_slope.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {PE : Type u_3} [Field k] [AddCommGroup E] [Module k E]
  [AddTorsor E PE] (f : k → PE) (a b : k) : (b - a) • slope f a b = f b -ᵥ f a
sub_smul_slope.description: This theorem states that scaling the slope of a function over an interval by the interval's width equals the difference in the function's values at the endpoints.

sub_smul_slope_vadd.code:
sub_smul_slope_vadd.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {PE : Type u_3} [Field k] [AddCommGroup E]
  [Module k E] [AddTorsor E PE] (f : k → PE) (a b : k) : (b - a) • slope f a b +ᵥ f a = f b
sub_smul_slope_vadd.description: This theorem asserts that adding the scaled slope of a function over an interval to the function's value at the start of that interval results in the function's value at the end of the interval.

slope_vadd_const.code:
slope_vadd_const.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {PE : Type u_3} [Field k] [AddCommGroup E] [Module k E]
  [AddTorsor E PE] (f : k → E) (c : PE) : (slope fun x => f x +ᵥ c) = slope f
slope_vadd_const.description: This theorem states that the slope of a function adjusted by adding a constant value is the same as the slope of the original function.

slope_sub_smul.code:

Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint.comment:
A weighted sum of the results of subtracting a base point from the
given points, as a linear map on the weights.  The main cases of
interest are where the sum of the weights is 0, in which case the sum
is independent of the choice of base point, and where the sum of the
weights is 1, in which case the sum added to the base point is
independent of the choice of base point.

Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint.fullDefinition: def weightedVSubOfPoint (p : ι → P) (b : P) : (ι → k) →ₗ[k] V :=   ∑ i ∈ s, (LinearMap.proj i : (ι → k) →ₗ[k] k).smulRight (p i -ᵥ b)
Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint.description: This definition describes a linear map representing a weighted sum of differences between a set of points and a base point in an affine space.

Finset.weightedVSub_apply.code:

  [Module k V] [S : AffineSpace V P] {ι : Type u_4} (s : Finset ι) (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) :
  (s.weightedVSub p) w = ∑ i ∈ s, w i • (p i -ᵥ Classical.choice ⋯)
Finset.weightedVSub_apply.comment:
Applying `weightedVSub` with given weights.  This is for the case
where a result involving a default base point is OK (for example, when
that base point will cancel out later); a more typical use case for
`weightedVSub` would involve selecting a preferred base point with
`weightedVSub_eq_weightedVSubOfPoint_of_sum_eq_zero` and then
using `weightedVSubOfPoint_apply`.
Finset.weightedVSub_apply.description: This theorem describes how to compute a weighted sum of vector differences from a default base point using specified weights over a finite set of points.

from the given points, added to that base point, as an affine map on
the weights.  This is intended to be used when the sum of the weights
is 1, in which case it is an affine combination (barycenter) of the
points with the given weights; that condition is specified as a
hypothesis on those lemmas that require it.

explanatories.Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint: This definition describes a linear map representing a weighted sum of differences between a set of points and a base point in an affine space.
explanatories.AddTorsor.nonempty: This theorem states that any additive torsor over an additive group contains at least one element.
explanatories.Finset.weightedVSub: This definition describes a linear map that computes the weighted sum of the differences between given points and a default base point, specifically under the condition that the total weight is zero.
explanatories.vadd_vadd: This theorem demonstrates that the addition of two vectors in an additive action distributes over vector addition with a third vector, maintaining the structure of vector addition.
explanatories.vadd_eq_add: This theorem demonstrates that the vector addition operation coincides with the ordinary addition operation for elements of a type that supports addition.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.
explanatories.AffineMap.linear: This defines a method to extract the linear part of an affine map between two affine spaces, resulting in a linear transformation between their corresponding vector spaces.

explanatories.LinearMap.proj: This definition introduces a linear map that extracts a specific component from a family of modules indexed by a set.
explanatories.Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint: This definition describes a linear map representing a weighted sum of differences between a set of points and a base point in an affine space.
explanatories.LinearMap.sum_apply: This theorem demonstrates that applying a linear map to a sum of elements is equivalent to summing the results of applying the linear map to each individual element.
explanatories.vadd_vsub_assoc: This theorem asserts that in an additive torsor, adding a group element to one point and then subtracting another point yields the same result as first subtracting the two points and then adding the group element.
explanatories.vsub_vadd_eq_vsub_sub: This theorem establishes that subtracting the sum of a group element and one point from another point is equivalent to first subtracting the point from the other and then subtracting the group element.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.AffineMap.linear: This defines a method to extract the linear part of an affine map between two affine spaces, resulting in a linear transformation between their corresponding vector spaces.
explanatories.Finset.sum_add_distrib: The theorem demonstrates that the sum of values obtained by adding two functions over a finite set equals the sum of the values from each function computed separately over the same set.
explanatories.Prod.fst: This defines a function that retrieves the first element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Prod.snd: This defines a function that retrieves the second element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp: This definition states that the composition of two linear maps, each between different modules over semirings, results in another linear map that connects the first and last modules directly.
explanatories.LinearMap.fst: This definition describes a linear map that projects the first component from a product of two modules.
explanatories.LinearMap.snd: This definition describes a linear map that projects the second component from a product of two modules.
explanatories.add_sub: In a structure with addition and subtraction, adding the difference of two elements to a third element is equivalent to adding one element to the third and then subtracting the second element.
explanatories.sub_add_eq_add_sub: In a subtraction commutative monoid, adding an element to the result of subtracting one element from another is the same as adding that element to the original and then subtracting the first element.
explanatories.Prod.mk_vadd_mk: This theorem establishes that adding a pair of group elements to a pair of points in their respective torsors results in the point obtained by adding the first element to the first point and the second element to the second point.

AffineMap.weightedVSubOfPoint.fullDefinition: def weightedVSubOfPoint (w : ι → k) : (ι → P) × P →ᵃ[k] V where   toFun p := s.weightedVSubOfPoint p.fst p.snd w   linear := ∑ i ∈ s, w i • ((LinearMap.proj i).comp (LinearMap.fst _ _ _) - LinearMap.snd _ _ _)   map_vadd' := by     rintro ⟨p, b⟩ ⟨v, b'⟩     -- Porting note: needed to give `Prod.mk_vadd_mk` a hint     simp [LinearMap.sum_apply, Finset.weightedVSubOfPoint, vsub_vadd_eq_vsub_sub,      vadd_vsub_assoc,      add_sub, ← sub_add_eq_add_sub, smul_add, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Prod.mk_vadd_mk v]
AffineMap.weightedVSubOfPoint.description: This definition describes a function that represents a weighted sum of points as an affine map in a given vector space, with specified weights for each point.

explanatories.AffineSubspace.map: This definition describes how the image of an affine subspace, when transformed by an affine map, results in another affine subspace.
explanatories.AffineEquiv.constVAdd: This definition describes an affine equivalence that shifts every point in an affine space by a fixed vector, effectively translating the space while preserving its structure.
explanatories.AffineMap.ext: This theorem asserts that two affine maps are considered equal if they produce the same output for every input when treated as functions.
explanatories.zero_vadd: This theorem asserts that adding the zero element of an additive monoid to any vector results in the same vector.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.AffineSubspace.map_id: This theorem demonstrates that applying the identity affine map to an affine subspace results in the same subspace.
explanatories.AddAction.add_vadd: This theorem demonstrates that the vector addition operation is associative when combined with the addition operation of the underlying additive monoid.
explanatories.AffineSubspace.map_map: This theorem states that applying two affine maps in succession to an affine subspace is equivalent to applying the composition of those two maps directly to the same subspace.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Submodule.map_id: This theorem asserts that applying the identity linear map to a submodule preserves the submodule itself.

AffineSubspace.pointwiseAddAction.fullDefinition: protected def pointwiseAddAction : AddAction V (AffineSubspace k P) where   vadd x S := S.map (AffineEquiv.constVAdd k P x)   zero_vadd p := ((congr_arg fun f => p.map f) <| AffineMap.ext <| zero_vadd _).trans p.map_id   add_vadd _ _ p :=     ((congr_arg fun f => p.map f) <| AffineMap.ext <| add_vadd _ _).trans (p.map_map _ _).symm

  [OrderedAddCommGroup E] [Module k E] [OrderedSMul k E] {f : k → E} {a b r : k} (h : 0 < r * (b - a)) :
  f ((lineMap a b) r) ≤ (lineMap (f a) (f b)) r ↔ slope f a ((lineMap a b) r) ≤ slope f a b
map_le_lineMap_iff_slope_le_slope_left.comment:
Given `c = lineMap a b r`, `a < c`, the point `(c, f c)` is non-strictly below the
segment `[(a, f a), (b, f b)]` if and only if `slope f a c ≤ slope f a b`.

all others along the line joining them to this member, the resulting new family of points is affine-

AffineBasis.basisOf.code:
AffineBasis.basisOf.{u_1, u_3, u_4, u_5} {ι : Type u_1} {k : Type u_3} {V : Type u_4} {P : Type u_5} [AddCommGroup V]
  [AffineSpace V P] [Ring k] [Module k V] (b : AffineBasis ι k P) (i : ι) : Basis { j // j ≠ i } k V
AffineBasis.basisOf.comment:
Given an affine basis for an affine space `P`, if we single out one member of the family, we
obtain a linear basis for the model space `V`.

The linear basis corresponding to the singled-out member `i : ι` is indexed by `{j : ι // j ≠ i}`
and its `j`th element is `b j -ᵥ b i`. (See `basisOf_apply`.)

explanatories.Inhabited.mk: Any type that has a default element is considered inhabited.
explanatories.AffineBasis.mk: This theorem constructs an affine basis from a set of points that are affine independent and span the entire space.

explanatories.AffineBasis.ind: This theorem states that any affine basis is affinely independent.
explanatories.AffineBasis.tot: This theorem states that the affine span of the range of an affine basis encompasses the entire affine space.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Basis.mk: This definition states that a family of vectors is a basis for a module if it is linearly independent and spans the entire module.
explanatories.affineIndependent_iff_linearIndependent_: A family of points is affinely independent if and only if the vectors formed by their differences from a chosen base point in the family are linearly independent.
explanatories.Submodule.span: This defines the smallest submodule of a module that contains a given set of vectors.
explanatories.vectorSpan: This definition describes a submodule generated by the differences of a set of points in an affine space over a specified ring and vector space.
explanatories.direction_affineSpan: This theorem states that the direction of the affine span of a set in an affine space is equal to the vector span generated by that set.
explanatories.AffineSubspace.direction_top: This theorem states that the direction of the top affine subspace is equal to the entire module.
explanatories.Set.image_univ: The image of the universal set under a function is equal to the range of that function.
explanatories.vectorSpan_image_eq_span_vsub_set_right_: This theorem states that the vector span of the images of a function from a set is equal to the span of the differences between the images and a particular element, excluding the case where that element is subtracted from itself.
explanatories.Set.mem_univ: Any element of a type belongs to the universal set of that type.
explanatories.Finset.mem_univ: This theorem asserts that every element of a finitely enumerable type is a member of the universal finite set that contains all elements of that type.

AffineBasis.basisOf.fullDefinition: noncomputable def basisOf (i : ι) : Basis { j : ι // j ≠ i } k V :=   Basis.mk ((affineIndependent_iff_linearIndependent_vsub k b i).mp b.ind)     (by       suffices         Submodule.span k (range fun j : { x // x ≠ i } => b ↑j -ᵥ b i) = vectorSpan k (range b) by         rw [this, ← direction_affineSpan, b.tot, AffineSubspace.direction_top]       conv_rhs => rw [← image_univ]       rw [vectorSpan_image_eq_span_vsub_set_right_ne k b (mem_univ i)]       congr       ext v       simp)
AffineBasis.basisOf.description: This definition specifies a linear basis for the model space corresponding to an affine basis from which one member has been singled out, indexing the new basis by the remaining members.

explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smulₛₗ: This theorem states that applying a linear map to a scalar multiplied by a vector yields the same result as multiplying the result of the linear map by the scalar.
explanatories.map_add: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.LinearMap.add_apply: This theorem states that the sum of two linear maps applied to an element of their domain equals the sum of the results obtained by applying each individual map to that element.
explanatories.MulActionSemiHomClass.map_smulₛₗ: This theorem asserts that a specified function maintains the group action structure when applied to elements acted upon by a monoid.
explanatories.LinearMap.smul_apply: This theorem states that applying a scalar multiplication to a linear map and then to a vector results in the same output as applying the scalar multiplication directly to the image of the vector under the linear map.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear map commutes with scalar multiplication, meaning that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is the same as multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar.

LinearMap.flip.fullDefinition: def flip (f : M →ₛₗ[ρ₁₂] N →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] P) : N →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M →ₛₗ[ρ₁₂] P :=   mk₂'ₛₗ σ₁₂ ρ₁₂ (fun n m => f m n) (fun n₁ n₂ m => (f m).map_add _ _)     (fun c n  m  => (f m).map_smulₛₗ _ _)     (fun n m₁ m₂ => by simp only [map_add, add_apply])     -- Note: #8386 changed `map_smulₛₗ` into `map_smulₛₗ _`.     -- It looks like we now run out of assignable metavariables.     (fun c n  m  => by simp only [map_smulₛₗ _, smul_apply])
LinearMap.flip.description: This definition describes a process that takes a bilinear map and rearranges the order of its variables to form a new linear map.

LinearMap.iInfKerProjEquiv.comment:
If `I` and `J` are disjoint index sets, the product of the kernels of the `J`th projections of
`φ` is linearly equivalent to the product over `I`.

explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.LinearMap.pi_apply: This theorem states that applying a specific linear function to an element yields the same result as applying the indexed linear function to that element.
explanatories.LinearMap.ker: The kernel of a linear map is defined as the set of elements in the domain that are mapped to zero in the codomain, and it forms a submodule of the domain.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp: This definition states that the composition of two linear maps, each between different modules over semirings, results in another linear map that connects the first and last modules directly.
explanatories.LinearMap.pi_comp: This theorem shows that composing a linear function from a family of linear functions with another linear function results in a linear function that is equivalent to applying the family function after the composition.
explanatories.LinearMap.proj: This definition introduces a linear map that extracts a specific component from a family of modules indexed by a set.
explanatories.LinearMap.coe_proj: This theorem states that the evaluation of a projection linear map at an index corresponds to the application of the corresponding evaluation function at that index.
explanatories.LinearMap.proj_apply: This theorem confirms that applying a projection operation to a family of elements retrieves the specific element indexed by that projection.
explanatories.LinearMap.ext: This theorem states that if two linear maps agree on all inputs, then they are equal as functions.
explanatories.LinearMap.proj_pi: This theorem demonstrates that applying a projection after a linear function constructed from a family of linear functions produces the same result as directly using the corresponding linear function from that family.
explanatories.Submodule.mem_iInf: This theorem states that an element belongs to the infimum of a family of submodules if and only if it belongs to each of the submodules in that family.
explanatories.LinearMap.mem_ker: An element belongs to the kernel of a linear map if and only if it is mapped to zero by that linear map.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.Finset.univ: This definition represents the universal finite set of a type that is finitely enumerable.
explanatories.RingHom.id_apply: This theorem states that the identity ring homomorphism returns any element from the semiring unchanged.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.DecidablePred: A decidable predicate is a property that can be determined to be either true or false for elements of a type.
explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.
explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ofLinear: This definition states that a pair of linear maps that are inverses of each other form a linear equivalence between two modules over different semirings.
explanatories.Submodule.subtype: This definition describes a natural linear map that embeds a submodule into the ambient module while retaining the elements' structure.
explanatories.Disjoint.le_bot: If two elements in a lattice are disjoint, then their infimum is less than or equal to the least element of the lattice.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.dif_neg: If a proposition is false, then the result of a dependent choice between two outcomes based on its truth will be equal to the outcome corresponding to its falsity.
explanatories.LinearMap.zero_apply: This theorem asserts that applying a linear map to the zero element of a module yields the zero element in the codomain.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp_assoc: This theorem establishes the associativity of the composition of linearly transformed maps, ensuring that the order of applying the transformations does not affect the final outcome.
explanatories.LinearMap.subtype_comp_codRestrict: This theorem establishes that the composition of a submodule's inclusion map and the codomain restriction of a linear map is equal to the original linear map itself, provided that outputs of the linear map lie within the submodule.
explanatories.Subtype.coe_prop: This theorem states that an element of a subtype belonging to a set also belongs to that set when viewed as its underlying value.
explanatories.dif_pos: The result of a dependent function based on a decidable proposition is equal to the function defined for the true case when that proposition holds.
explanatories.Function.comp_apply: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.
explanatories.Function.eval_apply: This demonstrates that evaluating a function at a specific argument yields the same result as directly applying the function to that argument.
explanatories.LinearMap.codRestrict_apply: This theorem establishes that applying the restricted linear map to an element produces the same result as applying the original linear map to that element, confirming that the restriction operation preserves values in the specified submodule.
explanatories.LinearMap.coe_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the function corresponding to the composition of two linear maps is equivalent to the composition of their respective functions.
explanatories.Submodule.subtype_apply: This theorem states that applying the natural linear map from a submodule to an element within it yields the underlying element of that subtype.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp_apply: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of two linear maps applied to an element yields the same result as applying each map sequentially to that element.
explanatories.LinearMap.id_apply: This theorem demonstrates that the identity function applied to an element of a module returns that element unchanged.
explanatories.trivial: The statement confirms that the proposition asserting truth is indeed valid and can be proven simply.
explanatories.Or.resolve_left: This theorem states that if one has a disjunction and knows that one of the propositions is false, then the other proposition must be true.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm: This definition specifies the symmetry of linear equivalences, indicating that the inverse relationship between two modules can be expressed as a linear equivalence in the opposite direction.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.

LinearMap.iInfKerProjEquiv.fullDefinition: def iInfKerProjEquiv {I J : Set ι} [DecidablePred fun i => i ∈ I] (hd : Disjoint I J)     (hu : Set.univ ⊆ I ∪ J) :     (⨅ i ∈ J, ker (proj i : ((i : ι) → φ i) →ₗ[R] φ i) :     Submodule R ((i : ι) → φ i)) ≃ₗ[R] (i : I) → φ i := by   refine     LinearEquiv.ofLinear (pi fun i => (proj (i : ι)).comp (Submodule.subtype _))       (codRestrict _ (pi fun i => if h : i ∈ I then proj (⟨i, h⟩ : I) else 0) ?_) ?_ ?_   · intro b     simp only [mem_iInf, mem_ker, funext_iff, proj_apply, pi_apply]     intro j hjJ     have : j ∉ I := fun hjI => hd.le_bot ⟨hjI, hjJ⟩     rw [dif_neg this, zero_apply]   · simp only [pi_comp, comp_assoc, subtype_comp_codRestrict, proj_pi, Subtype.coe_prop]     ext b ⟨j, hj⟩     simp only [dif_pos, Function.comp_apply, Function.eval_apply, LinearMap.codRestrict_apply,       LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearMap.coe_proj, LinearMap.pi_apply, Submodule.subtype_apply,       Subtype.coe_prop]     rfl   · ext1 ⟨b, hb⟩     apply Subtype.ext     ext j     have hb : ∀ i ∈ J, b i = 0 := by       simpa only [mem_iInf, mem_ker, proj_apply] using (mem_iInf _).1 hb     simp only [comp_apply, pi_apply, id_apply, proj_apply, subtype_apply, codRestrict_apply]     split_ifs with h     · rfl     · exact (hb _ <| (hu trivial).resolve_left h).symm
LinearMap.iInfKerProjEquiv.description: This definition describes a linear equivalence between the space formed by the intersection of the kernels of certain projection maps and the space of functions indexed by one set of indices, given two disjoint index sets.

  [Module R M₂] {φ : ι → Type i} [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (φ i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (φ i)] [DecidableEq ι]
  (f : (i : ι) → M₂ →ₗ[R] φ i) (c : M₂) (i j : ι) (b : M₂ →ₗ[R] φ i) :

LinearEquiv.piRing.code:
LinearEquiv.piRing.{u, v, x, u_4} (R : Type u) (M : Type v) (ι : Type x) [Semiring R] (S : Type u_4) [Fintype ι]
  [DecidableEq ι] [Semiring S] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [SMulCommClass R S M] :
  ((ι → R) →ₗ[R] M) ≃ₗ[S] ι → M
LinearEquiv.piRing.comment:
Linear equivalence between linear functions `Rⁿ → M` and `Mⁿ`. The spaces `Rⁿ` and `Mⁿ`
are represented as `ι → R` and `ι → M`, respectively, where `ι` is a finite type.

This as an `S`-linear equivalence, under the assumption that `S` acts on `M` commuting with `R`.
When `R` is commutative, we can take this to be the usual action with `S = R`.
Otherwise, `S = ℕ` shows that the equivalence is additive.
See note [bundled maps over different rings].

explanatories.LinearMap.lsum: This definition establishes a linear equivalence between linear functions defined on a finite product of modules and families of functions over those modules.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.trans: This definition establishes that if there are two linear equivalences between three modules with corresponding ring homomorphisms, then there exists a direct linear equivalence between the first and last modules.
explanatories.LinearMap.ringLmapEquivSelf: This definition establishes an equivalence between R-linear maps from a semiring to a module and the points of that module itself, under the condition that the action of another semiring on the module commutes with the first.

LinearEquiv.piRing.fullDefinition: def piRing : ((ι → R) →ₗ[R] M) ≃ₗ[S] ι → M :=   (LinearMap.lsum R (fun _ : ι => R) S).symm.trans     (piCongrRight fun _ => LinearMap.ringLmapEquivSelf R S M)
LinearEquiv.piRing.description: This definition establishes a linear equivalence between linear functions from a finite-dimensional space of tuples over one ring to another module, allowing for a structured mapping of these components when considering an additional semiring structure.

MultilinearMap.mk.injEq.{uR, uι, v₁, v₂} {R : Type uR} {ι : Type uι} {M₁ : ι → Type v₁} {M₂ : Type v₂} [Semiring R]
  [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (M₁ i)] [AddCommMonoid M₂] [(i : ι) → Module R (M₁ i)] [Module R M₂]
  (toFun : ((i : ι) → M₁ i) → M₂)
  (map_add' :
    ∀ [inst : DecidableEq ι] (m : (i : ι) → M₁ i) (i : ι) (x y : M₁ i),
      toFun (update m i (x + y)) = toFun (update m i x) + toFun (update m i y))
  (map_smul' :
    ∀ [inst : DecidableEq ι] (m : (i : ι) → M₁ i) (i : ι) (c : R) (x : M₁ i),
      toFun (update m i (c • x)) = c • toFun (update m i x)) :
  ∀ (toFun_1 : ((i : ι) → M₁ i) → M₂)
    (map_add'_1 :
      ∀ [inst : DecidableEq ι] (m : (i : ι) → M₁ i) (i : ι) (x y : M₁ i),
        toFun_1 (update m i (x + y)) = toFun_1 (update m i x) + toFun_1 (update m i y))
    (map_smul'_1 :
      ∀ [inst : DecidableEq ι] (m : (i : ι) → M₁ i) (i : ι) (c : R) (x : M₁ i),
        toFun_1 (update m i (c • x)) = c • toFun_1 (update m i x)),
    ({ toFun := toFun, map_add' := map_add', map_smul' := map_smul' } =
        { toFun := toFun_1, map_add' := map_add'_1, map_smul' := map_smul'_1 }) =
      (toFun = toFun_1)

MultilinearMap.restr.code:
MultilinearMap.restr.{uR, v', v₂} {R : Type uR} {M₂ : Type v₂} {M' : Type v'} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M₂]
  [AddCommMonoid M'] [Module R M₂] [Module R M'] {k n : ℕ} (f : MultilinearMap R (fun x => M') M₂) (s : Finset (Fin n))
  (hk : s.card = k) (z : M') : MultilinearMap R (fun x => M') M₂
MultilinearMap.restr.comment:
Given a multilinear map `f` on `n` variables (parameterized by `Fin n`) and a subset `s` of `k`
of these variables, one gets a new multilinear map on `Fin k` by varying these variables, and fixing
the other ones equal to a given value `z`. It is denoted by `f.restr s hk z`, where `hk` is a
proof that the cardinality of `s` is `k`. The implicit identification between `Fin k` and `s` that
we use is the canonical (increasing) bijection.

MultilinearMap.restr.fullDefinition: def restr {k n : ℕ} (f : MultilinearMap R (fun _ : Fin n => M') M₂) (s : Finset (Fin n))     (hk : s.card = k) (z : M') : MultilinearMap R (fun _ : Fin k => M') M₂ where   toFun v := f fun j => if h : j ∈ s then v ((DFunLike.coe (s.orderIsoOfFin hk).symm) ⟨j, h⟩) else z   /- Porting note: The proofs of the following two lemmas used to only use `erw` followed by `simp`,   but it seems `erw` no longer unfolds or unifies well enough to work without more help. -/   map_add' v i x y := by     have : DFunLike.coe (s.orderIsoOfFin hk).symm = (s.orderIsoOfFin hk).toEquiv.symm := rfl     simp only [this]     erw [dite_comp_equiv_update (s.orderIsoOfFin hk).toEquiv,       dite_comp_equiv_update (s.orderIsoOfFin hk).toEquiv,       dite_comp_equiv_update (s.orderIsoOfFin hk).toEquiv]     simp   map_smul' v i c x := by     have : DFunLike.coe (s.orderIsoOfFin hk).symm = (s.orderIsoOfFin hk).toEquiv.symm := rfl     simp only [this]     erw [dite_comp_equiv_update (s.orderIsoOfFin hk).toEquiv,       dite_comp_equiv_update (s.orderIsoOfFin hk).toEquiv]     simp
MultilinearMap.restr.description: This definition describes a method to create a new multilinear map that restricts the input variables to a selected subset while keeping the remaining variables fixed at a specified value.

  [(i : Fin n.succ) → AddCommMonoid (M i)] [AddCommMonoid M₂] [(i : Fin n.succ) → Module R (M i)] [Module R M₂]
  (f : MultilinearMap R M M₂) (m : (i : Fin n) → M i.succ) (x y : M 0) :
  f (cons (x + y) m) = f (cons x m) + f (cons y m)

an element of `∀ (i : Fin (n+1)), M i` using `cons`, one can express directly the additivity of a
multilinear map along the first variable.

MultilinearMap.map_piecewise_add.{uR, uι, v₁, v₂} {R : Type uR} {ι : Type uι} {M₁ : ι → Type v₁} {M₂ : Type v₂}
  [Semiring R] [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (M₁ i)] [AddCommMonoid M₂] [(i : ι) → Module R (M₁ i)] [Module R M₂]
  (f : MultilinearMap R M₁ M₂) [DecidableEq ι] (m m' : (i : ι) → M₁ i) (t : Finset ι) :
  f (t.piecewise (m + m') m') = ∑ s ∈ t.powerset, f (s.piecewise m m')
MultilinearMap.map_piecewise_add.comment:
If one adds to a vector `m'` another vector `m`, but only for coordinates in a finset `t`, then
the image under a multilinear map `f` is the sum of `f (s.piecewise m m')` along all subsets `s` of
`t`. This is mainly an auxiliary statement to prove the result when `t = univ`, given in
`map_add_univ`, although it can be useful in its own right as it does not require the index set `ι`
to be finite.

  [Semiring R] [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (M₁ i)] [AddCommMonoid M₂] [(i : ι) → Module R (M₁ i)] [Module R M₂]
  (f : MultilinearMap R M₁ M₂) {α : ι → Type u_1} (g : (i : ι) → α i → M₁ i) (A : (i : ι) → Finset (α i))
  [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] {n : ℕ} (h : ∑ i : ι, (A i).card = n) :
  (f fun i => ∑ j ∈ A i, g i j) = ∑ r ∈ piFinset A, f fun i => g i (r i)
MultilinearMap.map_sum_finset_aux.comment:
If `f` is multilinear, then `f (Σ_{j₁ ∈ A₁} g₁ j₁, ..., Σ_{jₙ ∈ Aₙ} gₙ jₙ)` is the sum of
`f (g₁ (r 1), ..., gₙ (r n))` where `r` ranges over all functions with `r 1 ∈ A₁`, ...,
`r n ∈ Aₙ`. This follows from multilinearity by expanding successively with respect to each
coordinate. Here, we give an auxiliary statement tailored for an inductive proof. Use instead
`map_sum_finset`.

MultilinearMap.domDomRestrict_aux.{uι, v₁} {ι : Type uι} {M₁ : ι → Type v₁} [DecidableEq ι] (P : ι → Prop)
  [DecidablePred P] [DecidableEq { a // P a }] (x : (i : { a // P a }) → M₁ ↑i) (z : (i : { a // ¬P a }) → M₁ ↑i)
  (i : { a // P a }) (c : M₁ ↑i) :
  (fun j => if h : P j then update x i c ⟨j, h⟩ else z ⟨j, h⟩) =
    update (fun j => if h : P j then x ⟨j, h⟩ else z ⟨j, h⟩) (↑i) c

MultilinearMap.domDomRestrict.code:
MultilinearMap.domDomRestrict.{uR, uι, v₁, v₂} {R : Type uR} {ι : Type uι} {M₁ : ι → Type v₁} {M₂ : Type v₂}
  [Semiring R] [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (M₁ i)] [AddCommMonoid M₂] [(i : ι) → Module R (M₁ i)] [Module R M₂]
  (f : MultilinearMap R M₁ M₂) (P : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred P] (z : (i : { a // ¬P a }) → M₁ ↑i) :
  MultilinearMap R (fun i => M₁ ↑i) M₂
MultilinearMap.domDomRestrict.comment:
Given a multilinear map `f` on `(i : ι) → M i`, a (decidable) predicate `P` on `ι` and
an element `z` of `(i : {a // ¬ P a}) → M₁ i`, construct a multilinear map on
`(i : {a // P a}) → M₁ i)` whose value at `x` is `f` evaluated at the vector with `i`th coordinate
`x i` if `P i` and `z i` otherwise.

The naming is similar to `MultilinearMap.domDomCongr`: here we are applying the restriction to the
domain of the domain.

For a linear map version, see `MultilinearMap.domDomRestrictₗ`.

MultilinearMap.domDomRestrict.fullDefinition: def domDomRestrict (f : MultilinearMap R M₁ M₂) (P : ι → Prop) [DecidablePred P]     (z : (i : {a : ι // ¬ P a}) → M₁ i) :     MultilinearMap R (fun (i : {a : ι // P a}) => M₁ i) M₂ where   toFun x := f (fun j ↦ if h : P j then x ⟨j, h⟩ else z ⟨j, h⟩)   map_add' x i a b := by     classical     simp only     repeat (rw [domDomRestrict_aux])     simp only [MultilinearMap.map_add]   map_smul' z i c a := by     classical     simp only     repeat (rw [domDomRestrict_aux])     simp only [MultilinearMap.map_smul]
MultilinearMap.domDomRestrict.description: This definition describes a method to create a new multilinear map that evaluates to values from an existing multilinear map when certain conditions are met, based on a given predicate and a specified input.

MultilinearMap.mkPiAlgebra.comment:

explanatories.False.elim: From a contradiction, any proposition can be inferred, illustrating that if something is false, anything follows.

multilinearCurryLeftEquiv.comment:
The space of multilinear maps on `∀ (i : Fin (n+1)), M i` is canonically isomorphic to
the space of linear maps from `M 0` to the space of multilinear maps on
`∀ (i : Fin n), M i.succ`, by separating the first variable. We register this isomorphism as a
linear isomorphism in `multilinearCurryLeftEquiv R M M₂`.

The direct and inverse maps are given by `f.uncurryLeft` and `f.curryLeft`. Use these
unless you need the full framework of linear equivs.

MultilinearMap.curryRight.fullDefinition: def MultilinearMap.curryRight (f : MultilinearMap R M M₂) :     MultilinearMap R (fun i : Fin n => M (Fin.castSucc i)) (M (last n) →ₗ[R] M₂) where   toFun m :=     { toFun := fun x => f (snoc m x)       map_add' := fun x y => by simp_rw [f.snoc_add]       map_smul' := fun c x => by simp only [f.snoc_smul, RingHom.id_apply] }   map_add' := @fun dec m i x y => by     rw [Subsingleton.elim dec (by clear dec; infer_instance)]; clear dec     ext z     change f (snoc (update m i (x + y)) z) = f (snoc (update m i x) z) + f (snoc (update m i y) z)     rw [snoc_update, snoc_update, snoc_update, f.map_add]   map_smul' := @fun dec m i c x => by     rw [Subsingleton.elim dec (by clear dec; infer_instance)]; clear dec     ext z     change f (snoc (update m i (c • x)) z) = c • f (snoc (update m i x) z)     rw [snoc_update, snoc_update, f.map_smul]

MultilinearMap.curryFinFinset.comment:

`l`, then the space of multilinear maps on `fun i : Fin n => M'` is isomorphic to the space of
multilinear maps on `fun i : Fin k => M'` taking values in the space of multilinear maps
on `fun i : Fin l => M'`.

MultilinearMap.domCoprod.code:
MultilinearMap.domCoprod.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_6, u_7, u_8} {R : Type u_1} {ι₁ : Type u_2} {ι₂ : Type u_3} [CommSemiring R]
  {N₁ : Type u_6} [AddCommMonoid N₁] [Module R N₁] {N₂ : Type u_7} [AddCommMonoid N₂] [Module R N₂] {N : Type u_8}
  [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] (a : MultilinearMap R (fun x => N) N₁) (b : MultilinearMap R (fun x => N) N₂) :
  MultilinearMap R (fun x => N) (N₁ ⊗[R] N₂)
MultilinearMap.domCoprod.comment:
Given two multilinear maps `(ι₁ → N) → N₁` and `(ι₂ → N) → N₂`, this produces the map
`(ι₁ ⊕ ι₂ → N) → N₁ ⊗ N₂` by taking the coproduct of the domain and the tensor product
of the codomain.

This can be thought of as combining `Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow.symm` with
`TensorProduct.map`, noting that the two operations can't be separated as the intermediate result
is not a `MultilinearMap`.

While this can be generalized to work for dependent `Π i : ι₁, N'₁ i` instead of `ι₁ → N`, doing so
introduces `Sum.elim N'₁ N'₂` types in the result which are difficult to work with and not defeq
to the simple case defined here. See [this zulip thread](
https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/217875-Is-there.20code.20for.20X.3F/topic/Instances.20on.20.60sum.2Eelim.20A.20B.20i.60/near/218484619).

explanatories.TensorProduct.tmul_add: This theorem asserts that the tensor product of a module with the sum of two elements from another module is equal to the sum of the tensor products of the first module with each of those elements individually.

explanatories.Submodule.toAddSubmonoid: This definition allows a submodule of a module over a semiring to be regarded as an additive submonoid, thereby establishing a connection between these two algebraic structures.
explanatories.Submodule.smul_mem: This theorem demonstrates that if an element belongs to a submodule, then its scalar multiplication by any element from the semiring also lies within the same submodule, thereby confirming closure under scalar multiplication.
explanatories.Submodule.smul_mem': This theorem asserts that if an element belongs to the carrier of a submodule, then its scalar multiplication by any element of the semiring also belongs to the same carrier, demonstrating closure under scalar multiplication within the submodule.

TensorProduct.liftAddHom.comment:
Lift an `R`-balanced map to the tensor product.

A map `f : M →+ N →+ P` additive in both components is `R`-balanced, or middle linear with respect
to `R`, if scalar multiplication in either argument is equivalent, `f (r • m) n = f m (r • n)`.

Note that strictly the first action should be a right-action by `R`, but for now `R` is commutative
so it doesn't matter.

explanatories.TensorProduct.Eqv.add_comm: This theorem demonstrates that the tensor product of two modules over a commutative semiring is commutative when treated as an equivalence relation on their free additive monoids.
explanatories.AddCon.lift: This definition describes a homomorphism from the quotient of an additive monoid by a specified additive congruence relation to another additive structure, which is defined under the condition that the homomorphism is constant on the equivalence classes of the congruence relation.
explanatories.FreeAddMonoid.lift: This definition establishes an equivalence between functions from a type to an additive monoid and additive monoid homomorphisms from the free additive monoid generated by that type to the additive monoid.
explanatories.AddCon.addConGen_le: This theorem asserts that the smallest additive congruence relation generated by a given binary relation is a subset of any additive congruence relation that includes that binary relation.
explanatories.TensorProduct.Eqv.of_zero_left: This theorem establishes that the tensor product of a module with the zero element from another module is equivalent to the zero element in the context of free additive monoids.
explanatories.AddCon.ker_rel: This theorem characterizes the additive congruence relation induced by the kernel of an additive monoid homomorphism, stating that two elements are congruent if and only if they are mapped to the same element in the codomain.
explanatories.map_zero: This theorem asserts a property about a type of morphism that maintains the identity element across two algebraic structures with defined identity elements.
explanatories.FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of: This theorem demonstrates that applying the lift of a function to the free additive monoid generated by an element yields the function's value at that element.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.zero_apply: This theorem asserts that a homomorphism between additive monoids maps the additive identity in the source to the additive identity in the target, ensuring that applying the homomorphism to zero yields zero.
explanatories.TensorProduct.Eqv.of_zero_right: This theorem establishes that an element from the tensor product of two modules combined with the zero element of the additive monoid is equivalent to zero.
explanatories.TensorProduct.Eqv.of_add_left: This theorem establishes that adding two elements from the tensor product of a module with a fixed element from another module is equivalent to adding the corresponding elements together within the free additive monoid framework.
explanatories.map_add: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.add_apply: This theorem is not applicable as there is no content to describe.
explanatories.TensorProduct.Eqv.of_add_right: This theorem demonstrates that summing two elements from the tensor product of a module with a fixed element from another module is equivalent to summing the corresponding elements within the free additive monoid.
explanatories.TensorProduct.Eqv.of_smul: This theorem shows that scaling an element from one module by a scalar is equivalent to scaling an element from another module in the context of free additive monoids when combined in a specific manner.
explanatories.add_comm: This theorem asserts that the addition operation in a commutative magma is commutative, meaning the sum of two elements does not depend on the order in which they are added.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.map_zero: An additive monoid homomorphism maps the zero element of one additive monoid to the zero element of another.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.map_add: This theorem asserts that an additive monoid homomorphism preserves the addition operation, meaning the image of the sum of two elements is equal to the sum of their images.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_zero: This theorem demonstrates that a linear map assigns the zero element of its domain to the zero element of its codomain.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.
explanatories.LinearMap.add_apply: This theorem states that the sum of two linear maps applied to an element of their domain equals the sum of the results obtained by applying each individual map to that element.

TensorProduct.liftAddHom.fullDefinition: def liftAddHom (f : M →+ N →+ P)     (hf : ∀ (r : R) (m : M) (n : N), f (r • m) n = f m (r • n)) :     M ⊗[R] N →+ P :=   (addConGen (TensorProduct.Eqv R M N)).lift (FreeAddMonoid.lift (fun mn : M × N => f mn.1 mn.2)) <|     AddCon.addConGen_le fun x y hxy =>       match x, y, hxy with       | _, _, .of_zero_left n =>         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_zero, FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, map_zero,           AddMonoidHom.zero_apply]       | _, _, .of_zero_right m =>         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_zero, FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, map_zero]       | _, _, .of_add_left m₁ m₂ n =>         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_add, FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, map_add,           AddMonoidHom.add_apply]       | _, _, .of_add_right m n₁ n₂ =>         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_add, FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, map_add]       | _, _, .of_smul s m n =>         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by rw [FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, hf]       | _, _, .add_comm x y =>         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_add, add_comm]

TensorProduct.CompatibleSMul.isScalarTow.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) CompatibleSMul.isScalarTower [SMul R' R] [IsScalarTower R' R M]     [DistribMulAction R' N] [IsScalarTower R' R N] : CompatibleSMul R R' M N :=   ⟨fun r m n => by     conv_lhs => rw [← one_smul R m]     conv_rhs => rw [← one_smul R n]     rw [← smul_assoc, ← smul_assoc]     exact Quotient.sound' <| AddConGen.Rel.of _ _ <| Eqv.of_smul _ _ _⟩

explanatories.AddCon.addConGen_le: This theorem asserts that the smallest additive congruence relation generated by a given binary relation is a subset of any additive congruence relation that includes that binary relation.
explanatories.TensorProduct.Eqv.of_zero_left: This theorem establishes that the tensor product of a module with the zero element from another module is equivalent to the zero element in the context of free additive monoids.
explanatories.AddCon.ker_rel: This theorem characterizes the additive congruence relation induced by the kernel of an additive monoid homomorphism, stating that two elements are congruent if and only if they are mapped to the same element in the codomain.
explanatories.map_zero: This theorem asserts a property about a type of morphism that maintains the identity element across two algebraic structures with defined identity elements.
explanatories.TensorProduct.Eqv.of_zero_right: This theorem establishes that an element from the tensor product of two modules combined with the zero element of the additive monoid is equivalent to zero.
explanatories.TensorProduct.Eqv.of_add_left: This theorem establishes that adding two elements from the tensor product of a module with a fixed element from another module is equivalent to adding the corresponding elements together within the free additive monoid framework.

explanatories.TensorProduct.Eqv.of_smul: This theorem shows that scaling an element from one module by a scalar is equivalent to scaling an element from another module in the context of free additive monoids when combined in a specific manner.
explanatories.add_comm: This theorem asserts that the addition operation in a commutative magma is commutative, meaning the sum of two elements does not depend on the order in which they are added.
explanatories.TensorProduct.zero_tmul: This theorem states that the tensor product of the zero element with any element from another module results in the zero element of the tensor product.
explanatories.TensorProduct.add_tmul: This theorem proves that the tensor product distributes over addition in the first argument when combining elements from two modules.
explanatories.TensorProduct.tmul_zero: This theorem asserts that the tensor product of any element with the zero element of a module over a commutative semiring results in the zero element of the tensor product.
explanatories.TensorProduct.tmul_add: This theorem asserts that the tensor product of a module with the sum of two elements from another module is equal to the sum of the tensor products of the first module with each of those elements individually.
explanatories.TensorProduct.CompatibleSMul.smul_tmul: This theorem establishes that scaling an element from one module and taking the tensor product with an element from another module is equivalent to taking the tensor product of the first element with the scaled version of the second element.
explanatories.TensorProduct.smul_tmul: This theorem states that the scalar multiplication operation can be transferred across the tensor product of two modules, allowing it to act on either the first or the second element.
explanatories.TensorProduct.SMul.aux: This definition introduces an auxiliary function that facilitates the establishment of scalar multiplication on the tensor product of two modules.
explanatories.TensorProduct.SMul.aux_of: This theorem shows that the auxiliary function for scalar multiplication applied to a singleton element from a free additive monoid produces the tensor product of the scaled element with a fixed element from another module.
explanatories.SMulCommClass.smul_comm: This theorem states that in the presence of a commutative scalar multiplication structure, the order of multiplying two elements with a third remains unchanged when using scalar multiplication.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.map_zero: An additive monoid homomorphism maps the zero element of one additive monoid to the zero element of another.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.map_add: This theorem asserts that an additive monoid homomorphism preserves the addition operation, meaning the image of the sum of two elements is equal to the sum of their images.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_zero: This theorem demonstrates that a linear map assigns the zero element of its domain to the zero element of its codomain.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.

TensorProduct.leftHasSMul.fullDefinition: instance leftHasSMul : SMul R' (M ⊗[R] N) :=   ⟨fun r =>     (addConGen (TensorProduct.Eqv R M N)).lift (SMul.aux r : _ →+ M ⊗[R] N) <|       AddCon.addConGen_le fun x y hxy =>         match x, y, hxy with         | _, _, .of_zero_left n =>           (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_zero, SMul.aux_of, smul_zero, zero_tmul]         | _, _, .of_zero_right m =>           (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_zero, SMul.aux_of, tmul_zero]         | _, _, .of_add_left m₁ m₂ n =>           (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_add, SMul.aux_of, smul_add, add_tmul]         | _, _, .of_add_right m n₁ n₂ =>           (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_add, SMul.aux_of, tmul_add]         | _, _, .of_smul s m n =>           (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by rw [SMul.aux_of, SMul.aux_of, ← smul_comm, smul_tmul]         | _, _, .add_comm x y =>           (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [map_add, add_comm]⟩
TensorProduct.leftHasSMul.description: This definition introduces the concept of a scalar multiplication action on the tensor product of two modules over a commutative semiring, establishing a structure where one module can be multiplied by scalars from another.

  [Module R T] (f : M →ₗ[R] P →ₗ[R] Q) (g : N →ₗ[R] S →ₗ[R] T) : M ⊗[R] N →ₗ[R] P ⊗[R] S →ₗ[R] Q ⊗[R] T
TensorProduct.map₂.comment:
This is a binary version of `TensorProduct.map`: Given a bilinear map `f : M ⟶ P ⟶ Q` and a
bilinear map `g : N ⟶ S ⟶ T`, if we think `f` and `g` as linear maps with two inputs, then
`map₂ f g` is a bilinear map taking two inputs `M ⊗ N → P ⊗ S → Q ⊗ S` defined by
`map₂ f g (m ⊗ n) (p ⊗ s) = f m p ⊗ g n s`.

Mathematically, `TensorProduct.map₂` is defined as the composition
`M ⊗ N -map→ Hom(P, Q) ⊗ Hom(S, T) -homTensorHomMap→ Hom(P ⊗ S, Q ⊗ T)`.

  (N : Type u_5) (P : Type u_6) (Q : Type u_7) [AddCommMonoid M] [AddCommMonoid N] [AddCommMonoid P] [AddCommMonoid Q]
  [Module R M] [Module R N] [Module R P] [Module R Q] : (M ⊗[R] N) ⊗[R] P ⊗[R] Q ≃ₗ[R] (M ⊗[R] P) ⊗[R] N ⊗[R] Q
TensorProduct.tensorTensorTensorComm.comment:
This special case is worth defining explicitly since it is useful for defining multiplication
on tensor products of modules carrying multiplications (e.g., associative rings, Lie rings, ...).

E.g., suppose `M = P` and `N = Q` and that `M` and `N` carry bilinear multiplications:
`M ⊗ M → M` and `N ⊗ N → N`. Using `map`, we can define `(M ⊗ M) ⊗ (N ⊗ N) → M ⊗ N` which, when
combined with this definition, yields a bilinear multiplication on `M ⊗ N`:
`(M ⊗ N) ⊗ (M ⊗ N) → M ⊗ N`. In particular we could use this to define the multiplication in
the `TensorProduct.semiring` instance (currently defined "by hand" using `TensorProduct.mul`).

See also `mul_mul_mul_comm`.

TensorProduct.tensorTensorTensorAssoc.comment:
This special case is useful for describing the interplay between `dualTensorHomEquiv` and
composition of linear maps.

E.g., composition of linear maps gives a map `(M → N) ⊗ (N → P) → (M → P)`, and applying
`dual_tensor_hom_equiv.symm` to the three hom-modules gives a map
`(M.dual ⊗ N) ⊗ (N.dual ⊗ P) → (M.dual ⊗ P)`, which agrees with the application of `contractRight`
on `N ⊗ N.dual` after the suitable rebracketting.

  [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R M] [Module R N] : CompatibleSMul R ℤ M N
TensorProduct.CompatibleSMul.int.comment:
While the tensor product will automatically inherit a ℤ-module structure from
`AddCommGroup.intModule`, that structure won't be compatible with lemmas like `tmul_smul` unless
we use a `ℤ-Module` instance provided by `TensorProduct.left_module`.

When `R` is a `Ring` we get the required `TensorProduct.compatible_smul` instance through
`IsScalarTower`, but when it is only a `Semiring` we need to build it from scratch.
The instance diamond in `compatible_smul` doesn't matter because it's in `Prop`.

explanatories.AddCon.induction_on: This theorem provides an inductive framework for proving properties about elements in a quotient space defined by an additive congruence relation, given that a certain property holds for all representatives of those elements.
explanatories.TensorProduct.induction_on: This theorem establishes a method for proving a property for all elements in the tensor product of two modules by demonstrating its validity for zero, for tensor products of elements, and for their sum.
explanatories.TensorProduct.add_tmul: This theorem proves that the tensor product distributes over addition in the first argument when combining elements from two modules.
explanatories.TensorProduct.tmul_add: This theorem asserts that the tensor product of a module with the sum of two elements from another module is equal to the sum of the tensor products of the first module with each of those elements individually.
explanatories.add_smul: This theorem states that the operation of scalar multiplication distributes over the addition of scalars in a module.
explanatories.TensorProduct.add_smul: This theorem asserts that scalar multiplication distributes over the addition of scalars when applied to the tensor product of two modules.
explanatories.TensorProduct.tmul_sub: This theorem establishes that taking the tensor product of an element from one module with the difference of two elements from another module is equivalent to the difference of the tensor products of the individual elements.
explanatories.TensorProduct.sub_tmul: This theorem demonstrates that the tensor product of the difference between two elements from one module and an element from another module is equal to the difference of their individual tensor products with that element.
explanatories.Int.induction_on: This theorem asserts that there is no formal statement provided to summarize.
explanatories.sub_smul: This theorem states that scalar multiplication with the difference of two scalars in a module can be expressed as the difference of the scalar multiplications of each scalar with the element.

TensorProduct.CompatibleSMul.int.fullDefinition: instance CompatibleSMul.int : CompatibleSMul R ℤ M N :=   ⟨fun r m n =>     Int.induction_on r (by simp) (fun r ih => by simpa [add_smul, tmul_add, add_tmul] using ih)       fun r ih => by simpa [sub_smul, tmul_sub, sub_tmul] using ih⟩
TensorProduct.CompatibleSMul.int.description: This definition asserts that the tensor product of two additive commutative groups, when viewed as modules over the integers, has a compatible scalar multiplication structure.

explanatories.LinearMap.coprod: This definition describes a linear map that combines two linear maps from two modules into a single linear map to a third module by mapping pairs of elements to the sum of their images under the individual maps.
explanatories.LinearMap.lTensor: This definition describes a natural linear map that takes a tensor product of one module with another and produces a tensor product with a third module, guided by a specified linear map.
explanatories.LinearMap.inl: This definition describes a linear map that injects an element from one module into the first component of a product of two modules.

TensorProduct.prodRight.fullDefinition: def prodRight : M₁ ⊗[R] (M₂ × M₃) ≃ₗ[R] ((M₁ ⊗[R] M₂) × (M₁ ⊗[R] M₃)) :=   LinearEquiv.ofLinear     (lift <|       LinearMap.prodMapLinear R M₂ M₃ (M₁ ⊗[R] M₂) (M₁ ⊗[R] M₃) R         ∘ₗ LinearMap.prod (mk _ _ _) (mk _ _ _))     (LinearMap.coprod       (LinearMap.lTensor _ <| LinearMap.inl _ _ _)       (LinearMap.lTensor _ <| LinearMap.inr _ _ _))     (by ext <;> simp)     (by ext <;> simp)
TensorProduct.prodRight.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the tensor product of a module with a product of two modules and the product of the tensor products of the first module with each of the other two modules.

TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.curry.comment:
Heterobasic version of `TensorProduct.curry`:

Given a linear map `M ⊗[R] N →[A] P`, compose it with the canonical
bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] M ⊗[R] N` to form a bilinear map `M →[A] N →[R] P`.

explanatories.LinearMap.ext: This theorem states that if two linear maps agree on all inputs, then they are equal as functions.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear map commutes with scalar multiplication, meaning that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is the same as multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar.
explanatories.TensorProduct.ext: This theorem establishes that if two linear maps from the tensor product of two modules to a third module are equal when restricted through a specific construction, then the linear maps themselves must be identical.

TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.curry.fullDefinition: nonrec def curry (f : M ⊗[R] N →ₗ[A] P) : M →ₗ[A] N →ₗ[R] P :=   { curry (f.restrictScalars R) with     toFun := curry (f.restrictScalars R)     map_smul' := fun c x => LinearMap.ext fun y => f.map_smul c (x ⊗ₜ y) }
TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.curry.description: The definition describes a transformation that takes a linear map from the tensor product of two modules to a third module and converts it into a bilinear map from one module to another that ultimately outputs elements in the third module.

explanatories.TensorProduct.lift: This definition describes a method to construct a linear map from the tensor product of two modules to a third module, based on a given bilinear map.

explanatories.LinearMap.comp_apply: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of two linear maps applied to an element yields the same result as applying each map sequentially to that element.
explanatories.Algebra.lsmul_coe: This theorem states that the action of an algebra element on a module via the defined morphism is equivalent to scalar multiplication of that algebra element with any given module element.
explanatories.TensorProduct.smul_tmul': This theorem demonstrates that scaling an element from one module before taking its tensor product with an element from another module is equivalent to taking the tensor product first and then scaling, provided both modules are appropriately structured.
explanatories.TensorProduct.lift.tmul: This theorem states that applying a lifted bilinear map to the tensor product of two elements yields the same result as applying the original bilinear map to each element and then the second component.
explanatories.LinearMap.coe_restrictScalars: This theorem asserts that the action of coercing a linear map to restrict its scalars does not change its underlying function.
explanatories.LinearMap.smul_apply: This theorem states that applying a scalar multiplication to a linear map and then to a vector results in the same output as applying the scalar multiplication directly to the image of the vector under the linear map.

  [Module ι (Additive ℤˣ)] [DecidableEq ι] (𝒜 : ι → Type u_5) (ℬ : ι → Type u_6) [CommRing R]
  [(i : ι) → AddCommGroup (𝒜 i)] [(i : ι) → AddCommGroup (ℬ i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (𝒜 i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (ℬ i)] :
  gradedCommAux R 𝒜 ℬ =
    DirectSum.toModule R (ι × ι) (⨁ (i : ι × ι), ℬ i.1 ⊗[R] 𝒜 i.2) fun i =>
      let_fun o := lof R (ι × ι) (fun i => ℬ i.1 ⊗[R] 𝒜 i.2) i.swap;
      let_fun s := (-1) ^ (i.1 * i.2);
      (s • o) ∘ₗ ↑(TensorProduct.comm R (𝒜 i.1) (ℬ i.2))

TensorProduct.gradedMul.fullDefinition: noncomputable irreducible_def gradedMul :     letI AB := DirectSum _ 𝒜 ⊗[R] DirectSum _ ℬ     letI : Module R AB := TensorProduct.leftModule     AB →ₗ[R] AB →ₗ[R] AB := by   refine TensorProduct.curry ?_   refine map (LinearMap.mul' R (⨁ i, 𝒜 i)) (LinearMap.mul' R (⨁ i, ℬ i)) ∘ₗ ?_   refine (assoc R _ _ _).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ .lTensor _ ?_ ∘ₗ (assoc R _ _ _).toLinearMap   refine (assoc R _ _ _).toLinearMap ∘ₗ .rTensor _ ?_ ∘ₗ (assoc R _ _ _).symm.toLinearMap   exact (gradedComm _ _ _).toLinearMap

TensorProduct.gradedMul_def.code:
TensorProduct.gradedMul_def.{u_7, u_8, u_9, u_10} (R : Type u_7) {ι : Type u_8} [CommSemiring ι]
  [Module ι (Additive ℤˣ)] [DecidableEq ι] (𝒜 : ι → Type u_9) (ℬ : ι → Type u_10) [CommRing R]
  [(i : ι) → AddCommGroup (𝒜 i)] [(i : ι) → AddCommGroup (ℬ i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (𝒜 i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (ℬ i)]
  [DirectSum.GRing 𝒜] [DirectSum.GRing ℬ] [DirectSum.GAlgebra R 𝒜] [DirectSum.GAlgebra R ℬ] :
  gradedMul R 𝒜 ℬ =
    curry
      (map (LinearMap.mul' R (⨁ (i : ι), 𝒜 i)) (LinearMap.mul' R (⨁ (i : ι), ℬ i)) ∘ₗ
        ↑(TensorProduct.assoc R (⨁ (i : ι), 𝒜 i) (⨁ (i : ι), 𝒜 i) ((⨁ (i : ι), ℬ i) ⊗[R] ⨁ (i : ι), ℬ i)).symm ∘ₗ
          LinearMap.lTensor (⨁ (i : ι), 𝒜 i)
              (↑(TensorProduct.assoc R (⨁ (i : ι), 𝒜 i) (⨁ (i : ι), ℬ i) (⨁ (i : ι), ℬ i)) ∘ₗ
                LinearMap.rTensor (⨁ (i : ι), ℬ i) ↑(gradedComm R ℬ 𝒜) ∘ₗ
                  ↑(TensorProduct.assoc R (DirectSum ι ℬ) (DirectSum ι 𝒜) (DirectSum ι ℬ)).symm) ∘ₗ
            ↑(TensorProduct.assoc R (DirectSum ι 𝒜) (DirectSum ι ℬ) (DirectSum ι 𝒜 ⊗[R] DirectSum ι ℬ)))

GradedTensorProduct.mulHom.fullDefinition: noncomputable def mulHom : (𝒜 ᵍ⊗[R] ℬ) →ₗ[R] (𝒜 ᵍ⊗[R] ℬ) →ₗ[R] (𝒜 ᵍ⊗[R] ℬ) := by   letI fAB1 := auxEquiv R 𝒜 ℬ   have := ((gradedMul R (𝒜 ·) (ℬ ·)).compl₁₂ fAB1.toLinearMap fAB1.toLinearMap).compr₂     fAB1.symm.toLinearMap   exact this

GradedTensorProduct.mulHom_apply.code:
GradedTensorProduct.mulHom_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {R : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {A : Type u_3} {B : Type u_4}
  [CommSemiring ι] [Module ι (Additive ℤˣ)] [DecidableEq ι] [CommRing R] [Ring A] [Ring B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]

explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.

explanatories.TensorProduct.add_tmul: This theorem proves that the tensor product distributes over addition in the first argument when combining elements from two modules.

explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.Prod.ext: If two pairs of elements have equal first components and equal second components, then the pairs themselves are equal.

GradedTensorProduct.lift.fullDefinition: def lift (f : A →ₐ[R] C) (g : B →ₐ[R] C)     (h_anti_commutes : ∀ ⦃i j⦄ (a : 𝒜 i) (b : ℬ j), f a * g b = (-1 : ℤˣ)^(j * i) • (g b * f a)) :     (𝒜 ᵍ⊗[R] ℬ) →ₐ[R] C :=   AlgHom.ofLinearMap     (LinearMap.mul' R C       ∘ₗ (TensorProduct.map f.toLinearMap g.toLinearMap)       ∘ₗ ((of R 𝒜 ℬ).symm : 𝒜 ᵍ⊗[R] ℬ →ₗ[R] A ⊗[R] B))     (by       dsimp [Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def]       simp only [_root_.map_one, mul_one])     (by       rw [LinearMap.map_mul_iff]       ext a₁ : 3       refine DirectSum.decompose_lhom_ext ℬ fun j₁ => ?_       ext b₁ : 3       refine DirectSum.decompose_lhom_ext 𝒜 fun i₂ => ?_       ext a₂ b₂ : 2       dsimp       rw [tmul_coe_mul_coe_tmul]       rw [@Units.smul_def _ _ (_) (_), zsmul_eq_smul_cast R, map_smul, map_smul, map_smul]       rw [← zsmul_eq_smul_cast R, ← @Units.smul_def _ _ (_) (_)]       rw [of_symm_of, map_tmul, LinearMap.mul'_apply]       simp_rw [AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply, _root_.map_mul]       simp_rw [mul_assoc (f a₁), ← mul_assoc _ _ (g b₂), h_anti_commutes, mul_smul_comm,         smul_mul_assoc, smul_smul, Int.units_mul_self, one_smul])
GradedTensorProduct.lift.description: This definition describes a construction that allows for an algebra morphism from the graded tensor product to be formed using individual morphisms from the components of the graded algebras, with specific anti-commutation conditions applied to pure elements.

GradedTensorProduct.liftEquiv.fullDefinition: def liftEquiv :     { fg : (A →ₐ[R] C) × (B →ₐ[R] C) //         ∀ ⦃i j⦄ (a : 𝒜 i) (b : ℬ j), fg.1 a * fg.2 b = (-1 : ℤˣ)^(j * i) • (fg.2 b * fg.1 a)} ≃       ((𝒜 ᵍ⊗[R] ℬ) →ₐ[R] C) where   toFun fg := lift 𝒜 ℬ _ _ fg.prop   invFun F := ⟨(F.comp (includeLeft 𝒜 ℬ), F.comp (includeRight 𝒜 ℬ)), fun i j a b => by     dsimp     rw [← _root_.map_mul, ← _root_.map_mul F, tmul_coe_mul_coe_tmul, one_mul, mul_one,       AlgHom.map_smul_of_tower, tmul_one_mul_one_tmul, smul_smul, Int.units_mul_self, one_smul]⟩   left_inv fg := by ext <;> (dsimp; simp only [_root_.map_one, mul_one, one_mul])   right_inv F := by     apply AlgHom.toLinearMap_injective     ext     dsimp     rw [← _root_.map_mul, tmul_one_mul_one_tmul]

tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul_symm_comp_mkQ.description: The inverse of the linear equivalence established by the tensor product of a module with a ring quotient can be expressed as a composition with a specific quotient map associated with that ideal.

explanatories.lTensor.inverse.eq_1: This theorem establishes the equality between a specific inverse of a linear map and the inverse that results from the existence of a right inverse for that map, when the two maps satisfy certain exactness and surjectivity conditions.
explanatories.rTensor.inverse.eq_1: This theorem establishes the equality between a specific inverse of a linear map involving exactness and surjectivity conditions, and another derived from the existence of a right inverse for that map.

Ideal.map.eq_1.description: The theorem asserts that the image of an ideal under a function is equal to the span of the image of that ideal's elements transformed by the function.

Ideal.map_includeRight_eq.code:
Ideal.map_includeRight_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {R : Type u_1} [CommSemiring R] {A : Type u_2} {B : Type u_3} [Semiring A]
  [Semiring B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] (I : Ideal B) :

  {M' : Type u_5} {N' : Type u_6} {ι : Type u_7} {κ : Type u_8} {ι' : Type u_10} {κ' : Type u_11} [DecidableEq ι]
  [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [Finite ι'] [Finite κ'] [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N]
  [AddCommGroup M'] [AddCommGroup N'] [Module R M] [Module R N] [Module R M'] [Module R N'] (bM : Basis ι R M)
  (bN : Basis κ R N) (bM' : Basis ι' R M') (bN' : Basis κ' R N') (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (g : N →ₗ[R] N') :
  (toMatrix (bM.tensorProduct bN) (bM'.tensorProduct bN')) (TensorProduct.map f g) =
    kroneckerMap (fun x x_1 => x * x_1) ((toMatrix bM bM') f) ((toMatrix bN bN') g)

`Matrix.kronecker`.

TensorProduct.VanishesTrivially.code:
TensorProduct.VanishesTrivially.{u} (R : Type u) [CommRing R] {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {N : Type u}
  [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] (m : ι → M) (n : ι → N) : Prop
TensorProduct.VanishesTrivially.comment:
An expression $\sum_i m_i \otimes n_i$ in $M \otimes N$
*vanishes trivially* if there exist a finite index type $\kappa$,
elements $(y_j)_{j \in \kappa}$ of $N$, and elements $(a_{ij})_{i \in \iota, j \in \kappa}$ of $R$
such that for all $i$,
$$n_i = \sum_j a_{ij} y_j$$
and for all $j$,
$$\sum_{i} a_{ij} m_i = 0.$$
Note that this condition is not symmetric in $M$ and $N$.
(The terminology "trivial" comes from [Stacks 00HK](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00HK).)
TensorProduct.VanishesTrivially.fullDefinition: abbrev VanishesTrivially : Prop :=   ∃ (κ : Type u) (_ : Fintype κ) (a : ι → κ → R) (y : κ → N),     (∀ i, n i = ∑ j, a i j • y j) ∧ ∀ j, ∑ i, a i j • m i = 0
TensorProduct.VanishesTrivially.description: This definition characterizes when an expression in the tensor product vanishes trivially by requiring a specific linear dependence of elements from one module on elements from another, along with a corresponding relationship between the coefficients.

TensorProduct.sum_tmul_eq_zero_of_vanish.comment:
**Equational criterion for vanishing**
[A. Altman and S. Kleiman, *A term of commutative algebra* (Lemma 8.16)][altman2021term],
backward direction.

If the expression $\sum_i m_i \otimes n_i$ vanishes trivially, then it vanishes.
That is, $\sum_i m_i \otimes n_i = 0$.

  [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] ⦃φ ψ : (α →₀ M) →ₗ[R] N⦄
  (h : ∀ (a : α), φ ∘ₗ lsingle a = ψ ∘ₗ lsingle a) : φ = ψ
Finsupp.lhom_ext'.comment:
Two `R`-linear maps from `Finsupp X M` which agree on each `single x y` agree everywhere.

We formulate this fact using equality of linear maps `φ.comp (lsingle a)` and `ψ.comp (lsingle a)`
so that the `ext` tactic can apply a type-specific extensionality lemma to prove equality of these
maps. E.g., if `M = R`, then it suffices to verify `φ (single a 1) = ψ (single a 1)`.

explanatories.False.elim: From a contradiction, any proposition can be inferred, illustrating that if something is false, anything follows.
explanatories.Set.Subset.trans: The transitive property of set inclusion states that if one set is included in a second set, and that second set is included in a third set, then the first set is also included in the third set.
explanatories.Finset.coe_subset: This theorem states that the inclusion of the extended representations of two finite sets corresponds exactly to the inclusion of the finite sets themselves.
explanatories.Finsupp.support_add: This theorem asserts that the support of the sum of two finitely supported functions is contained within the union of their individual supports.
explanatories.Set.union_subset: The union of two sets, each of which is a subset of a third set, is also a subset of that third set.
explanatories.Finset.coe_union: This theorem states that the union of two finite sets, when expressed in a larger context, is equivalent to the union of their individual representations in that context.
explanatories.Set.subset_def: A set is a subset of another set if and only if every element of the first set is also an element of the second set.
explanatories.Finset.mem_coe: This theorem establishes that an element is a member of a finite set when considered as a subset of a larger set if and only if it is a member of the finite set itself.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element belongs to the set defined by a property if and only if that property holds for the element.

explanatories.Finsupp.support_smul: The support of a scalar multiplication of a finitely supported function is a subset of the support of the original function.

Finsupp.totalOn.comment:
`Finsupp.totalOn M v s` interprets `p : α →₀ R` as a linear combination of a
subset of the vectors in `v`, mapping it to the span of those vectors.

The subset is indicated by a set `s : Set α` of indices.

Finsupp.domLCongr.comment:
An equivalence of domains induces a linear equivalence of finitely supported functions.

This is `Finsupp.domCongr` as a `LinearEquiv`.
See also `LinearMap.funCongrLeft` for the case of arbitrary functions.

explanatories.map_smul: This theorem states that a morphism that is equivariant with respect to the actions of a monoid preserves the action when applied to the product of an element from the monoid and an element from the type.

explanatories.Finsupp.equivMapDomain_eq_mapDomain: The theorem establishes that mapping the domain of a finitely supported function through a bijection is equivalent to using the direct application of the bijection on the domain in the mapping process.
explanatories.Finsupp.domCongr: The domCongr definition establishes a bijective equivalence between finitely supported functions on two types that are related by a given equivalence.

Fintype.total.code:
Fintype.total.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} (R : Type u_3) [Fintype α] [Semiring R]
  [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] (S : Type u_4) [Semiring S] [Module S M] [SMulCommClass R S M] :
  (α → M) →ₗ[S] (α → R) →ₗ[R] M
Fintype.total.comment:
`Fintype.total R S v f` is the linear combination of vectors in `v` with weights in `f`.
This variant of `Finsupp.total` is defined on fintype indexed vectors.

This map is linear in `v` if `R` is commutative, and always linear in `f`.
See note [bundled maps over different rings] for why separate `R` and `S` semirings are used.
