Fintype.total.fullDefinition: protected def Fintype.total : (α → M) →ₗ[S] (α → R) →ₗ[R] M where   toFun v :=     { toFun := fun f => ∑ i, f i • v i       map_add' := fun f g => by simp_rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← add_smul]; rfl       map_smul' := fun r f => by simp_rw [Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul]; rfl }   map_add' u v := by ext; simp [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Pi.add_apply, smul_add]   map_smul' r v := by ext; simp [Finset.smul_sum, smul_comm]
Fintype.total.description: This definition describes a linear mapping that combines vectors indexed by a finite type with coefficients from a possibly different semiring, producing a resulting vector in the module associated with the first semiring.

Submodule.mulLeftMap.comment:
If `M` and `N` are submodules of an `R`-algebra `S`, `m : ι → M` is a family of elements, then
there is an `R`-linear map from `ι →₀ N` to `S` which maps `{ n_i }` to the sum of `m_i * n_i`.
This is used in the definition of linearly disjointness.

Submodule.mulLeftMap.fullDefinition: def mulLeftMap {M : Submodule R S} (N : Submodule R S) {ι : Type*} (m : ι → M) :     (ι →₀ N) →ₗ[R] S := Finsupp.lsum R fun i ↦ (m i).1 • N.subtype
Submodule.mulLeftMap.description: This definition establishes a linear map from finitely supported functions over a submodule to an algebra, which mapping multiple elements from another submodule into their scaled sum.

Submodule.mulRightMap.code:
Submodule.mulRightMap.{u_1, u_4, u_5} {R : Type u_1} [Semiring R] {S : Type u_4} [Semiring S] [Module R S]
  [SMulCommClass R R S] [IsScalarTower R S S] (M : Submodule R S) {N : Submodule R S} {ι : Type u_5} (n : ι → ↥N) :
  (ι →₀ ↥M) →ₗ[R] S
Submodule.mulRightMap.comment:
If `M` and `N` are submodules of an `R`-algebra `S`, `n : ι → N` is a family of elements, then
there is an `R`-linear map from `ι →₀ M` to `S` which maps `{ m_i }` to the sum of `m_i * n_i`.
This is used in the definition of linearly disjointness.

LinearPMap.mkSpanSingleton'.fullDefinition: noncomputable def mkSpanSingleton' (x : E) (y : F) (H : ∀ c : R, c • x = 0 → c • y = 0) :     E →ₗ.[R] F where   domain := R ∙ x   toFun :=     have H : ∀ c₁ c₂ : R, c₁ • x = c₂ • x → c₁ • y = c₂ • y := by       intro c₁ c₂ h       rw [← sub_eq_zero, ← sub_smul] at h ⊢       exact H _ h     { toFun := fun z => Classical.choose (mem_span_singleton.1 z.prop) • y       -- Porting note(#12129): additional beta reduction needed       -- Porting note: Were `Classical.choose_spec (mem_span_singleton.1 _)`.       map_add' := fun y z => by         beta_reduce         rw [← add_smul]         apply H         simp only [add_smul, sub_smul,           fun w : R ∙ x => Classical.choose_spec (mem_span_singleton.1 w.prop)]         apply coe_add       map_smul' := fun c z => by         beta_reduce         rw [smul_smul]         apply H         simp only [mul_smul,           fun w : R ∙ x => Classical.choose_spec (mem_span_singleton.1 w.prop)]         apply coe_smul }

linear_pmap.mk_span_singleton'.fullDefinition: noncomputable def mkSpanSingleton' (x : E) (y : F) (H : ∀ c : R, c • x = 0 → c • y = 0) :     E →ₗ.[R] F where   domain := R ∙ x   toFun :=     have H : ∀ c₁ c₂ : R, c₁ • x = c₂ • x → c₁ • y = c₂ • y := by       intro c₁ c₂ h       rw [← sub_eq_zero, ← sub_smul] at h ⊢       exact H _ h     { toFun := fun z => Classical.choose (mem_span_singleton.1 z.prop) • y       -- Porting note(#12129): additional beta reduction needed       -- Porting note: Were `Classical.choose_spec (mem_span_singleton.1 _)`.       map_add' := fun y z => by         beta_reduce         rw [← add_smul]         apply H         simp only [add_smul, sub_smul,           fun w : R ∙ x => Classical.choose_spec (mem_span_singleton.1 w.prop)]         apply coe_add       map_smul' := fun c z => by         beta_reduce         rw [smul_smul]         apply H         simp only [mul_smul,           fun w : R ∙ x => Classical.choose_spec (mem_span_singleton.1 w.prop)]         apply coe_smul }

Given two partial linear maps `f`, `g`, the set of points `x` such that
both `f` and `g` are defined at `x` and `f x = g x` form a submodule.

LinearPMap.eqLocus.fullDefinition: def eqLocus (f g : E →ₗ.[R] F) : Submodule R E where   carrier := { x | ∃ (hf : x ∈ f.domain) (hg : x ∈ g.domain), f ⟨x, hf⟩ = g ⟨x, hg⟩ }   zero_mem' := ⟨zero_mem _, zero_mem _, f.map_zero.trans g.map_zero.symm⟩   add_mem' := fun {x y} ⟨hfx, hgx, hx⟩ ⟨hfy, hgy, hy⟩ =>     ⟨add_mem hfx hfy, add_mem hgx hgy, by       erw [f.map_add ⟨x, hfx⟩ ⟨y, hfy⟩, g.map_add ⟨x, hgx⟩ ⟨y, hgy⟩, hx, hy]⟩   -- Porting note: `by rintro` is required, or error of a free variable happens.   smul_mem' := by     rintro c x ⟨hfx, hgx, hx⟩     exact       ⟨smul_mem _ c hfx, smul_mem _ c hgx,         by erw [f.map_smul c ⟨x, hfx⟩, g.map_smul c ⟨x, hgx⟩, hx]⟩

LinearPMap.semilatticeInf.fullDefinition: instance semilatticeInf : SemilatticeInf (E →ₗ.[R] F) where   le := (· ≤ ·)   le_refl f := ⟨le_refl f.domain, fun x y h => Subtype.eq h ▸ rfl⟩   le_trans := fun f g h ⟨fg_le, fg_eq⟩ ⟨gh_le, gh_eq⟩ =>     ⟨le_trans fg_le gh_le, fun x z hxz =>       have hxy : (x : E) = inclusion fg_le x := rfl       (fg_eq hxy).trans (gh_eq <| hxy.symm.trans hxz)⟩   le_antisymm f g fg gf := eq_of_le_of_domain_eq fg (le_antisymm fg.1 gf.1)   inf := (· ⊓ ·)   -- Porting note: `by rintro` is required, or error of a metavariable happens.   le_inf := by     rintro f g h ⟨fg_le, fg_eq⟩ ⟨fh_le, fh_eq⟩     exact ⟨fun x hx =>       ⟨fg_le hx, fh_le hx, by         -- Porting note: `[exact ⟨x, hx⟩, rfl, rfl]` → `[skip, exact ⟨x, hx⟩, skip] <;> rfl`         convert (fg_eq _).symm.trans (fh_eq _) <;> [skip; exact ⟨x, hx⟩; skip] <;> rfl⟩,       fun x ⟨y, yg, hy⟩ h => by         apply fg_eq         exact h⟩   inf_le_left f g := ⟨fun x hx => hx.fst, fun x y h => congr_arg f <| Subtype.eq <| h⟩   inf_le_right f g :=     ⟨fun x hx => hx.snd.fst, fun ⟨x, xf, xg, hx⟩ y h => hx.trans <| congr_arg g <| Subtype.eq <| h⟩

LinearPMap.orderBot.fullDefinition: instance orderBot : OrderBot (E →ₗ.[R] F) where   bot := ⊥   bot_le f :=     ⟨bot_le, fun x y h => by       have hx : x = 0 := Subtype.eq ((mem_bot R).1 x.2)       have hy : y = 0 := Subtype.eq (h.symm.trans (congr_arg _ hx))       rw [hx, hy, map_zero, map_zero]⟩

explanatories.RingHom.id_apply: This theorem states that the identity ring homomorphism returns any element from the semiring unchanged.

LinearMap.BilinForm.Nondegenerate.code:
LinearMap.BilinForm.Nondegenerate.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M]
  [Module R M] (B : BilinForm R M) : Prop
LinearMap.BilinForm.Nondegenerate.comment:
A nondegenerate bilinear form is a bilinear form such that the only element that is orthogonal
to every other element is `0`; i.e., for all nonzero `m` in `M`, there exists `n` in `M` with
`B m n ≠ 0`.

Note that for general (neither symmetric nor antisymmetric) bilinear forms this definition has a
chirality; in addition to this "left" nondegeneracy condition one could define a "right"
nondegeneracy condition that in the situation described, `B n m ≠ 0`.  This variant definition is
not currently provided in mathlib. In finite dimension either definition implies the other.
LinearMap.BilinForm.Nondegenerate.fullDefinition: def Nondegenerate (B : BilinForm R M) : Prop :=   ∀ m : M, (∀ n : M, B m n = 0) → m = 0
LinearMap.BilinForm.Nondegenerate.description: This definition states that a bilinear form is nondegenerate if the only element orthogonal to every other element is the zero element.

LinearMap.BilinForm.toDual.code:

  [FiniteDimensional K V] (B : BilinForm K V) (b : B.Nondegenerate) : V ≃ₗ[K] Module.Dual K V
LinearMap.BilinForm.toDual.comment:
Given a nondegenerate bilinear form `B` on a finite-dimensional vector space, `B.toDual` is
the linear equivalence between a vector space and its dual.

explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm: This definition specifies the symmetry of linear equivalences, indicating that the inverse relationship between two modules can be expressed as a linear equivalence in the opposite direction.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.LinearMap.BilinForm.Nondegenerate.ker_eq: This theorem states that if a bilinear form is nondegenerate, then its kernel is trivial.
explanatories.Module.Dual: The dual space of an R-module is defined as the set of all linear maps from that module to the ring R, forming an R-module itself.
explanatories.LinearMap.linearEquivOfInjective: This definition establishes an isomorphism between two finite-dimensional vector spaces when there exists an injective linear map between them and they share the same dimension.
explanatories.LinearMap.ker_eq_bot: The kernel of a linear map is trivial if and only if the map is injective.
explanatories.Subspace.dual_finrank_eq: The finite rank of the dual of a module is equal to the finite rank of the module itself.

LinearMap.BilinForm.toDual.fullDefinition: noncomputable def toDual (B : BilinForm K V) (b : B.Nondegenerate) : V ≃ₗ[K] Module.Dual K V :=   B.linearEquivOfInjective (LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mp <| b.ker_eq_bot)     Subspace.dual_finrank_eq.symm
LinearMap.BilinForm.toDual.description: This definition establishes a linear equivalence between a finite-dimensional vector space and its dual, assuming the existence of a nondegenerate bilinear form on that vector space.

LinearMap.BilinForm.dualBasis.comment:
The `B`-dual basis `B.dualBasis hB b` to a finite basis `b` satisfies
`B (B.dualBasis hB b i) (b j) = B (b i) (B.dualBasis hB b j) = if i = j then 1 else 0`,
where `B` is a nondegenerate (symmetric) bilinear form and `b` is a finite basis.

explanatories.LinearMap.BilinForm.toDual: This definition establishes a linear equivalence between a finite-dimensional vector space and its dual, assuming the existence of a nondegenerate bilinear form on that vector space.
explanatories.FiniteDimensional.of_fintype_basis: A vector space with a finite basis is necessarily finite-dimensional.
explanatories.Basis.dualBasis: A basis for a vector space can be transformed into a basis for its dual space, ensuring a corresponding structure between the two spaces.
explanatories.Basis.map: This definition introduces a new basis for a module formed by applying a given linear equivalence to the original basis vectors.

LinearMap.BilinForm.dualBasis.fullDefinition: noncomputable def dualBasis (B : BilinForm K V) (hB : B.Nondegenerate) (b : Basis ι K V) :     Basis ι K V :=   haveI := FiniteDimensional.of_fintype_basis b   b.dualBasis.map (B.toDual hB).symm
LinearMap.BilinForm.dualBasis.description: This definition introduces a dual basis associated with a nondegenerate bilinear form and a finite basis, ensuring that the dual basis satisfies a specific orthonormality condition with respect to the given bilinear form.

LinearMap.BilinForm.dualSubmodule.comment: The dual submodule of a submodule with respect to a bilinear form.

explanatories.AddMemClass.add_mem: This theorem states that a set defined by an addition property is closed under the operation of addition.
explanatories.LinearMap.BilinForm.zero_left: This theorem states that the value of a bilinear form evaluated at the zero element in its first argument and any element in its second argument is zero.
explanatories.ZeroMemClass.zero_mem: Any element of a set that belongs to a zero-member class contains the zero element.
explanatories.Submodule.smul_mem: This theorem demonstrates that if an element belongs to a submodule, then its scalar multiplication by any element from the semiring also lies within the same submodule, thereby confirming closure under scalar multiplication.
explanatories.IsScalarTower.algebraMap_smul: In a scalar tower, the action of an element from a commutative semiring on a module through the algebra map is equivalent to directly multiplying that element with the module element.
explanatories.algebraMap_smul: This theorem states that the action of an element from a commutative semiring on a module through the algebra map is equivalent to the action of that element directly on the module.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul_of_tower: This theorem indicates that a linear map from one module to another preserves scalar multiplication when both modules are acted on compatibly by two semirings.
explanatories.LinearMap.smul_apply: This theorem states that applying a scalar multiplication to a linear map and then to a vector results in the same output as applying the scalar multiplication directly to the image of the vector under the linear map.

LinearMap.BilinForm.dualSubmodule.fullDefinition: def dualSubmodule (N : Submodule R M) : Submodule R M where   carrier := { x | ∀ y ∈ N, B x y ∈ (1 : Submodule R S) }   add_mem' {a b} ha hb y hy := by simpa using add_mem (ha y hy) (hb y hy)   zero_mem' y _ := by rw [B.zero_left]; exact zero_mem _   smul_mem' r a ha y hy := by     convert (1 : Submodule R S).smul_mem r (ha y hy)     rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_smul S r a]     simp only [algebraMap_smul, map_smul_of_tower, LinearMap.smul_apply]
LinearMap.BilinForm.dualSubmodule.description: This definition introduces the dual submodule associated with a given submodule and a bilinear form, providing a structure that reflects their relationship within the module.

  {N : Submodule R M} {x : M} : x ∈ B.dualSubmodule N ↔ ∀ y ∈ N, (B x) y ∈ 1

LinearMap.BilinForm.mem_dualSubmodule.description: An element belongs to the dual submodule of a submodule with respect to a bilinear form if and only if it satisfies a specific condition involving the bilinear form and all elements of the submodule.

explanatories.LinearMap.BilinForm.dualSubmoduleParing: This definition establishes a natural pairing between the dual submodule related to a bilinear form and a submodule, which is formalized as a bilinear map.
explanatories.Module.Dual: The dual space of an R-module is defined as the set of all linear maps from that module to the ring R, forming an R-module itself.
explanatories.NoZeroSMulDivisors.algebraMap_injective: This theorem establishes that the algebra map from a commutative ring to a ring is injective when the target ring has no zero divisors under scalar multiplication.
explanatories.Algebra.smul_def: This theorem asserts that the scalar multiplication of an element in an algebra by a scalar from a commutative semiring can be expressed as the product of the image of that scalar under the algebra map and the algebra element.
explanatories.LinearMap.ext: This theorem states that if two linear maps agree on all inputs, then they are equal as functions.

LinearMap.BilinForm.dualSubmoduleToDual.fullDefinition: def dualSubmoduleToDual [NoZeroSMulDivisors R S] (N : Submodule R M) :     B.dualSubmodule N →ₗ[R] Module.Dual R N :=   { toFun := fun x ↦     { toFun := B.dualSubmoduleParing x       map_add' := fun x y ↦ NoZeroSMulDivisors.algebraMap_injective R S (by simp)       map_smul' := fun r m ↦ NoZeroSMulDivisors.algebraMap_injective R S         (by simp [← Algebra.smul_def]) }     map_add' := fun x y ↦ LinearMap.ext fun z ↦ NoZeroSMulDivisors.algebraMap_injective R S       (by simp)     map_smul' := fun r x ↦ LinearMap.ext fun y ↦ NoZeroSMulDivisors.algebraMap_injective R S       (by simp [← Algebra.smul_def]) }
LinearMap.BilinForm.dualSubmoduleToDual.description: This definition constructs a linear map that establishes a natural pairing between elements of the dual submodule associated with a bilinear form and elements of a submodule, connecting their structures in a mathematical context.

LinearMap.BilinForm.orthogonal.code:
LinearMap.BilinForm.orthogonal.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
  (B : BilinForm R M) (N : Submodule R M) : Submodule R M
LinearMap.BilinForm.orthogonal.comment:
The orthogonal complement of a submodule `N` with respect to some bilinear form is the set of
elements `x` which are orthogonal to all elements of `N`; i.e., for all `y` in `N`, `B x y = 0`.

Note that for general (neither symmetric nor antisymmetric) bilinear forms this definition has a
chirality; in addition to this "left" orthogonal complement one could define a "right" orthogonal
complement for which, for all `y` in `N`, `B y x = 0`.  This variant definition is not currently
provided in mathlib.

explanatories.MulZeroClass.mul_zero: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by zero results in zero, indicating that zero is an absorbing element in multiplication.
explanatories.LinearMap.BilinForm.add_right: This theorem asserts that the bilinear form exhibits linearity in its second argument, indicating that the value of the form evaluated at an element and the sum of two other elements is equal to the sum of the values of the form evaluated at the first element with each of the two other elements separately.
explanatories.zero_add: This theorem establishes that adding zero to any element in an additive structure results in that same element.
explanatories.LinearMap.BilinForm.smul_right: This theorem establishes that the bilinear form is linear in its second argument, meaning that scaling the second argument by a scalar results in the value of the form being scaled by the same scalar.

LinearMap.BilinForm.orthogonal.description: This definition describes the orthogonal complement of a submodule with respect to a bilinear form, consisting of elements that are orthogonal to all elements in the submodule.

bilin_form.orthogonal.fullDefinition: def orthogonal (B : BilinForm R M) (N : Submodule R M) : Submodule R M where   carrier := { m | ∀ n ∈ N, IsOrtho B n m }   zero_mem' x _ := isOrtho_zero_right x   add_mem' {x y} hx hy n hn := by     rw [IsOrtho, add_right, show B n x = 0 from hx n hn, show B n y = 0 from hy n hn, zero_add]   smul_mem' c x hx n hn := by     rw [IsOrtho, smul_right, show B n x = 0 from hx n hn, mul_zero]

explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function constructs a sum type from an element of the first type.
explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection into the sum type combines an element from one type with the sum type, indicating it originates from the second type.

explanatories.Or.inr: If there is a proof of a proposition, it can be included in a disjunction as the second option.

linearIndependent_sum.description: A family of vectors is linearly independent if and only if both of its components, defined by separate functions on disjoint sets, are independently spanning and their spans do not overlap.

LinearIndependent.totalEquiv.comment: Canonical isomorphism between linear combinations and the span of linearly independent vectors.

explanatories.Finsupp.total: This definition establishes a linear map that interprets finitely supported functions as linear combinations based on a given family of functions from one type to a module.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.Submodule.span: This defines the smallest submodule of a module that contains a given set of vectors.
explanatories.Set.mem_range_self: An element obtained by applying a function to an index is guaranteed to be part of the range of that function.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ofBijective: This definition states that a bijective linear transformation between modules establishes a linear equivalence between them.
explanatories.LinearMap.codRestrict: This definition describes a linear map that restricts the codomain of a given linear map to a specified submodule, ensuring that all outputs lie within that submodule.
explanatories.LinearMap.ker_eq_bot: The kernel of a linear map is trivial if and only if the map is injective.
explanatories.LinearMap.ker_codRestrict: The kernel of the codomain restriction of a linear map is equal to the kernel of the original linear map if the image of the restricted map lies within a specified submodule.
explanatories.Finsupp.range_total: This theorem states that the range of a linear map formed by associating finitely supported functions with their corresponding module values is equal to the span over the semiring of the images of those functions.
explanatories.LinearMap.mem_range: This theorem states that an element is in the range of a linear map if and only if there exists some input that maps to that element via the linear map.
explanatories.LinearMap.range_eq_top: This theorem states that the range of a linear map is the entire codomain if and only if the map is surjective.
explanatories.LinearMap.range_eq_map: This theorem states that the range of a linear map is equal to the image of the map applied to the whole space.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_codRestrict: This theorem asserts that the image of a submodule under a linear map restricted to another submodule is equivalent to the preimage of that submodule under the composition of the original linear map and the inclusion of the first submodule.
explanatories.LinearMap.range_le_iff_comap: This theorem states that the range of a linear map is contained in a submodule if and only if the preimage of that submodule under the map is the entire domain.
explanatories.Submodule.range_subtype: This theorem establishes that the image of the entire module under a semilinear map is equal to the range of that map.
explanatories.Submodule.map_top: This theorem establishes that the image of the entire module under a semilinear map is equal to the range of that map.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.range: This theorem establishes that the range of a semilinear equivalence between two modules is the entire target module.

LinearIndependent.totalEquiv.fullDefinition: def LinearIndependent.totalEquiv (hv : LinearIndependent R v) :     (ι →₀ R) ≃ₗ[R] span R (range v) := by   apply LinearEquiv.ofBijective (LinearMap.codRestrict (span R (range v)) (Finsupp.total ι M R v) _)   constructor   · rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, LinearMap.ker_codRestrict]     · apply hv     · intro l       rw [← Finsupp.range_total]       rw [LinearMap.mem_range]       apply mem_range_self l   · rw [← LinearMap.range_eq_top, LinearMap.range_eq_map, LinearMap.map_codRestrict, ←       LinearMap.range_le_iff_comap, range_subtype, Submodule.map_top]     rw [Finsupp.range_total]
LinearIndependent.totalEquiv.description: There exists a canonical isomorphism between the vector space of linear combinations of linearly independent vectors and the span of those vectors.

LinearIndependent.repr.comment:
Linear combination representing a vector in the span of linearly independent vectors.

Given a family of linearly independent vectors, we can represent any vector in their span as
a linear combination of these vectors. These are provided by this linear map.
It is simply one direction of `LinearIndependent.total_equiv`.

explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Submodule.span: This defines the smallest submodule of a module that contains a given set of vectors.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.

Submodule.quotientRel.code:
Submodule.quotientRel.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
  (p : Submodule R M) : Setoid M
Submodule.quotientRel.comment:
The equivalence relation associated to a submodule `p`, defined by `x ≈ y` iff `-x + y ∈ p`.

Module.rank.code: Module.rank.{u_1, u_2} (R : Type u_1) (M : Type u_2) [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] : Cardinal.{u_2}
Module.rank.comment:
The rank of a module, defined as a term of type `Cardinal`.

We define this as the supremum of the cardinalities of linearly independent subsets.

For a free module over any ring satisfying the strong rank condition
(e.g. left-noetherian rings, commutative rings, and in particular division rings and fields),
this is the same as the dimension of the space (i.e. the cardinality of any basis).

In particular this agrees with the usual notion of the dimension of a vector space.

lift_rank_le_of_injective_injective.code:
lift_rank_le_of_injective_injective.{u, u', v, v'} {R : Type u} {R' : Type u'} {M : Type v} {M' : Type v'} [Ring R]
  [Ring R'] [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M] [Module R' M'] (i : R' → R) (j : M →+ M')
  (hi : ∀ (r : R'), i r = 0 → r = 0) (hj : Injective ⇑j) (hc : ∀ (r : R') (m : M), j (i r • m) = r • j m) :
  lift.{v', v} (Module.rank R M) ≤ lift.{v, v'} (Module.rank R' M')
lift_rank_le_of_injective_injective.comment:
If `M / R` and `M' / R'` are modules, `i : R' → R` is a map which sends non-zero elements to
non-zero elements, `j : M →+ M'` is an injective group homomorphism, such that the scalar
multiplications on `M` and `M'` are compatible, then the rank of `M / R` is smaller than or equal to
the rank of `M' / R'`. As a special case, taking `R = R'` it is
`LinearMap.lift_rank_le_of_injective`.

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

lift_rank_le_of_injective_injective.description: The rank of a module over one ring is less than or equal to the rank of another module over a different ring if there is an injective homomorphism connecting them with compatible scalar multiplications.

  lift.{v', v} (Module.rank R M) ≤ lift.{v, v'} (Module.rank R' M')
lift_rank_le_of_surjective_injective.comment:
If `M / R` and `M' / R'` are modules, `i : R → R'` is a surjective map which maps zero to zero,
`j : M →+ M'` is an injective group homomorphism, such that the scalar multiplications on `M` and
`M'` are compatible, then the rank of `M / R` is smaller than or equal to the rank of `M' / R'`.
As a special case, taking `R = R'` it is `LinearMap.lift_rank_le_of_injective`.

lift_rank_le_of_surjective_injective.description: The rank of one module is less than or equal to the rank of another module when there exists a surjective ring homomorphism and an injective group homomorphism that are compatible with their respective scalar multiplications.

lift_rank_eq_of_equiv_equiv.comment:
If `M / R` and `M' / R'` are modules, `i : R → R'` is a bijective map which maps zero to zero,
`j : M ≃+ M'` is a group isomorphism, such that the scalar multiplications on `M` and `M'` are
compatible, then the rank of `M / R` is equal to the rank of `M' / R'`.
As a special case, taking `R = R'` it is `LinearEquiv.lift_rank_eq`.

lift_rank_eq_of_equiv_equiv.description: The rank of one module is equal to the rank of another module when there is a bijective homomorphism between their scalar fields and an isomorphism between the modules that preserves scalar multiplication.

Algebra.lift_rank_le_of_injective_injective.{w, w', v, v'} {R : Type w} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [Ring S] [Algebra R S]
  {R' : Type w'} {S' : Type v'} [CommRing R'] [Ring S'] [Algebra R' S'] (i : R' →+* R) (j : S →+* S')
  (hi : Injective ⇑i) (hj : Injective ⇑j) (hc : (j.comp (algebraMap R S)).comp i = algebraMap R' S') :
  lift.{v', v} (Module.rank R S) ≤ lift.{v, v'} (Module.rank R' S')
Algebra.lift_rank_le_of_injective_inject.comment:
If `S / R` and `S' / R'` are algebras, `i : R' →+* R` and `j : S →+* S'` are injective ring
homomorphisms, such that `R' → R → S → S'` and `R' → S'` commute, then the rank of `S / R` is
smaller than or equal to the rank of `S' / R'`.

[Les familles libres maximales d'un module ont-elles le meme cardinal?][lazarus1973]

  [StrongRankCondition R] [IsDomain R] [Finite ι] (b : Basis ι R M) (P : Submodule R M → Sort u_1)
  (ih :
    (N : Submodule R M) →
      ((N' : Submodule R M) → N' ≤ N → (x : M) → x ∈ N → (∀ (c : R), ∀ y ∈ N', c • x + y = 0 → c = 0) → P N') → P N)
  (N : Submodule R M) : P N
Submodule.inductionOnRank.comment:
An induction (and recursion) principle for proving results about all submodules of a fixed
finite free module `M`. A property is true for all submodules of `M` if it satisfies the following
"inductive step": the property is true for a submodule `N` if it's true for all submodules `N'`
of `N` with the property that there exists `0 ≠ x ∈ N` such that the sum `N' + Rx` is direct.

explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.
explanatories.Basis.card_le_card_of_linearIndependent: If a module with a strong rank condition has a basis, then the cardinality of any linearly independent set is less than or equal to the cardinality of the basis.
explanatories.Submodule.inductionOnRankAux: This definition describes a method for performing induction on a property related to submodules of finite rank by adjoining a linearly independent element.
explanatories.Nat.card: This definition assigns a natural number representing the cardinality of a type, with the convention that infinite types are assigned the value zero.

Submodule.inductionOnRank.fullDefinition: def Submodule.inductionOnRank [IsDomain R] [Finite ι] (b : Basis ι R M)     (P : Submodule R M → Sort*) (ih : ∀ N : Submodule R M,     (∀ N' ≤ N, ∀ x ∈ N, (∀ (c : R), ∀ y ∈ N', c • x + y = (0 : M) → c = 0) → P N') → P N)     (N : Submodule R M) : P N :=   letI := Fintype.ofFinite ι   Submodule.inductionOnRankAux b P ih (Fintype.card ι) N fun hs hli => by     simpa using b.card_le_card_of_linearIndependent hli

fin_dim_vectorspace_equiv.fullDefinition: def finDimVectorspaceEquiv (n : ℕ) (hn : Module.rank R M = n) : M ≃ₗ[R] Fin n → R := by   haveI := nontrivial_of_invariantBasisNumber R   have : Cardinal.lift.{u} (n : Cardinal.{v}) = Cardinal.lift.{v} (n : Cardinal.{u}) := by simp   have hn := Cardinal.lift_inj.{v, u}.2 hn   rw [this] at hn   rw [← @rank_fin_fun R _ _ n] at hn   haveI : Module.Free R (Fin n → R) := Module.Free.pi _ _   exact Classical.choice (nonempty_linearEquiv_of_lift_rank_eq hn)
fin_dim_vectorspace_equiv.description: An n-dimensional vector space over a ring is isomorphic to the space of functions from a finite set of n elements to the ring.

SameRay.code:
SameRay.{u_1, u_2} (R : Type u_1) [StrictOrderedCommSemiring R] {M : Type u_2} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
  (v₁ v₂ : M) : Prop
SameRay.comment:
Two vectors are in the same ray if either one of them is zero or some positive multiples of them
are equal (in the typical case over a field, this means one of them is a nonnegative multiple of
the other).
SameRay.fullDefinition: def SameRay (v₁ v₂ : M) : Prop :=   v₁ = 0 ∨ v₂ = 0 ∨ ∃ r₁ r₂ : R, 0 < r₁ ∧ 0 < r₂ ∧ r₁ • v₁ = r₂ • v₂
SameRay.description: This definition characterizes two vectors as being in the same ray if they are either both zero or there exists a positive scalar such that one vector is a multiple of the other.

same_ray.fullDefinition: def SameRay (v₁ v₂ : M) : Prop :=   v₁ = 0 ∨ v₂ = 0 ∨ ∃ r₁ r₂ : R, 0 < r₁ ∧ 0 < r₂ ∧ r₁ • v₁ = r₂ • v₂

explanatories.SameRay: This definition characterizes two vectors as being in the same ray if they are either both zero or there exists a positive scalar such that one vector is a multiple of the other.

explanatories.SameRay.trans: This theorem asserts that if two vectors are in the same ray and a third vector is in the same ray with one of them, then the first and third vectors are also in the same ray, provided that the middle vector is not zero unless at least one of the other vectors is zero.
explanatories.M): This definition establishes a natural way to treat ray vectors as elements of the underlying vector space.
explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.

explanatories.Equiv.refl: This definition states that every type is self-equivalent, meaning it has an equivalence relation to itself.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm: This definition specifies the symmetry of linear equivalences, indicating that the inverse relationship between two modules can be expressed as a linear equivalence in the opposite direction.

explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.

explanatories.LinearMap.comp: This definition states that the composition of two linear maps, each between different modules over semirings, results in another linear map that connects the first and last modules directly.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.LinearMap.range_eq_top: This theorem states that the range of a linear map is the entire codomain if and only if the map is surjective.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm: This definition specifies the symmetry of linear equivalences, indicating that the inverse relationship between two modules can be expressed as a linear equivalence in the opposite direction.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ofBijective: This definition states that a bijective linear transformation between modules establishes a linear equivalence between them.
explanatories.LinearMap.ker_eq_bot: The kernel of a linear map is trivial if and only if the map is injective.
explanatories.LinearMap.ker_comp: The kernel of the composition of two linear maps is equal to the preimage under the first map of the kernel of the second map.
explanatories.Submodule.ker_mkQ: This theorem states that the kernel of the quotient map associated with a submodule is exactly the submodule itself.
explanatories.Submodule.disjoint_iff_comap_eq_bot: The theorem states that two submodules are disjoint if and only if the preimage of one through the inclusion map of the other is the zero submodule.
explanatories.IsCompl.symm: The complementary relationship between two elements in a bounded partially ordered set is symmetric.
explanatories.IsCompl.disjoint: If two elements are complementary in a partially ordered set with bounds, then they are disjoint.
explanatories.LinearMap.range_comp: This theorem states that the range of the composition of two linear maps is equal to the image of the range of the first linear map under the second linear map.
explanatories.Submodule.range_subtype: This theorem establishes that the image of the entire module under a semilinear map is equal to the range of that map.
explanatories.Submodule.map_mkQ_eq_top: This theorem states that the image of a submodule's quotient map is equal to the entire module if and only if the join of two submodules is the entirety of the module.
explanatories.IsCompl.sup_eq_top: If two elements in a lattice are complementary, then their supremum is equal to the top element of the lattice.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.

Submodule.quotientEquivOfIsCompl.fullDefinition: def quotientEquivOfIsCompl (h : IsCompl p q) : (E ⧸ p) ≃ₗ[R] q :=   LinearEquiv.symm <|     LinearEquiv.ofBijective (p.mkQ.comp q.subtype)       ⟨by rw [← ker_eq_bot, ker_comp, ker_mkQ, disjoint_iff_comap_eq_bot.1 h.symm.disjoint], by         rw [← range_eq_top, range_comp, range_subtype, map_mkQ_eq_top, h.sup_eq_top]⟩
Submodule.quotientEquivOfIsCompl.description: The quotient of a module by a submodule is isomorphic to another submodule when the latter serves as a complement to the former.

Submodule.prodEquivOfIsCompl.comment:
If `q` is a complement of `p`, then `p × q` is isomorphic to `E`. It is the unique
linear map `f : E → p` such that `f x = x` for `x ∈ p` and `f x = 0` for `x ∈ q`.

explanatories.LinearMap.ofIsCompl_smul: Scaling linear maps defined on complementary submodules by a common scalar results in a linear map that is effectively scaled by that same scalar.
explanatories.Prod.snd_add: The second component of the sum of two pairs equals the sum of their respective second components.
explanatories.Prod.fst_add: The first component of the sum of two pairs equals the sum of their respective first components.
explanatories.Prod.smul_snd: This theorem confirms that when multiplying a pair of elements by a scalar, the operation applied to the second component of the pair yields the same result as applying the scalar directly to that component.
explanatories.Prod.smul_fst: This theorem asserts that when multiplying a pair of elements with a scalar, the operation applied to the first component of the pair yields the same result as applying the scalar directly to that component.

linear_map.of_is_compl_prod.fullDefinition: def ofIsComplProd {p q : Submodule R₁ E} (h : IsCompl p q) :     (p →ₗ[R₁] F) × (q →ₗ[R₁] F) →ₗ[R₁] E →ₗ[R₁] F where   toFun φ := ofIsCompl h φ.1 φ.2   map_add' := by intro φ ψ; dsimp only; rw [Prod.snd_add, Prod.fst_add, ofIsCompl_add]   map_smul' := by intro c φ; simp [Prod.smul_snd, Prod.smul_fst, ofIsCompl_smul]
linear_map.of_is_compl_prod.description: The linear map constructed from the product of two linear maps defined on complementary submodules gives a linear map from the whole module to the target module.

LinearMap.ofIsComplProd_apply.description: The linear map constructed from the product of two complementary submodules is equal to the linear map derived from the individual mappings of each submodule.

explanatories.Submodule.ext: This theorem states that two submodules of a module are equal if every element of one is also an element of the other.
explanatories.LinearMap.ext: This theorem states that if two linear maps agree on all inputs, then they are equal as functions.
explanatories.Submodule.existsUnique_add_of_isCompl: Given two complementary submodules, any element in the larger module can be uniquely expressed as a sum of elements from each of the submodules.
explanatories.LinearMap.ofIsCompl_left_apply: The image of an element from a complementary submodule under a linear map defined on the submodules corresponds exactly to the value of that linear map at that element.
explanatories.LinearMap.ofIsCompl_right_apply: The linear map constructed from two complementary submodules evaluates the element from the right submodule to its corresponding image in the codomain module.
explanatories.LinearMap.domRestrict: This definition describes a linear map that restricts a given linear transformation from a module to a submodule.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.

LinearMap.ofIsComplProdEquiv.fullDefinition: def ofIsComplProdEquiv {p q : Submodule R₁ E} (h : IsCompl p q) :     ((p →ₗ[R₁] F) × (q →ₗ[R₁] F)) ≃ₗ[R₁] E →ₗ[R₁] F :=   { ofIsComplProd h with     invFun := fun φ => ⟨φ.domRestrict p, φ.domRestrict q⟩     left_inv := fun φ ↦ by       ext x       · exact ofIsCompl_left_apply h x       · exact ofIsCompl_right_apply h x     right_inv := fun φ ↦ by       ext x       obtain ⟨a, b, hab, _⟩ := existsUnique_add_of_isCompl h x       rw [← hab]; simp }
LinearMap.ofIsComplProdEquiv.description: This defines a natural linear equivalence between the direct sum of linear maps from each of two complementary submodules to a codomain and a linear map from the entire module to the codomain.

  [Module R E] {F : Type u_3} [AddCommGroup F] [Module R F] {G : Type u_4} [AddCommGroup G] [Module R G] (f : E →ₗ[R] F)
  (g : E →ₗ[R] G) (hf : range f = ⊤) (hg : range g = ⊤) (hfg : IsCompl (ker f) (ker g)) : E ≃ₗ[R] F × G
LinearMap.equivProdOfSurjectiveOfIsCompl.comment:
If `f : E →ₗ[R] F` and `g : E →ₗ[R] G` are two surjective linear maps and
their kernels are complement of each other, then `x ↦ (f x, g x)` defines
a linear equivalence `E ≃ₗ[R] F × G`.

explanatories.LinearMap.range: This definition states that the range of a linear map between modules is a submodule of the codomain module.
explanatories.LinearMap.range_eq_top: This theorem states that the range of a linear map is the entire codomain if and only if the map is surjective.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ofBijective: This definition states that a bijective linear transformation between modules establishes a linear equivalence between them.
explanatories.LinearMap.ker_eq_bot: The kernel of a linear map is trivial if and only if the map is injective.
explanatories.IsCompl.sup_eq_top: If two elements in a lattice are complementary, then their supremum is equal to the top element of the lattice.
explanatories.LinearMap.prod: This definition state that the combination of two linear maps into a new linear map produces a mapping from one module to a product of two other modules.
explanatories.IsCompl.inf_eq_bot: If two elements in a lattice are complements of each other, then their infimum is the least element of that lattice.
explanatories.LinearMap.range_prod_eq: This theorem states that if the combination of the kernels of two linear maps spans the entire domain, then the range of their product map is equal to the product of their individual ranges.

LinearMap.equivProdOfSurjectiveOfIsCompl.fullDefinition: def equivProdOfSurjectiveOfIsCompl (f : E →ₗ[R] F) (g : E →ₗ[R] G) (hf : range f = ⊤)     (hg : range g = ⊤) (hfg : IsCompl (ker f) (ker g)) : E ≃ₗ[R] F × G :=   LinearEquiv.ofBijective (f.prod g)     ⟨by simp [← ker_eq_bot, hfg.inf_eq_bot], by       rw [← range_eq_top]       simp [range_prod_eq hfg.sup_eq_top, *]⟩
LinearMap.equivProdOfSurjectiveOfIsCompl.description: When two surjective linear maps have complementary kernels, an element can be uniquely represented as a pair of its images under these maps, establishing a linear isomorphism between the original module and the product of the two target modules.

explanatories.Subtype.coe_mk: This theorem shows that the value of an element formed by a subtype is equal to the underlying value itself when the property is satisfied.
explanatories.LinearMap.isCompl_of_proj: The submodule is complementary to the kernel of a linear map when every element of the submodule is preserved by that map.
explanatories.Submodule.linearProjOfIsCompl_apply_left: The linear projection associated with a complementary submodule returns the original element when applied to an element from the first submodule.
explanatories.Submodule.linearProjOfIsCompl_ker: The kernel of the linear projection from one complementary submodule onto another is equal to the second submodule itself.
explanatories.LinearMap.linearProjOfIsCompl_of_proj: The linear projection onto a complementary submodule, determined by a linear map that acts as the identity on its domain, coincides with the original linear map.
explanatories.Subtype.eq: If two elements of a subtype have the same underlying value, then they are considered equal as elements of that subtype.

Submodule.isComplEquivProj.fullDefinition: def isComplEquivProj : { q // IsCompl p q } ≃ { f : E →ₗ[R] p // ∀ x : p, f x = x } where   toFun q := ⟨linearProjOfIsCompl p q q.2, linearProjOfIsCompl_apply_left q.2⟩   invFun f := ⟨ker (f : E →ₗ[R] p), isCompl_of_proj f.2⟩   left_inv := fun ⟨q, hq⟩ => by simp only [linearProjOfIsCompl_ker, Subtype.coe_mk]   right_inv := fun ⟨f, hf⟩ => Subtype.eq <| f.linearProjOfIsCompl_of_proj hf
Submodule.isComplEquivProj.description: This establishes a natural equivalence between submodules that are complementary to a given submodule and linear maps that act as identity on elements of that submodule.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.DFinsupp.mk: This definition constructs a finitely-supported dependent function from a given finite set and a function defined on that set.
explanatories.DFinsupp.mk_add: This theorem asserts that the operation of constructing a finitely supported function from the sum of two finitely supported functions is equivalent to constructing it from the sum of their respective components.
explanatories.DFinsupp.mk_smul: This theorem demonstrates that scaling a finitely supported function by a constant results in the same output as scaling the constructed function from its indexed values.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul': This theorem asserts that a specific linear map interacts with scalar multiplication in such a way that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is equivalent to multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar's image under a specified semiring homomorphism.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This theorem states that for any element and a property it satisfies, one can construct a subtype consisting of elements that possess that property.
explanatories.Finsupp.mk: This theorem provides a construction method for creating a finitely supported function from a specified support set and a mapping function, ensuring the function's non-zero values correspond to the elements in the support.

DFinsupp.lmk.fullDefinition: def lmk (s : Finset ι) : (∀ i : (↑s : Set ι), M i) →ₗ[R] Π₀ i, M i where   toFun := mk s   map_add' _ _ := mk_add   map_smul' c x := mk_smul c x
DFinsupp.lmk.description: A function maps elements from a finite set of indices to a direct sum of their corresponding modules in a way that preserves linearity.

explanatories.DFinsupp.single_smul: This theorem demonstrates that scaling the value of a finitely supported function at a specific index by a scalar yields a function that is equivalent to scaling the entire function itself, preserving the structure of finitely supported functions.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp: This definition states that the composition of two linear maps, each between different modules over semirings, results in another linear map that connects the first and last modules directly.
explanatories.DFinsupp.lhom_ext': If two linear maps from a finitely supported function space agree on the linear combinations formed by the action of single-index mappings, then they are equal as linear maps across the entire function space.
explanatories.DFinsupp.sumAddHom: This definition specifies a homomorphism that maps finitely supported functions to a commutative monoid, applying a given additive function to each supported value in the summation.
explanatories.LinearMap.toAddMonoidHom: This definition describes how to convert a linear map into an additive homomorphism between two modules over semirings.
explanatories.DFinsupp.liftAddHom: This definition establishes a bijective correspondence between additive homomorphisms from dependent functions and those from finitely supported functions, under certain conditions.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.map_add: This theorem asserts that an additive monoid homomorphism preserves the addition operation, meaning the image of the sum of two elements is equal to the sum of their images.
explanatories.DFinsupp.induction: This theorem provides a principle of induction for finitely supported functions, allowing one to establish a property for such functions by demonstrating it for the zero function and a successor constructed by adding a non-zero value at a specified index.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.map_zero: An additive monoid homomorphism maps the zero element of one additive monoid to the zero element of another.
explanatories.DFinsupp.sumAddHom_single: This theorem asserts that the sum of a homomorphism applied to a finitely supported function that assigns a value at a single index equals the result of applying the homomorphism directly at that index.
explanatories.LinearMap.toAddMonoidHom_coe: This theorem demonstrates that the function associated with a linear map, when viewed as an additive monoid homomorphism, is identical to the original linear map's function itself.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear map commutes with scalar multiplication, meaning that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is the same as multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_zero: This theorem demonstrates that a linear map assigns the zero element of its domain to the zero element of its codomain.
explanatories.LinearMap.ext: This theorem states that if two linear maps agree on all inputs, then they are equal as functions.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.map_zero: This theorem asserts that the linear equivalence maps the zero element of one module to the zero element of another module.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul': This theorem asserts that a specific linear map interacts with scalar multiplication in such a way that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is equivalent to multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar's image under a specified semiring homomorphism.
explanatories.Equiv.left_inv: This theorem asserts that the inverse function of an equivalence relation is a left inverse of the original function.
explanatories.Equiv.right_inv: This theorem states that the inverse function of an equivalence relation has a right inverse that retrieves the original function.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ext: This theorem establishes that if two linear equivalences agree on their action for all elements, then they are identical.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.comp: This definition states that the composition of morphisms between additive monoids results in a morphism that also operates within the framework of additive monoids.
explanatories.AddEquiv.toAddMonoidHom: This definition describes the process of extracting the additive function that preserves addition from an additive equivalence between two structures.

DFinsupp.lsum.fullDefinition: def lsum [Semiring S] [Module S N] [SMulCommClass R S N] :     (∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] N) ≃ₗ[S] (Π₀ i, M i) →ₗ[R] N where   toFun F :=     { toFun := sumAddHom fun i => (F i).toAddMonoidHom       map_add' := (DFinsupp.liftAddHom fun (i : ι) => (F i).toAddMonoidHom).map_add       map_smul' := fun c f => by         dsimp         apply DFinsupp.induction f         · rw [smul_zero, AddMonoidHom.map_zero, smul_zero]         · intro a b f _ _ hf           rw [smul_add, AddMonoidHom.map_add, AddMonoidHom.map_add, smul_add, hf, ← single_smul,             sumAddHom_single, sumAddHom_single, LinearMap.toAddMonoidHom_coe,             LinearMap.map_smul] }   invFun F i := F.comp (lsingle i)   left_inv F := by     ext     simp   right_inv F := by     refine DFinsupp.lhom_ext' (fun i ↦ ?_)     ext     simp   map_add' F G := by     refine DFinsupp.lhom_ext' (fun i ↦ ?_)     ext     simp   map_smul' c F := by     refine DFinsupp.lhom_ext' (fun i ↦ ?_)     ext     simp
DFinsupp.lsum.description: A linear isomorphism is established between a family of linear functions from a module to another module and a linear function that maps finitely supported functions to an output module.

DFinsupp.mapRange_smul.{u_1, u_2, u_7, u_8} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [Semiring R] {β₁ : ι → Type u_7}
  {β₂ : ι → Type u_8} [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (β₁ i)] [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (β₂ i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (β₁ i)]
  [(i : ι) → Module R (β₂ i)] (f : (i : ι) → β₁ i → β₂ i) (hf : ∀ (i : ι), f i 0 = 0) (r : R)
  (hf' : ∀ (i : ι) (x : β₁ i), f i (r • x) = r • f i x) (g : Π₀ (i : ι), β₁ i) :
  mapRange f hf (r • g) = r • mapRange f hf g
DFinsupp.mapRange_smul.description: Scaling a finitely supported function and then applying a mapping transforms it in a way that is equivalent to first applying the mapping and then scaling the result.

explanatories.LinearMap.toAddMonoidHom: This definition describes how to convert a linear map into an additive homomorphism between two modules over semirings.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.map_zero: An additive monoid homomorphism maps the zero element of one additive monoid to the zero element of another.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear map commutes with scalar multiplication, meaning that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is the same as multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar.

explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul': This theorem asserts that a specific linear map interacts with scalar multiplication in such a way that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is equivalent to multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar's image under a specified semiring homomorphism.
explanatories.AddEquiv.toAddMonoidHom: This definition describes the process of extracting the additive function that preserves addition from an additive equivalence between two structures.

DFinsupp.mapRange.linearMap.description: A linear map is defined that transforms finitely supported functions from one type to another by applying a specified linear function at each index.

  {β₁ : ι → Type u_7} {β₂ : ι → Type u_8} [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (β i)] [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (β₁ i)]
  [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (β₂ i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (β i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (β₁ i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (β₂ i)]

DFinsupp.coprodMap.code:
DFinsupp.coprodMap.{u_1, u_2, u_4, u_5} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} {M : ι → Type u_4} {N : Type u_5} [Semiring R]
  [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (M i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (M i)] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [DecidableEq ι]
  (f : (i : ι) → M i →ₗ[R] N) : (Π₀ (i : ι), M i) →ₗ[R] N
DFinsupp.coprodMap.comment:
Given a family of linear maps `f i : M i →ₗ[R] N`, we can form a linear map
`(Π₀ i, M i) →ₗ[R] N` which sends `x : Π₀ i, M i` to the sum over `i` of `f i` applied to `x i`.
This is the map coming from the universal property of `Π₀ i, M i` as the coproduct of the `M i`.
See also `LinearMap.coprod` for the binary product version.

explanatories.DFinsupp.lsum: A linear isomorphism is established between a family of linear functions from a module to another module and a linear function that maps finitely supported functions to an output module.
explanatories.DFinsupp.mapRange.linearMap: A linear map is defined that transforms finitely supported functions from one type to another by applying a specified linear function at each index.
explanatories.DFinsupp.sum_mapRange_index.linearMap: The sum of the images under a linear map of a finitely supported function can be expressed as the linear combination of the images obtained by composing two linear maps applied to its components.

DFinsupp.coprodMap.fullDefinition: def coprodMap (f : ∀ i : ι, M i →ₗ[R] N) : (Π₀ i, M i) →ₗ[R] N :=   (DFinsupp.lsum ℕ fun _ : ι => LinearMap.id) ∘ₗ DFinsupp.mapRange.linearMap f
DFinsupp.coprodMap.description: A linear map is constructed from a family of linear functions such that it sums the results of applying each linear function to a finitely supported function.

DFinsupp.coprodMap_apply.code:
DFinsupp.coprodMap_apply.{u_1, u_2, u_4, u_5} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} {M : ι → Type u_4} {N : Type u_5}
  [Semiring R] [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (M i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (M i)] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [DecidableEq ι]
  [(x : N) → Decidable (x ≠ 0)] (f : (i : ι) → M i →ₗ[R] N) (x : Π₀ (i : ι), M i) :
  (coprodMap f) x = (mapRange (fun i => ⇑(f i)) ⋯ x).sum fun x => id

Submodule.iSup_eq_range_dfinsupp_lsum.comment:
The supremum of a family of submodules is equal to the range of `DFinsupp.lsum`; that is
every element in the `iSup` can be produced from taking a finite number of non-zero elements
of `p i`, coercing them to `N`, and summing them.

  [DecidableEq ι] [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] (p : ι → Submodule R N) :

    ∀ (i : ι) (x : ↥(p i)) (v : Π₀ (i : ι), ↥(p i)), ((lsum ℕ) fun i => (p i).subtype) (erase i v) = ↑x → x = 0
CompleteLattice.independent_iff_forall_d.comment:
Independence of a family of submodules can be expressed as a quantifier over `DFinsupp`s.

`CompleteLattice.independent_of_dfinsupp_lsum_injective` and
`CompleteLattice.Independent.dfinsupp_lsum_injective`.

CompleteLattice.Independent.dfinsupp_lsu.comment:
The canonical map out of a direct sum of a family of submodules is injective when the submodules
are `CompleteLattice.Independent`.

Note that this is not generally true for `[Semiring R]`, for instance when `A` is the
`ℕ`-submodules of the positive and negative integers.

See `Counterexamples/DirectSumIsInternal.lean` for a proof of this fact.

Submodule.piQuotientLift.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [CommRing R] {Ms : ι → Type u_3}
  [(i : ι) → AddCommGroup (Ms i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (Ms i)] {N : Type u_4} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Fintype ι]
  [DecidableEq ι] (p : (i : ι) → Submodule R (Ms i)) (q : Submodule R N) (f : (i : ι) → Ms i →ₗ[R] N)
  (hf : ∀ (i : ι), p i ≤ comap (f i) q) : ((i : ι) → Ms i ⧸ p i) →ₗ[R] N ⧸ q
Submodule.piQuotientLift.comment: Lift a family of maps to the direct sum of quotients.

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.Submodule.comap: This definition introduces the pullback of a submodule through a semilinear map, producing a corresponding submodule in the original space.
explanatories.LinearMap.lsum: This definition establishes a linear equivalence between linear functions defined on a finite product of modules and families of functions over those modules.
explanatories.Submodule.mapQ: This definition establishes a linear map from the quotient of one module by a submodule to the quotient of another module by a corresponding submodule through a specified linear transformation.

Submodule.piQuotientLift.fullDefinition: def piQuotientLift [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (p : ∀ i, Submodule R (Ms i)) (q : Submodule R N)     (f : ∀ i, Ms i →ₗ[R] N) (hf : ∀ i, p i ≤ q.comap (f i)) : (∀ i, Ms i ⧸ p i) →ₗ[R] N ⧸ q :=   lsum R (fun i => Ms i ⧸ p i) R fun i => (p i).mapQ q (f i) (hf i)
Submodule.piQuotientLift.description: This definition describes a mapping that allows the lifting of a collection of linear functions from a family of quotient modules to facilitate their interaction with another quotient module formed by a different submodule.

explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.LinearMap.pi: This defines a linear function that maps an element to a family of modules based on a collection of linear functions.
explanatories.Submodule.quotientPi_aux.invFun: This definition establishes a function that translates a collection of individual quotient modules into a single quotient module formed by a product of submodules.
explanatories.Submodule.quotientPi_aux.toFun: This definition describes a mapping from the quotient of a family of modules under a product of submodules to an individual quotient module corresponding to each submodule in that family.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear map commutes with scalar multiplication, meaning that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is the same as multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar.
explanatories.Submodule.quotientPi_aux.map_add: This theorem asserts that the function defined on a quotient of a family of modules preserves addition, meaning that the image of the sum of two representatives in the quotient is equal to the sum of their images.
explanatories.Submodule.quotientPi_aux.map_smul: This theorem establishes that scaling an element in a quotient module by a scalar results in the same scaling effect when the element is first mapped through a specific function related to that quotient.
explanatories.Submodule.quotientPi_aux.left_inv: This theorem establishes that a specific mapping from a quotient of a family of modules to another family preserves structure by demonstrating that the inverse function of this mapping is a left inverse of the original function.
explanatories.Submodule.quotientPi_aux.right_inv: This theorem establishes that a certain mapping from the quotient of a family of modules to individual quotient modules has a right inverse, confirming a specific relationship between the two constructions.

submodule.quotient_pi.fullDefinition: def quotientPi [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (p : ∀ i, Submodule R (Ms i)) :     ((∀ i, Ms i) ⧸ pi Set.univ p) ≃ₗ[R] ∀ i, Ms i ⧸ p i where   toFun := toFun p   invFun := invFun p   map_add' := map_add p   map_smul' := quotientPi_aux.map_smul p   left_inv := left_inv p   right_inv := right_inv p
submodule.quotient_pi.description: This definition asserts that there is an isomorphism between the quotient of a direct sum of modules and the direct sum of their respective quotients by corresponding submodules.

PiTensorProduct.tprodCoeff.comment:
`tprodCoeff R r f` with `r : R` and `f : Π i, s i` is the tensor product of the vectors `f i`
over all `i : ι`, multiplied by the coefficient `r`. Note that this is meant as an auxiliary
definition for this file alone, and that one should use `tprod` defined below for most purposes.

explanatories.FreeAddMonoid.of: This definition embeds an element from a set into a free additive monoid as a singleton list.

PiTensorProduct.liftAddHom.{u_1, u_4, u_7, u_10} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_4} [CommSemiring R] {s : ι → Type u_7}
  [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (s i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (s i)] {F : Type u_10} [AddCommMonoid F]
  (φ : R × ((i : ι) → s i) → F) (C0 : ∀ (r : R) (f : (i : ι) → s i) (i : ι), f i = 0 → φ (r, f) = 0)
  (C0' : ∀ (f : (i : ι) → s i), φ (0, f) = 0)
  (C_add :
    ∀ [inst : DecidableEq ι] (r : R) (f : (i : ι) → s i) (i : ι) (m₁ m₂ : s i),
      φ (r, update f i m₁) + φ (r, update f i m₂) = φ (r, update f i (m₁ + m₂)))
  (C_add_scalar : ∀ (r r' : R) (f : (i : ι) → s i), φ (r, f) + φ (r', f) = φ (r + r', f))
  (C_smul :
    ∀ [inst : DecidableEq ι] (r : R) (f : (i : ι) → s i) (i : ι) (r' : R),
      φ (r, update f i (r' • f i)) = φ (r' * r, f)) :
  (⨂[R] (i : ι), s i) →+ F

explanatories.PiTensorProduct.Eqv.of_add: This theorem demonstrates that the tensor product of a family of modules with a common scalar, when adding two updated elements at the same index, is equivalent to updating the resulting element of that scalar with the sum of those two elements.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.Eqv.of_add_scalar: This theorem demonstrates that adding two scalar multiples of a family of modules within a free additive monoid is equivalent to combining their scalar coefficients into a single scalar multiple of the same family.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.Eqv.of_smul: This theorem shows that replacing an element in a family of modules with a scaled version affects the tensor product equivalently to adjusting the scalar associated with that family.
explanatories.AddCon.lift: This definition describes a homomorphism from the quotient of an additive monoid by a specified additive congruence relation to another additive structure, which is defined under the condition that the homomorphism is constant on the equivalence classes of the congruence relation.
explanatories.FreeAddMonoid.lift: This definition establishes an equivalence between functions from a type to an additive monoid and additive monoid homomorphisms from the free additive monoid generated by that type to the additive monoid.
explanatories.AddCon.addConGen_le: This theorem asserts that the smallest additive congruence relation generated by a given binary relation is a subset of any additive congruence relation that includes that binary relation.
explanatories.AddCon.ker_rel: This theorem characterizes the additive congruence relation induced by the kernel of an additive monoid homomorphism, stating that two elements are congruent if and only if they are mapped to the same element in the codomain.
explanatories.FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of: This theorem demonstrates that applying the lift of a function to the free additive monoid generated by an element yields the function's value at that element.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.map_add: This theorem asserts that an additive monoid homomorphism preserves the addition operation, meaning the image of the sum of two elements is equal to the sum of their images.
explanatories.add_comm: This theorem asserts that the addition operation in a commutative magma is commutative, meaning the sum of two elements does not depend on the order in which they are added.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a multilinear map preserves addition when one of its inputs is updated with the sum of two elements.

explanatories.LinearEquiv.map_add: This theorem states that a linear equivalence preserves the addition of elements from one module when mapped to another module.

PiTensorProduct.liftAddHom.fullDefinition: def liftAddHom (φ : (R × Π i, s i) → F)     (C0 : ∀ (r : R) (f : Π i, s i) (i : ι) (_ : f i = 0), φ (r, f) = 0)     (C0' : ∀ f : Π i, s i, φ (0, f) = 0)     (C_add : ∀ [DecidableEq ι] (r : R) (f : Π i, s i) (i : ι) (m₁ m₂ : s i),       φ (r, update f i m₁) + φ (r, update f i m₂) = φ (r, update f i (m₁ + m₂)))     (C_add_scalar : ∀ (r r' : R) (f : Π i, s i), φ (r, f) + φ (r', f) = φ (r + r', f))     (C_smul : ∀ [DecidableEq ι] (r : R) (f : Π i, s i) (i : ι) (r' : R),       φ (r, update f i (r' • f i)) = φ (r' * r, f)) :     (⨂[R] i, s i) →+ F :=   (addConGen (PiTensorProduct.Eqv R s)).lift (FreeAddMonoid.lift φ) <|     AddCon.addConGen_le fun x y hxy ↦       match hxy with       | Eqv.of_zero r' f i hf =>         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp [FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, C0 r' f i hf]       | Eqv.of_zero_scalar f =>         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp [FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, C0']       | Eqv.of_add inst z f i m₁ m₂ =>         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp [FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, @C_add inst]       | Eqv.of_add_scalar z₁ z₂ f =>         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp [FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, C_add_scalar]       | Eqv.of_smul inst z f i r' =>         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp [FreeAddMonoid.lift_eval_of, @C_smul inst]       | Eqv.add_comm x y =>         (AddCon.ker_rel _).2 <| by simp_rw [AddMonoidHom.map_add, add_comm]
PiTensorProduct.liftAddHom.description: This definition constructs an additive homomorphism from the tensor product of a family of modules over a commutative semiring to another additive monoid by specifying a mapping function that satisfies certain linearity and zero conditions.

PiTensorProduct.liftAddHom.{u_1, u_4, u_7, u_10} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_4} [CommSemiring R] {s : ι → Type u_7}
  [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (s i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (s i)] {F : Type u_10} [AddCommMonoid F]
  (φ : R × ((i : ι) → s i) → F) (C0 : ∀ (r : R) (f : (i : ι) → s i) (i : ι), f i = 0 → φ (r, f) = 0)
  (C0' : ∀ (f : (i : ι) → s i), φ (0, f) = 0)
  (C_add :
    ∀ [inst : DecidableEq ι] (r : R) (f : (i : ι) → s i) (i : ι) (m₁ m₂ : s i),
      φ (r, update f i m₁) + φ (r, update f i m₂) = φ (r, update f i (m₁ + m₂)))
  (C_add_scalar : ∀ (r r' : R) (f : (i : ι) → s i), φ (r, f) + φ (r', f) = φ (r + r', f))
  (C_smul :
    ∀ [inst : DecidableEq ι] (r : R) (f : (i : ι) → s i) (i : ι) (r' : R),
      φ (r, update f i (r' • f i)) = φ (r' * r, f)) :
  (⨂[R] (i : ι), s i) →+ F

explanatories.PiTensorProduct.tprodCoeff: This definition outlines a method for constructing the tensor product of a collection of vectors scaled by a coefficient from a commutative semiring, facilitating specific operations within that context.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.zero_tprodCoeff: This theorem demonstrates that the tensor product coefficient of a family of modules with respect to a zero scalar is equal to zero.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.zero_tprodCoeff': This theorem asserts that the tensor product coefficient of a family of modules with respect to a scalar vanishes if one of the vectors in the family is zero.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.add_tprodCoeff: This theorem demonstrates that the tensor product coefficient of a family of modules is additive when the entries of the family are updated at a specific index with two different elements added together.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.add_tprodCoeff': This theorem states that the tensor product coefficient for a family of modules with respect to two scalars is equal to the sum of the tensor product coefficients for each scalar separately.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.smul_tprodCoeff: This theorem states that scaling an element in a collection of modules followed by an update maintains the equivalence of the tensor product coefficient, appropriately modified by the scaling factor applied to the original coefficient.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.liftAddHom: This definition constructs an additive homomorphism from the tensor product of a family of modules over a commutative semiring to another additive monoid by specifying a mapping function that satisfies certain linearity and zero conditions.
explanatories.mul_add: This theorem states that in a structure where multiplication is left distributive over addition, the product of an element and the sum of two other elements equals the sum of the products of the first element with each of the other two elements.
explanatories.mul_smul_comm: This theorem demonstrates that in the presence of a commutativity condition for scalar multiplication, the operation of multiplying an element by a scalar and then scaling another element is equivalent to first scaling the second element and then multiplying the two results.

PiTensorProduct.hasSMul'.fullDefinition: instance hasSMul' : SMul R₁ (⨂[R] i, s i) :=   ⟨fun r ↦     liftAddHom (fun f : R × Π i, s i ↦ tprodCoeff R (r • f.1) f.2)       (fun r' f i hf ↦ by simp_rw [zero_tprodCoeff' _ f i hf])       (fun f ↦ by simp [zero_tprodCoeff]) (fun r' f i m₁ m₂ ↦ by simp [add_tprodCoeff])       (fun r' r'' f ↦ by simp [add_tprodCoeff', mul_add]) fun z f i r' ↦ by       simp [smul_tprodCoeff, mul_smul_comm]⟩

PiTensorProduct.map.comment:
Let `sᵢ` and `tᵢ` be two families of `R`-modules.
Let `f` be a family of `R`-linear maps between `sᵢ` and `tᵢ`, i.e. `f : Πᵢ sᵢ → tᵢ`,
then there is an induced map `⨂ᵢ sᵢ → ⨂ᵢ tᵢ` by `⨂ aᵢ ↦ ⨂ fᵢ aᵢ`.

This is `TensorProduct.map` for an arbitrary family of modules.

PiTensorProduct.piTensorHomMap.comment:
Let `sᵢ` and `tᵢ` be families of `R`-modules.
Then there is an `R`-linear map between `⨂ᵢ Hom(sᵢ, tᵢ)` and `Hom(⨂ᵢ sᵢ, ⨂ tᵢ)` defined by
`⨂ᵢ fᵢ ↦ ⨂ᵢ aᵢ ↦ ⨂ᵢ fᵢ aᵢ`.

This is `TensorProduct.homTensorHomMap` for an arbitrary family of modules.

Note that `PiTensorProduct.piTensorHomMap (tprod R f)` is equal to `PiTensorProduct.map f`.

explanatories.AddCon.lift: This definition describes a homomorphism from the quotient of an additive monoid by a specified additive congruence relation to another additive structure, which is defined under the condition that the homomorphism is constant on the equivalence classes of the congruence relation.
explanatories.FreeAddMonoid.lift: This definition establishes an equivalence between functions from a type to an additive monoid and additive monoid homomorphisms from the free additive monoid generated by that type to the additive monoid.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.tprod: This definition introduces a multilinear map that constructs the tensor product of a family of modules over a commutative semiring.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.lift: This definition establishes a linear isomorphism between multilinear maps from a family of modules to an additive commutative monoid and linear maps from the tensor product of those modules to the monoid.
explanatories.PiTensorProduct.lift.tprod: This theorem establishes that the lift of a multilinear map applied to the tensor product of a collection of modules equals the application of the multilinear map to the collection itself.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.toLinearMap: This definition constructs a linear map from one module to another using a linear equivalence that relates the two modules through compatible ring homomorphisms.
explanatories.TensorProduct.lift: This definition describes a method to construct a linear map from the tensor product of two modules to a third module, based on a given bilinear map.

PiTensorProduct.piTensorHomMap.fullDefinition: def piTensorHomMap : (⨂[R] i, s i →ₗ[R] t i) →ₗ[R] (⨂[R] i, s i) →ₗ[R] ⨂[R] i, t i :=   lift.toLinearMap ∘ₗ lift (MultilinearMap.piLinearMap <| tprod R)
PiTensorProduct.piTensorHomMap.description: This definition establishes an R-linear map that relates the tensor product of a family of homomorphisms between two families of modules to the homomorphism from the tensor product of the first family to the tensor product of the second family.

PiTensorProduct.congr.comment:

explanatories.MultilinearMap.ext: This theorem establishes that if two multilinear maps produce the same output for all inputs, then they are equal as maps.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ofLinear: This definition states that a pair of linear maps that are inverses of each other form a linear equivalence between two modules over different semirings.
explanatories.TensorProduct.ext: This theorem establishes that if two linear maps from the tensor product of two modules to a third module are equal when restricted through a specific construction, then the linear maps themselves must be identical.

PiTensorProduct.map₂.comment:

LinearMap.quotKerEquivRange.comment:
The **first isomorphism law for modules**. The quotient of `M` by the kernel of `f` is linearly
equivalent to the range of `f`.

explanatories.LinearMap.ker: The kernel of a linear map is defined as the set of elements in the domain that are mapped to zero in the codomain, and it forms a submodule of the domain.
explanatories.LinearMap.range: This definition states that the range of a linear map between modules is a submodule of the codomain module.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ofInjective: This definition establishes that an injective linear map creates a linear equivalence between its domain and its image.
explanatories.Submodule.liftQ: This definition describes a linear map from the quotient of a module by a submodule to another module, induced by a linear transformation that vanishes on the submodule.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.LinearMap.ker_eq_bot: The kernel of a linear map is trivial if and only if the map is injective.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Submodule.ker_liftQ_eq_bot: This theorem establishes that when two submodules are equivalent to the kernel of a linear transformation, the kernel of the lifted transformation is trivial.
explanatories.le_refl: This theorem confirms that in a preorder, any element is related to itself under the less than or equal relation.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.trans: This definition establishes that if there are two linear equivalences between three modules with corresponding ring homomorphisms, then there exists a direct linear equivalence between the first and last modules.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ofEq: This definition establishes a linear equivalence between two submodules when they are equal.
explanatories.Submodule.range_liftQ: This theorem demonstrates that if a linear map maps a module to another while the submodule is contained in the kernel of that map, then the range of the quotient of the submodule by the map is equivalent to the range of the original linear map.
explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.

LinearMap.quotKerEquivRange.fullDefinition: noncomputable def quotKerEquivRange : (M ⧸ LinearMap.ker f) ≃ₗ[R] LinearMap.range f :=   (LinearEquiv.ofInjective (f.ker.liftQ f <| le_rfl) <|         ker_eq_bot.mp <| Submodule.ker_liftQ_eq_bot _ _ _ (le_refl (LinearMap.ker f))).trans     (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ <| Submodule.range_liftQ _ _ _)
LinearMap.quotKerEquivRange.description: This definition expresses that the quotient of a module by the kernel of a linear map is isomorphic to the image of that map.

equivalence between linear maps `M₁ →ₗ M₁` and square matrices over `R` indexed by the basis.

explanatories.LinearMap.toMatrix_mul: This theorem asserts that the matrix representation of the product of two linear maps is equivalent to the product of their respective matrix representations.

A linear equivalence of two modules induces an equivalence of algebras of their

explanatories.RingHom.id: This definition describes the identity ring homomorphism that maps each element of a semiring to itself.
explanatories.LinearMap.id: This definition specifies the identity linear map for a module over a semiring that maps each element to itself.

explanatories.LinearEquiv.arrowCongr_comp: This theorem asserts that the composition of linear maps between modules commutes with the arrow-congruent mappings induced by linear equivalences.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear equivalence preserves scalar multiplication when applied to elements of two modules over the same semiring.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.conj: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the spaces of linear maps from one module to itself and another module to itself when the two modules are linearly isomorphic.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.conj_id: This theorem states that the conjugation of the identity linear map by a linear equivalence is itself the identity linear map.

LinearEquiv.algConj.description: This definition establishes that a linear equivalence between two modules creates an algebraic equivalence between the algebras of their endomorphisms.
