Basis.linearMap.comment:
The standard basis of the space linear maps between two modules
induced by a basis of the domain and codomain.

If `M₁` and `M₂` are modules with basis `b₁` and `b₂` respectively indexed
by finite types `ι₁` and `ι₂`,
then `Basis.linearMap b₁ b₂` is the basis of `M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂` indexed by `ι₂ × ι₁`
where `(i, j)` indexes the linear map that sends `b j` to `b i`
and sends all other basis vectors to `0`.

explanatories.LinearMap.stdBasis: This definition describes a linear map that represents the standard basis element of a product type associated with a given index in a family of modules.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm: This definition specifies the symmetry of linear equivalences, indicating that the inverse relationship between two modules can be expressed as a linear equivalence in the opposite direction.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.symm: This definition indicates that every algebra equivalence has a corresponding inverse that switches the roles of the two algebras involved.
explanatories.LinearMap.toMatrix: This definition specifies a linear equivalence between linear maps from one module to another and matrices formed over a commutative ring, given specific bases for the modules.
explanatories.Matrix.stdBasis: This definition specifies the standard basis of matrices as a basis for the space of all matrices with dimensions corresponding to specified finite types.
explanatories.Basis.map: This definition introduces a new basis for a module formed by applying a given linear equivalence to the original basis vectors.

Basis.linearMap.fullDefinition: def linearMap (b₁ : Basis ι₁ R M₁) (b₂ : Basis ι₂ R M₂) :     Basis (ι₂ × ι₁) R (M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂) :=   (Matrix.stdBasis R ι₂ ι₁).map (LinearMap.toMatrix b₁ b₂).symm
Basis.linearMap.description: This definition describes the basis of the space of linear maps between two modules, constructed from the bases of the domain and codomain.

  {ι₂ : Type u_7} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M₁] [AddCommMonoid M₂] [Module R M₁] [Module R M₂] [Fintype ι₁]
  [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₁] (b₁ : Basis ι₁ R M₁) (b₂ : Basis ι₂ R M₂) :
  ∀ (a : ι₂ × ι₁ →₀ R),
    (b₁.linearMap b₂).repr.symm a =

  {ι₂ : Type u_7} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M₁] [AddCommMonoid M₂] [Module R M₁] [Module R M₂] [Fintype ι₁]

Basis.linearMap_apply_apply.{u_1, u_3, u_4, u_6, u_7} {R : Type u_1} {M₁ : Type u_3} {M₂ : Type u_4} {ι₁ : Type u_6}
  {ι₂ : Type u_7} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M₁] [AddCommMonoid M₂] [Module R M₁] [Module R M₂] [Fintype ι₁]

Matrix.transvection.code: Matrix.transvection.{u₂, u_1} {n : Type u_1} {R : Type u₂} [DecidableEq n] [CommRing R] (i j : n) (c : R) : Matrix n n R
Matrix.transvection.comment:
The transvection matrix `transvection i j c` is equal to the identity plus `c` at position
`(i, j)`. Multiplying by it on the left (as in `transvection i j c * M`) corresponds to adding
`c` times the `j`-th row of `M` to its `i`-th row. Multiplying by it on the right corresponds
to adding `c` times the `i`-th column to the `j`-th column.

explanatories.Matrix.stdBasisMatrix: The standard basis matrix for given row and column indices contains a specified value at that position and zeroes everywhere else.

Matrix.Pivot.exists_list_transvec_mul_mul_list_transvec_eq_diagonal_induction.{u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_3} [Field 𝕜] {r : ℕ}
  (IH :
    ∀ (M : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) 𝕜),
      ∃ L₀ L₀' D₀, (List.map toMatrix L₀).prod * M * (List.map toMatrix L₀').prod = diagonal D₀)
  (M : Matrix (Fin r ⊕ Unit) (Fin r ⊕ Unit) 𝕜) :
  ∃ L L' D, (List.map toMatrix L).prod * M * (List.map toMatrix L').prod = diagonal D
Matrix.Pivot.exists_list_transvec_mul_mu.comment:
Inductive step for the reduction: if one knows that any size `r` matrix can be reduced to
diagonal form by elementary operations, then one deduces it for matrices over `Fin r ⊕ Unit`.

Matrix.diagonal_transvection_induction.{u_1, u_3} {n : Type u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_3} [Field 𝕜] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n]
  (P : Matrix n n 𝕜 → Prop) (M : Matrix n n 𝕜) (hdiag : ∀ (D : n → 𝕜), (diagonal D).det = M.det → P (diagonal D))
  (htransvec : ∀ (t : TransvectionStruct n 𝕜), P t.toMatrix) (hmul : ∀ (A B : Matrix n n 𝕜), P A → P B → P (A * B)) :
  P M
Matrix.diagonal_transvection_induction.comment:
Induction principle for matrices based on transvections: if a property is true for all diagonal
matrices, all transvections, and is stable under product, then it is true for all matrices. This is
the useful way to say that matrices are generated by diagonal matrices and transvections.

We state a slightly more general version: to prove a property for a matrix `M`, it suffices to
assume that the diagonal matrices we consider have the same determinant as `M`. This is useful to
obtain similar principles for `SLₙ` or `GLₙ`.

  (b : n → α) (i : n) : α
Matrix.cramerMap.comment:
`cramerMap A b i` is the determinant of the matrix `A` with column `i` replaced with `b`,
and thus `cramerMap A b` is the vector output by Cramer's rule on `A` and `b`.

If `A * x = b` has a unique solution in `x`, `cramerMap A` sends the vector `b` to `A.det • x`.
Otherwise, the outcome of `cramerMap` is well-defined but not necessarily useful.

If `A * x = b` has a unique solution in `x`, `cramer A` sends the vector `b` to `A.det • x`.
Otherwise, the outcome of `cramer` is well-defined but not necessarily useful.

The adjugate matrix is the transpose of the cofactor matrix.

Typically, the cofactor matrix is defined by taking minors,
i.e. the determinant of the matrix with a row and column removed.
However, the proof of `mul_adjugate` becomes a lot easier if we use the
matrix replacing a column with a basis vector, since it allows us to use
facts about the `cramer` map.

Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.term↑ₘ_._@..la.comment:
In this file, Lean often has a hard time working out the values of `n` and `R` for an expression
like `det ↑A`. Rather than writing `(A : Matrix n n R)` everywhere in this file which is annoyingly
verbose, or `A.val` which is not the simp-normal form for subtypes, we create a local notation
`↑ₘA`. This notation references the local `n` and `R` variables, so is not valid as a global
notation.

Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.center_equiv_r.fullDefinition: def center_equiv_rootsOfUnity' (i : n) :     center (SpecialLinearGroup n R) ≃* rootsOfUnity (Fintype.card n).toPNat' R where   toFun A := rootsOfUnity.mkOfPowEq (↑ₘA i i) <| by     have : Nonempty n := ⟨i⟩     obtain ⟨r, hr, hr'⟩ := mem_center_iff.mp A.property     replace hr' : A.val i i = r := by simp [← hr']     simp [hr, hr']   invFun a := ⟨⟨a • (1 : Matrix n n R), by aesop⟩,     Subgroup.mem_center_iff.mpr fun B ↦ Subtype.val_injective <| by simp [coe_mul]⟩   left_inv A := by     refine SetCoe.ext <| SetCoe.ext ?_     obtain ⟨r, _, hr⟩ := mem_center_iff.mp A.property     simpa [← hr, Submonoid.smul_def, Units.smul_def] using smul_one_eq_diagonal r   right_inv a := by     obtain ⟨⟨a, _⟩, ha⟩ := a     exact SetCoe.ext <| Units.eq_iff.mp <| by simp   map_mul' A B := by     dsimp     ext     simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, coe_mul, rootsOfUnity.val_mkOfPowEq_coe, Units.val_mul]     rw [← scalar_eq_coe_self_center A i, ← scalar_eq_coe_self_center B i]     simp

ModularGroup.S.comment:
The matrix `S = [[0, -1], [1, 0]]` as an element of `SL(2, ℤ)`.

This element acts naturally on the Euclidean plane as a rotation about the origin by `π / 2`.

This element also acts naturally on the hyperbolic plane as rotation about `i` by `π`. It
represents the Mobiüs transformation `z ↦ -1/z` and is an involutive elliptic isometry.

explanatories.smul_mul_assoc: This theorem states that when a scalar multiplication and multiplication structure satisfy a certain scalar tower condition, scaling one factor in a product does not affect the result of the product itself.
explanatories.Matrix.adjugate_mul: This theorem states that the product of a matrix and its adjugate equals the determinant of the matrix multiplied by the identity matrix.
explanatories.smul_smul: This theorem shows that the action of the product of two elements from a monoid on another element is the same as performing the actions sequentially and is associative.
explanatories.invOf_mul_self: This theorem states that the product of the inverse of an invertible element and the element itself equals the identity in a multiplicative structure.
explanatories.one_smul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by the identity element of a monoid does not change the element itself.
explanatories.mul_smul_comm: This theorem demonstrates that in the presence of a commutativity condition for scalar multiplication, the operation of multiplying an element by a scalar and then scaling another element is equivalent to first scaling the second element and then multiplying the two results.
explanatories.Matrix.mul_adjugate: This theorem shows that multiplying a matrix by its adjugate results in a scalar multiple of the identity matrix, where the scalar is the determinant of the matrix.
explanatories.mul_invOf_self: This theorem asserts that an invertible element, when multiplied by its inverse, equals the identity element in a multiplicative structure.

Matrix.equiv_GL_linearindependent.fullDefinition: noncomputable def equiv_GL_linearindependent (hn : 0 < n) :     GL (Fin n) 𝔽 ≃ { s : Fin n → Fin n → 𝔽 // LinearIndependent 𝔽 s } where   toFun M := ⟨transpose M, by     apply linearIndependent_iff_card_eq_finrank_span.2     rw [Set.finrank, ← rank_eq_finrank_span_cols, rank_unit]⟩   invFun M := GeneralLinearGroup.mk'' (transpose (M.1)) <| by     have : Nonempty (Fin n) := Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.1 hn     rw [← Basis.coePiBasisFun.toMatrix_eq_transpose,       ← coe_basisOfLinearIndependentOfCardEqFinrank M.2]     let b := basisOfLinearIndependentOfCardEqFinrank M.2 (by simp)     have := (Pi.basisFun 𝔽 (Fin n)).invertibleToMatrix b     exact isUnit_det_of_invertible _   left_inv := fun x ↦ Units.ext (ext fun i j ↦ rfl)   right_inv := by exact congrFun rfl
Matrix.equiv_GL_linearindependent.description: This establishes a correspondence between invertible matrices over a field and sets of linearly independent vectors of the same dimension, where the mapping takes a matrix to its columns.

card_linearIndependent.code:
card_linearIndependent.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [DivisionRing K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
  [Fintype K] [Fintype V] {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ FiniteDimensional.finrank K V) :

    ∏ i : Fin k, (Fintype.card K ^ FiniteDimensional.finrank K V - Fintype.card K ^ ↑i)
card_linearIndependent.comment:
The cardinal of the set of linearly independent vectors over a finite dimensional vector space
over a finite field.

`BlockTriangular M n b` says the matrix is block triangular.

explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.

matrix.to_linear_equiv'_symm_apply.description: The inverse of the linear equivalence associated with an invertible matrix corresponds to the linear transformation defined by the matrix's inverse.

Matrix.toLinearEquiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {R : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [CommRing R]
  [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (b : Basis n R M) [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n R) (hA : IsUnit A.det) : M ≃ₗ[R] M
Matrix.toLinearEquiv.comment:
Given `hA : IsUnit A.det` and `b : Basis R b`, `A.toLinearEquiv b hA` is
the `LinearEquiv` arising from `toLin b b A`.

See `Matrix.toLinearEquiv'` for this result on `n → R`.

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.IsUnit: An element in a monoid is defined as a unit if there exists another element in the monoid that serves as its two-sided inverse.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp_apply: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of two linear maps applied to an element yields the same result as applying each map sequentially to that element.
explanatories.Matrix.toLin_mul: This theorem demonstrates that applying a linear transformation associated with a product of matrices results in a composition of linear transformations derived from individual matrices and specified bases.
explanatories.Matrix.nonsing_inv_mul: This theorem proves that if the determinant of a matrix is a unit, then the nonsingular inverse of that matrix acts as a left inverse, satisfying the equation of the inverse multiplied by the original matrix equaling the identity.
explanatories.Matrix.toLin_one: This theorem asserts that the linear transformation represented by a matrix corresponding to a basis applied to the scalar one is equivalent to the identity linear map.
explanatories.LinearMap.id_apply: This theorem demonstrates that the identity function applied to an element of a module returns that element unchanged.
explanatories.Matrix.mul_nonsing_inv: This theorem states that if a matrix has a unit determinant, then the product of the matrix and its right inverse equals the identity matrix.
explanatories.Function.comp_apply: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.

Matrix.toLinearEquiv.fullDefinition: noncomputable def toLinearEquiv [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n R) (hA : IsUnit A.det) :     M ≃ₗ[R] M where   __ := toLin b b A   toFun := toLin b b A   invFun := toLin b b A⁻¹   left_inv x := by     simp_rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, ← Matrix.toLin_mul b b b, Matrix.nonsing_inv_mul _ hA,       toLin_one, LinearMap.id_apply]   right_inv x := by     simp_rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply, ← Matrix.toLin_mul b b b, Matrix.mul_nonsing_inv _ hA,       toLin_one, LinearMap.id_apply]
Matrix.toLinearEquiv.description: A matrix with a unit determinant induces a linear equivalence between a free module and itself when paired with a specified basis.

eigenvalue_mem_ball.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [NormedField K] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n K} {μ : K} (hμ : Module.End.HasEigenvalue (Matrix.toLin' A) μ) :
  ∃ k, μ ∈ Metric.closedBall (A k k) (∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase k, ‖A k j‖)
eigenvalue_mem_ball.comment:
**Gershgorin's circle theorem**: for any eigenvalue `μ` of a square matrix `A`, there exists an
index `k` such that `μ` lies in the closed ball of center the diagonal term `A k k` and of
radius the sum of the norms `∑ j ≠ k, ‖A k j‖.

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.Matrix: A matrix is defined as a data structure with entries from a specified type, organized in rows indexed by one type and columns indexed by another type.
explanatories.Module.End.HasEigenvalue: This definition specifies that a scalar is considered an eigenvalue for a linear map if there exist nonzero vectors that are scaled by that scalar when the map is applied to them.
explanatories.Matrix.toLin': This definition establishes a linear equivalence between a matrix and a specific linear map that transforms functions from one vector space to another.
explanatories.Metric.closedBall: The closed ball around a point in a pseudo-metric space consists of all points whose distance from that point is less than or equal to a specified radius.
explanatories.Finset.erase: This definition specifies a function that creates a new finite set containing all elements from the original set except for a specified element.

eigenvalue_mem_ball.description: This theorem states that if a square matrix has an eigenvalue, then there exists an index such that the eigenvalue is contained within a specific closed ball defined by the diagonal entry and the sum of the norms of the off-diagonal entries in that row.

Matrix.charpoly.univ.comment:
The universal characteristic polynomial for `n × n`-matrices,
is the charactistic polynomial of `Matrix.mvPolynomialX n n ℤ` with entries `Xᵢⱼ`.

Its `i`-th coefficient is a homogeneous polynomial of degree `n - i`,
see `Matrix.charpoly.univ_coeff_isHomogeneous`.

By evaluating the coefficients at the entries of a matrix `M`,
one obtains the characteristic polynomial of `M`,
see `Matrix.charpoly.univ_map_eval₂Hom`.

LinearMap.exists_monic_and_coeff_mem_pow_and_aeval_eq_zero_of_range_le_smul.{u_2, u_3} {M : Type u_2} [AddCommGroup M]
  (R : Type u_3) [CommRing R] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] (f : Module.End R M) (I : Ideal R)
  (hI : LinearMap.range f ≤ I • ⊤) : ∃ p, p.Monic ∧ (∀ (k : ℕ), p.coeff k ∈ I ^ (p.natDegree - k)) ∧ (aeval f) p = 0
LinearMap.exists_monic_and_coeff_mem_pow.comment:
The **Cayley-Hamilton Theorem** for f.g. modules over arbitrary rings states that for each
`R`-endomorphism `φ` of an `R`-module `M` such that `φ(M) ≤ I • M` for some ideal `I`, there
exists some `n` and some `aᵢ ∈ Iⁱ` such that `φⁿ + a₁ φⁿ⁻¹ + ⋯ + aₙ = 0`.

This is the version found in Eisenbud 4.3, which is slightly weaker than Matsumura 2.1
(this lacks the constraint on `n`), and is slightly stronger than Atiyah-Macdonald 2.4.

linear_map.exists_monic_and_coeff_mem_po.comment:
The **Cayley-Hamilton Theorem** for f.g. modules over arbitrary rings states that for each
`R`-endomorphism `φ` of an `R`-module `M` such that `φ(M) ≤ I • M` for some ideal `I`, there
exists some `n` and some `aᵢ ∈ Iⁱ` such that `φⁿ + a₁ φⁿ⁻¹ + ⋯ + aₙ = 0`.

This is the version found in Eisenbud 4.3, which is slightly weaker than Matsumura 2.1
(this lacks the constraint on `n`), and is slightly stronger than Atiyah-Macdonald 2.4.

charpoly_leftMulMatrix.comment:
The characteristic polynomial of the map `fun x => a * x` is the minimal polynomial of `a`.

In combination with `det_eq_sign_charpoly_coeff` or `trace_eq_neg_charpoly_coeff`

field norm resp. trace of `x` is the product resp. sum of `x`'s conjugates.

Matrix.IsHermitian.code: Matrix.IsHermitian.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {n : Type u_4} [Star α] (A : Matrix n n α) : Prop
Matrix.IsHermitian.comment:
A matrix is hermitian if it is equal to its conjugate transpose. On the reals, this definition
captures symmetric matrices.
Matrix.IsHermitian.fullDefinition: def IsHermitian (A : Matrix n n α) : Prop := Aᴴ = A
Matrix.IsHermitian.description: A matrix is considered hermitian if it is equal to its conjugate transpose, which coincides with the concept of symmetric matrices when the entries are real numbers.

Matrix.NormedAddCommGroup.ofMatrix.fullDefinition: noncomputable abbrev NormedAddCommGroup.ofMatrix {M : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hM : M.PosDef) :     NormedAddCommGroup (n → 𝕜) :=   @InnerProductSpace.Core.toNormedAddCommGroup _ _ _ _ _     { inner := fun x y => dotProduct (star x) (M *ᵥ y)       conj_symm := fun x y => by         dsimp only [Inner.inner]         rw [star_dotProduct, starRingEnd_apply, star_star, star_mulVec, dotProduct_mulVec,           hM.isHermitian.eq]       nonneg_re := fun x => by         by_cases h : x = 0         · simp [h]         · exact le_of_lt (hM.re_dotProduct_pos h)       definite := fun x (hx : dotProduct _ _ = 0) => by         by_contra! h         simpa [hx, lt_irrefl] using hM.re_dotProduct_pos h       add_left := by simp only [star_add, add_dotProduct, eq_self_iff_true, forall_const]       smul_left := fun x y r => by         simp only         rw [← smul_eq_mul, ← smul_dotProduct, starRingEnd_apply, ← star_smul] }

  [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] [Fintype n] {A : Matrix m m 𝕜} (B : Matrix m n 𝕜) (D : Matrix n n 𝕜) (x : m → 𝕜)
  (y : n → 𝕜) [Invertible A] (hA : A.IsHermitian) :
  star (x ⊕ᵥ y) ᵥ* fromBlocks A B Bᴴ D ⬝ᵥ (x ⊕ᵥ y) =
    star (x + (A⁻¹ * B) *ᵥ y) ᵥ* A ⬝ᵥ (x + (A⁻¹ * B) *ᵥ y) + star y ᵥ* (D - Bᴴ * A⁻¹ * B) ⬝ᵥ y

LDL.lowerInv.code:
LDL.lowerInv.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {n : Type u_2} [LinearOrder n] [IsWellOrder n fun x x_1 => x < x_1]
  [LocallyFiniteOrderBot n] {S : Matrix n n 𝕜} [Fintype n] (hS : S.PosDef) : Matrix n n 𝕜
LDL.lowerInv.comment:
The inverse of the lower triangular matrix `L` of the LDL-decomposition. It is obtained by
applying Gram-Schmidt-Orthogonalization w.r.t. the inner product induced by `Sᵀ` on the standard
basis vectors `Pi.basisFun`.

explanatories.Matrix: A matrix is defined as a data structure with entries from a specified type, organized in rows indexed by one type and columns indexed by another type.
explanatories.Matrix.InnerProductSpace.ofMatrix: A positive definite matrix defines an inner product space by inducing a specific inner product form involving the matrix and vectors.
explanatories.Matrix.PosDef.transpose: The transpose of a positive definite matrix is also positive definite.
explanatories.Pi.basisFun: This definition describes a basis for the vector space of functions from a finite set to the reals, where each basis vector corresponds to a function that assigns 1 to a specific element and 0 to all others.
explanatories.Matrix.NormedAddCommGroup.ofMatrix: A positive definite matrix induces a normed additive commutative group structure on the vector space of sequences of its column vectors.

LDL.lowerInv.fullDefinition: noncomputable def LDL.lowerInv : Matrix n n 𝕜 :=   @gramSchmidt 𝕜 (n → 𝕜) _ (_ : _) (InnerProductSpace.ofMatrix hS.transpose) n _ _ _     (Pi.basisFun 𝕜 n)
LDL.lowerInv.description: This definition describes a construction for the inverse of the lower triangular matrix from the LDL decomposition, utilizing a specific orthogonalization method based on a given positive definite matrix.

Matrix.IsHermitian.cfcAux.fullDefinition: noncomputable def cfcAux : C(spectrum ℝ A, ℝ) →⋆ₐ[ℝ] (Matrix n n 𝕜) where   toFun := fun g => (eigenvectorUnitary hA : Matrix n n 𝕜) *     diagonal (RCLike.ofReal ∘ g ∘ (fun i ↦ ⟨hA.eigenvalues i, hA.eigenvalues_mem_spectrum_real i⟩))     * star (eigenvectorUnitary hA : Matrix n n 𝕜)   map_one' := by simp [Pi.one_def (f := fun _ : n ↦ 𝕜)]   map_mul' f g := by     have {a b c d e f : Matrix n n 𝕜} : (a * b * c) * (d * e * f) = a * (b * (c * d) * e) * f := by       simp only [mul_assoc]     simp only [this, ContinuousMap.coe_mul, SetLike.coe_mem, unitary.star_mul_self_of_mem, mul_one,       diagonal_mul_diagonal, Function.comp_apply]     congr! with i     simp   map_zero' := by simp [Pi.zero_def (f := fun _ : n ↦ 𝕜)]   map_add' f g := by     simp only [ContinuousMap.coe_add, ← add_mul, ← mul_add, diagonal_add, Function.comp_apply]     congr! with i     simp   commutes' r := by     simp only [Function.comp, algebraMap_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]     rw [← mul_one (algebraMap _ _ _), ← unitary.coe_mul_star_self hA.eigenvectorUnitary,       ← Algebra.left_comm, unitary.coe_star, mul_assoc]     congr!   map_star' f := by     simp only [star_trivial, StarMul.star_mul, star_star, star_eq_conjTranspose (diagonal _),       diagonal_conjTranspose, mul_assoc]     congr!     ext     simp
Matrix.IsHermitian.cfcAux.description: This definition introduces an auxiliary structure that represents a star algebra homomorphism related to the continuous functional calculus for Hermitian matrices.

Matrix.IsHermitian.cfcAux_apply.code:
Matrix.IsHermitian.cfcAux_apply.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (g : C(↑(spectrum ℝ A), ℝ)) :
  hA.cfcAux g =
    ↑hA.eigenvectorUnitary * diagonal (RCLike.ofReal ∘ ⇑g ∘ fun i => ⟨hA.eigenvalues i, ⋯⟩) *
      star ↑hA.eigenvectorUnitary

Matrix.IsHermitian.cfc.comment:
The continuous functional calculus of a Hermitian matrix as a triple product using the
spectral theorem. Note that this actually operates on bare functions since every function is
continuous on the spectrum of a matrix, since the spectrum is finite. This is shown to be equal to
the generic continuous functional calculus API in `Matrix.IsHermitian.cfc_eq`. In general, users
should prefer the generic API, especially because it will make rewriting easier.

Basis.constr.comment:
Construct a linear map given the value at the basis, called `Basis.constr b S f` where `b` is
a basis, `f` is the value of the linear map over the elements of the basis, and `S` is an
extra semiring (typically `S = R` or `S = ℕ`).

This definition is parameterized over an extra `Semiring S`,
such that `SMulCommClass R S M'` holds.
If `R` is commutative, you can set `S := R`; if `R` is not commutative,
you can recover an `AddEquiv` by setting `S := ℕ`.
See library note [bundled maps over different rings].

Submodule.inductionOnRankAux.fullDefinition: def Submodule.inductionOnRankAux (b : Basis ι R M) (P : Submodule R M → Sort*)     (ih : ∀ N : Submodule R M,       (∀ N' ≤ N, ∀ x ∈ N, (∀ (c : R), ∀ y ∈ N', c • x + y = (0 : M) → c = 0) → P N') → P N)     (n : ℕ) (N : Submodule R M)     (rank_le : ∀ {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → N), LinearIndependent R ((↑) ∘ v : Fin m → M) → m ≤ n) :     P N := by   haveI : DecidableEq M := Classical.decEq M   have Pbot : P ⊥ := by     apply ih     intro N _ x x_mem x_ortho     exfalso     rw [mem_bot] at x_mem     simpa [x_mem] using x_ortho 1 0 N.zero_mem   induction' n with n rank_ih generalizing N   · suffices N = ⊥ by rwa [this]     apply Basis.eq_bot_of_rank_eq_zero b _ fun m hv => Nat.le_zero.mp (rank_le _ hv)   apply ih   intro N' N'_le x x_mem x_ortho   apply rank_ih   intro m v hli   refine Nat.succ_le_succ_iff.mp (rank_le (Fin.cons ⟨x, x_mem⟩ fun i => ⟨v i, N'_le (v i).2⟩) ?_)   convert hli.fin_cons' x _ ?_   · ext i     refine Fin.cases ?_ ?_ i <;> simp   · intro c y hcy     refine x_ortho c y (Submodule.span_le.mpr ?_ y.2) hcy     rintro _ ⟨z, rfl⟩     exact (v z).2
Submodule.inductionOnRankAux.description: This definition describes a method for performing induction on a property related to submodules of finite rank by adjoining a linearly independent element.

Basis.mem_span_iff_repr_mem.comment:
Let `b` be an `S`-basis of `M`. Then `m : M` lies in the `R`-module spanned by `b` iff all the
coordinates of `m` on the basis `b` are in `R` (see `Basis.mem_span` for the case `R = S`).

explanatories.Set.subset_univ: Every set is a subset of the universal set.
explanatories.Basis.mk: This definition states that a family of vectors is a basis for a module if it is linearly independent and spans the entire module.
explanatories.LinearIndependent.restrict_of_comp_subty: If a set of vectors is linearly independent when restricted to a subset, then it remains linearly independent under a restriction of the original family of vectors.

explanatories.LinearIndependent.linearIndependent_exte: If a subset of vectors is linearly independent and is contained within a larger set, then the extended set of vectors remains linearly independent.

explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.LinearIndependent.subset_span_extend: If a set of vectors is linearly independent and is a subset of another set, then the larger set is contained within the span of the extended linearly independent set.

Submodule.orthogonalBilin.comment:
The orthogonal complement of a submodule `N` with respect to some bilinear map is the set of
elements `x` which are orthogonal to all elements of `N`; i.e., for all `y` in `N`, `B x y = 0`.

Note that for general (neither symmetric nor antisymmetric) bilinear maps this definition has a
chirality; in addition to this "left" orthogonal complement one could define a "right" orthogonal
complement for which, for all `y` in `N`, `B y x = 0`.  This variant definition is not currently
provided in mathlib.

explanatories.LinearMap.map_smulₛₗ: This theorem states that applying a linear map to a scalar multiplied by a vector yields the same result as multiplying the result of the linear map by the scalar.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.

Submodule.orthogonalBilin.fullDefinition: def orthogonalBilin (N : Submodule R₁ M₁) (B : M₁ →ₛₗ[I₁] M₁ →ₛₗ[I₂] M) : Submodule R₁ M₁ where   carrier := { m | ∀ n ∈ N, B.IsOrtho n m }   zero_mem' x _ := B.isOrtho_zero_right x   add_mem' hx hy n hn := by     rw [LinearMap.IsOrtho, map_add, show B n _ = 0 from hx n hn, show B n _ = 0 from hy n hn,       zero_add]   smul_mem' c x hx n hn := by     rw [LinearMap.IsOrtho, LinearMap.map_smulₛₗ, show B n x = 0 from hx n hn, smul_zero]

  {ι₁ : Type v₁} {ι₂ : Type v₂} [DecidableEq ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₂] (M₁ : ι₁ → Type w₁) (M₂ : ι₂ → Type w₂)
  [(i₁ : ι₁) → AddCommMonoid (M₁ i₁)] [(i₂ : ι₂) → AddCommMonoid (M₂ i₂)] [(i₁ : ι₁) → Module R (M₁ i₁)]
  [(i₂ : ι₂) → Module R (M₂ i₂)] [(i₁ : ι₁) → Module S (M₁ i₁)] [∀ (i₁ : ι₁), IsScalarTower R S (M₁ i₁)] :
  ((⨁ (i₁ : ι₁), M₁ i₁) ⊗[R] ⨁ (i₂ : ι₂), M₂ i₂) ≃ₗ[S] ⨁ (i : ι₁ × ι₂), M₁ i.1 ⊗[R] M₂ i.2
TensorProduct.directSum.comment:
The linear equivalence `(⨁ i₁, M₁ i₁) ⊗ (⨁ i₂, M₂ i₂) ≃ (⨁ i₁, ⨁ i₂, M₁ i₁ ⊗ M₂ i₂)`, i.e.
"tensor product distributes over direct sum".

explanatories.TensorProduct.ext: This theorem establishes that if two linear maps from the tensor product of two modules to a third module are equal when restricted through a specific construction, then the linear maps themselves must be identical.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ofLinear: This definition states that a pair of linear maps that are inverses of each other form a linear equivalence between two modules over different semirings.
explanatories.TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.lift: The definition describes a process for creating a linear map from the tensor product of two modules to a third module based on a specified bilinear map that holds a particular composition property with respect to a canonical bilinear map.
explanatories.DirectSum.toModule: This definition provides a linear map from the direct sum of a family of R-modules to another module, constructed using a specified linear function for each component.
explanatories.LinearMap.flip: This definition describes a process that takes a bilinear map and rearranges the order of its variables to form a new linear map.
explanatories.TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.curry: The definition describes a transformation that takes a linear map from the tensor product of two modules to a third module and converts it into a bilinear map from one module to another that ultimately outputs elements in the third module.
explanatories.DirectSum.lof: This definition provides a linear map that includes each individual component of a family of R-modules into their direct sum.
explanatories.TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.map: The definition describes a process for creating a linear map from the tensor product of two modules to the tensor product of their respective images under given linear maps.
explanatories.DirectSum.linearMap_ext: This theorem states that two linear maps from a direct sum of modules are identical if they produce the same output when applied to each generator of that sum.
explanatories.TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.ext: The theorem asserts that if two linear maps from the tensor product of two modules to a third module produce the same outputs for all combinations of inputs from the first two modules, then those linear maps are identical.
explanatories.LinearMap.coe_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the function corresponding to the composition of two linear maps is equivalent to the composition of their respective functions.
explanatories.Function.comp_apply: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.
explanatories.DirectSum.toModule_lof: This theorem states that the linear map derived from the universal property of a direct sum, when restricted to a specific component, reproduces the original linear functions defined for each individual module.
explanatories.TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.map_tm: The theorem demonstrates that applying a linear map to the tensor product of two elements is equivalent to taking the tensor product of the mapped results of each element under their respective linear maps.
explanatories.TensorProduct.lift.tmul: This theorem states that applying a lifted bilinear map to the tensor product of two elements yields the same result as applying the original bilinear map to each element and then the second component.
explanatories.LinearMap.coe_restrictScalars: This theorem asserts that the action of coercing a linear map to restrict its scalars does not change its underlying function.
explanatories.LinearMap.flip_apply: This theorem establishes that applying a flipped linear map to a pair of inputs yields the same result as first applying the original map to one input and then the result to the other input.
explanatories.TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.curry_: The definition describes a transformation that takes a linear map from the tensor product of two modules to a third module and converts it into a bilinear map from one module to another that ultimately outputs elements in the third module.
explanatories.TensorProduct.curry_apply: This theorem states that applying a linear map to the tensor product of two elements can be achieved by first curving one element and then applying the resulting function to the other element.
explanatories.LinearMap.id_comp: This theorem confirms that the composition of an identity linear map with any linear map results in the original linear map unchanged.
explanatories.TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.curry_: The theorem establishes that the transformation converting a linear map from the tensor product of two modules into a bilinear map is injective, meaning that different linear maps yield different bilinear maps.
explanatories.LinearMap.ext: This theorem states that if two linear maps agree on all inputs, then they are equal as functions.
explanatories.LinearMap.id_coe: This theorem shows that the identity linear map is equivalent to the usual identity function when viewed as a function from a module over a semiring.
explanatories.id_eq: The identity function returns each element unchanged, establishing that applying it to any element results in that same element.
explanatories.TensorProduct.lift: This definition describes a method to construct a linear map from the tensor product of two modules to a third module, based on a given bilinear map.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp_apply: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of two linear maps applied to an element yields the same result as applying each map sequentially to that element.
explanatories.TensorProduct.tmul: This definition introduces a canonical function that maps elements from two modules over a commutative semiring to their tensor product.

TensorProduct.directSum.fullDefinition: protected def directSum :     ((⨁ i₁, M₁ i₁) ⊗[R] ⨁ i₂, M₂ i₂) ≃ₗ[S] ⨁ i : ι₁ × ι₂, M₁ i.1 ⊗[R] M₂ i.2 := by   -- Porting note: entirely rewritten to allow unification to happen one step at a time   refine LinearEquiv.ofLinear (R := S) (R₂ := S) ?toFun ?invFun ?left ?right   · refine AlgebraTensorModule.lift ?_     refine DirectSum.toModule S _ _ fun i₁ => ?_     refine LinearMap.flip ?_     refine DirectSum.toModule R _ _ fun i₂ => LinearMap.flip <| ?_     refine AlgebraTensorModule.curry ?_     exact DirectSum.lof S (ι₁ × ι₂) (fun i => M₁ i.1 ⊗[R] M₂ i.2) (i₁, i₂)   · refine DirectSum.toModule S _ _ fun i => ?_     exact AlgebraTensorModule.map (DirectSum.lof S _ M₁ i.1) (DirectSum.lof R _ M₂ i.2)   · refine DirectSum.linearMap_ext S fun ⟨i₁, i₂⟩ => ?_     refine TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.ext fun m₁ m₂ => ?_     -- Porting note: seems much nicer than the `repeat` lean 3 proof.     simp only [coe_comp, Function.comp_apply, toModule_lof, AlgebraTensorModule.map_tmul,       AlgebraTensorModule.lift_apply, lift.tmul, coe_restrictScalars, flip_apply,       AlgebraTensorModule.curry_apply, curry_apply, id_comp]   · -- `(_)` prevents typeclass search timing out on problems that can be solved immediately by     -- unification     apply TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.curry_injective     refine DirectSum.linearMap_ext _ fun i₁ => ?_     refine LinearMap.ext fun x₁ => ?_     refine DirectSum.linearMap_ext _ fun i₂ => ?_     refine LinearMap.ext fun x₂ => ?_     -- Porting note: seems much nicer than the `repeat` lean 3 proof.     simp only [coe_comp, Function.comp_apply, AlgebraTensorModule.curry_apply, curry_apply,       coe_restrictScalars, AlgebraTensorModule.lift_apply, lift.tmul, toModule_lof, flip_apply,       AlgebraTensorModule.map_tmul, id_coe, id_eq]   /- was:
TensorProduct.directSum.description: This definition states that the tensor product of direct sums of two modules is linearly equivalent to the direct sum of their individual tensor products, demonstrating the distributive property of the tensor product over direct sums.

explanatories.DirectSum.toModule: This definition provides a linear map from the direct sum of a family of R-modules to another module, constructed using a specified linear function for each component.
explanatories.DirectSum.lof: This definition provides a linear map that includes each individual component of a family of R-modules into their direct sum.
explanatories.Prod.mk: A pair is constructed from two given terms, resulting in a tuple that combines them.
explanatories.DirectSum.linearMap_ext: This theorem states that two linear maps from a direct sum of modules are identical if they produce the same output when applied to each generator of that sum.
explanatories.TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.ext: The theorem asserts that if two linear maps from the tensor product of two modules to a third module produce the same outputs for all combinations of inputs from the first two modules, then those linear maps are identical.
explanatories.Function.comp_apply: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.
explanatories.DirectSum.toModule_lof: This theorem states that the linear map derived from the universal property of a direct sum, when restricted to a specific component, reproduces the original linear functions defined for each individual module.
explanatories.TensorProduct.lift.tmul: This theorem states that applying a lifted bilinear map to the tensor product of two elements yields the same result as applying the original bilinear map to each element and then the second component.
explanatories.LinearMap.ext: This theorem states that if two linear maps agree on all inputs, then they are equal as functions.
explanatories.LinearMap.compr₂: This defines a bilinear map created by composing a linear map from one module to another with a bilinear map from a third module to the first two modules.
explanatories.LinearMap.rTensor: This definition describes a natural linear map that extends a linear transformation from one module to a tensor product with another module.
explanatories.LinearMap.ext₂: This theorem states that if two linear maps yield the same output for all input pairs, then they are equal as maps.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp_apply: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of two linear maps applied to an element yields the same result as applying each map sequentially to that element.
explanatories.LinearMap.compr₂_apply: This theorem asserts that applying a composed linear map to an element from one module and an element from another module results in the same value as first applying the original linear map and then applying a subsequent linear map to that result.
explanatories.LinearMap.id_apply: This theorem demonstrates that the identity function applied to an element of a module returns that element unchanged.
explanatories.TensorProduct.mk_apply: This theorem asserts that the application of the tensor product to two elements from distinct modules corresponds to their associated representation in a specific tensor product construction.
explanatories.LinearMap.rTensor_tmul: This theorem states that applying a linear map to one component of a tensor product and then performing the tensor product operation with another element yields the same result as first performing the tensor product and then applying the linear map to the first component.
explanatories.TensorProduct.tmul: This definition introduces a canonical function that maps elements from two modules over a commutative semiring to their tensor product.

TensorProduct.directSumLeft.fullDefinition: def directSumLeft : (⨁ i₁, M₁ i₁) ⊗[R] M₂' ≃ₗ[R] ⨁ i, M₁ i ⊗[R] M₂' :=   LinearEquiv.ofLinear     (lift <|       DirectSum.toModule R _ _ fun i =>         (mk R _ _).compr₂ <| DirectSum.lof R ι₁ (fun i => M₁ i ⊗[R] M₂') _)     (DirectSum.toModule R _ _ fun i => rTensor _ (DirectSum.lof R ι₁ _ _))     (DirectSum.linearMap_ext R fun i =>       TensorProduct.ext <|         LinearMap.ext₂ fun m₁ m₂ => by           dsimp only [comp_apply, compr₂_apply, id_apply, mk_apply]           simp_rw [DirectSum.toModule_lof, rTensor_tmul, lift.tmul, DirectSum.toModule_lof,             compr₂_apply, mk_apply])     (TensorProduct.ext <|       DirectSum.linearMap_ext R fun i =>         LinearMap.ext₂ fun m₁ m₂ => by           dsimp only [comp_apply, compr₂_apply, id_apply, mk_apply]           simp_rw [lift.tmul, DirectSum.toModule_lof, compr₂_apply,             mk_apply, DirectSum.toModule_lof, rTensor_tmul])
TensorProduct.directSumLeft.description: This definition states that the tensor product of a direct sum of modules on the left is linearly equivalent to the direct sum of the tensor products of the individual modules, highlighting the distributive property of tensor products over direct sums.

TensorProduct.directSum_lof_tmul_lof.{u, v₁, v₂, w₁, w₂, u_1} (R : Type u) [CommSemiring R] (S : Type u_1) [Semiring S]
  [Algebra R S] {ι₁ : Type v₁} {ι₂ : Type v₂} [DecidableEq ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₂] {M₁ : ι₁ → Type w₁} {M₂ : ι₂ → Type w₂}
  [(i₁ : ι₁) → AddCommMonoid (M₁ i₁)] [(i₂ : ι₂) → AddCommMonoid (M₂ i₂)] [(i₁ : ι₁) → Module R (M₁ i₁)]
  [(i₂ : ι₂) → Module R (M₂ i₂)] [(i₁ : ι₁) → Module S (M₁ i₁)] [∀ (i₁ : ι₁), IsScalarTower R S (M₁ i₁)] (i₁ : ι₁)
  (m₁ : M₁ i₁) (i₂ : ι₂) (m₂ : M₂ i₂) :
  (TensorProduct.directSum R S M₁ M₂) ((lof S ι₁ M₁ i₁) m₁ ⊗ₜ[R] (lof R ι₂ M₂ i₂) m₂) =
    (lof S (ι₁ × ι₂) (fun i => M₁ i.1 ⊗[R] M₂ i.2) (i₁, i₂)) (m₁ ⊗ₜ[R] m₂)

  {M₁ : ι₁ → Type w₁} {M₂' : Type w₂'} [(i₁ : ι₁) → AddCommMonoid (M₁ i₁)] [AddCommMonoid M₂']

explanatories.MultilinearMap.toFun: This definition specifies a function that represents the action of a given multilinear map on a multivariate input.
explanatories.DFunLike.ext: There is no theorem stated in this input.
explanatories.AlternatingMap.ext: This theorem states that if two alternating maps produce the same output for all inputs, then the maps themselves are equal.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.map_add': This theorem states that a multilinear map is additive with respect to each of its arguments.
explanatories.AlternatingMap: This theorem states that for an alternating map, if two elements are equal at different indices, then the value of the map at that input is zero.
explanatories.AlternatingMap.smul_apply: This theorem states that scaling an alternating map by a scalar from a multipicative monoid commutes with the action of that map on an indexed family of elements, producing the same result as first applying the map and then scaling the output.
explanatories.Prod.ext: If two pairs of elements have equal first components and equal second components, then the pairs themselves are equal.
explanatories.AlternatingMap.add_apply: This theorem confirms that the sum of two alternating maps applied to a vector yields the same result as applying each map to the vector individually and then adding the results.
explanatories.AlternatingMap.zero_apply: This theorem states that applying an alternating map to the zero vector will yield zero regardless of the input.
explanatories.AlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq': This theorem states that for an alternating map, if two elements are equal at different indices, then the value of the map at that input is zero.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.LinearMap.zero_apply: This theorem asserts that applying a linear map to the zero element of a module yields the zero element in the codomain.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ext: This theorem establishes that if two linear equivalences agree on their action for all elements, then they are identical.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm: This definition introduces the type that represents all bijections from a set to itself.
explanatories.Equiv.Perm.sign: This definition specifies a function that assigns a parity value of either 1 for even permutations or -1 for odd permutations, serving as a surjective group homomorphism from the group of permutations to the two-element group representing sign.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.domDomCongr: This definition establishes a construction that modifies a multilinear map by transferring its input indices according to an equivalence between two types of indexing sets.
explanatories.AlternatingMap.domDomCongr_apply: This definition provides a way to adapt an alternating map to a new set of argument indices by utilizing a given equivalence between the original and new indices.
explanatories.AlternatingMap.domDomCongr: This definition provides a way to adapt an alternating map to a new set of argument indices by utilizing a given equivalence between the original and new indices.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.ext: This theorem establishes that if two multilinear maps produce the same output for all inputs, then they are equal as maps.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.sum_apply: This theorem states that the sum of the outputs of a collection of multilinear maps applied to a multivariate input is equal to the application of the sum of those multilinear maps to the same input.
explanatories._private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli: This theorem asserts that if two entries of a multivariate input to a multilinear map are equal, then the sum of the permuted contributions from all permutations of the input equals zero.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.mk_coe: This theorem establishes that a multilinear map, defined by its properties of additivity and scalar multiplication, can be represented as a function with these same characteristics.
explanatories.AlternatingMap.coe_mk: This theorem establishes that the function associated with an alternating map constructed from a multilinear map and a given condition is equivalent to the function of the multilinear map itself when viewed in a specific way.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.smul_apply: This theorem states that scaling a multilinear map by a scalar results in scaling the output of the map at any multivariate input by the same scalar.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.domDomCongr_apply: This definition establishes a construction that modifies a multilinear map by transferring its input indices according to an equivalence between two types of indexing sets.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.zero_apply: This theorem asserts that applying a multilinear map to the zero input yields zero as the result.
explanatories.Finset.sum_const_zero: The sum of zero over any finite set equals zero.
explanatories.MultilinearMap.add_apply: This theorem states that the addition of two multilinear maps results in applying the addition operation to their outputs when evaluated at the same multivariate input.
explanatories.Finset.sum_add_distrib: The theorem demonstrates that the sum of values obtained by adding two functions over a finite set equals the sum of the values from each function computed separately over the same set.

AlternatingMap.curryLeft.code:
AlternatingMap.curryLeft.{u_10, u_11, u_13} {R' : Type u_10} {M'' : Type u_11} {N'' : Type u_13} [CommSemiring R']
  [AddCommMonoid M''] [AddCommMonoid N''] [Module R' M''] [Module R' N''] {n : ℕ} (f : M'' [⋀^Fin n.succ]→ₗ[R'] N'') :
  M'' →ₗ[R'] M'' [⋀^Fin n]→ₗ[R'] N''
AlternatingMap.curryLeft.comment:
Given an alternating map `f` in `n+1` variables, split the first variable to obtain
a linear map into alternating maps in `n` variables, given by `x ↦ (m ↦ f (Matrix.vecCons x m))`.
It can be thought of as a map $Hom(\bigwedge^{n+1} M, N) \to Hom(M, Hom(\bigwedge^n M, N))$.

This is `MultilinearMap.curryLeft` for `AlternatingMap`. See also
`AlternatingMap.curryLeftLinearMap`.

AlternatingMap.domCoprod.summand.fullDefinition: def domCoprod.summand (a : Mᵢ [⋀^ιa]→ₗ[R'] N₁) (b : Mᵢ [⋀^ιb]→ₗ[R'] N₂)     (σ : Perm.ModSumCongr ιa ιb) : MultilinearMap R' (fun _ : Sum ιa ιb => Mᵢ) (N₁ ⊗[R'] N₂) :=   Quotient.liftOn' σ     (fun σ =>       Equiv.Perm.sign σ •         (MultilinearMap.domCoprod ↑a ↑b : MultilinearMap R' (fun _ => Mᵢ) (N₁ ⊗ N₂)).domDomCongr σ)     fun σ₁ σ₂ H => by     rw [QuotientGroup.leftRel_apply] at H     obtain ⟨⟨sl, sr⟩, h⟩ := H     ext v     simp only [MultilinearMap.domDomCongr_apply, MultilinearMap.domCoprod_apply,       coe_multilinearMap, MultilinearMap.smul_apply]     replace h := inv_mul_eq_iff_eq_mul.mp h.symm     have : Equiv.Perm.sign (σ₁ * Perm.sumCongrHom _ _ (sl, sr))       = Equiv.Perm.sign σ₁ * (Equiv.Perm.sign sl * Equiv.Perm.sign sr) := by simp     rw [h, this, mul_smul, mul_smul, smul_left_cancel_iff, ← TensorProduct.tmul_smul,       TensorProduct.smul_tmul']     simp only [Sum.map_inr, Perm.sumCongrHom_apply, Perm.sumCongr_apply, Sum.map_inl,       Function.comp_apply, Perm.coe_mul]     -- Porting note (#10691): was `rw`.     erw [← a.map_congr_perm fun i => v (σ₁ _), ← b.map_congr_perm fun i => v (σ₁ _)]

  {R' : Type u_3} {Mᵢ : Type u_4} {N₁ : Type u_5} {N₂ : Type u_6} [CommSemiring R'] [AddCommGroup N₁] [Module R' N₁]

  (a : Mᵢ [⋀^ιa]→ₗ[R'] N₁) (b : Mᵢ [⋀^ιb]→ₗ[R'] N₂) : Mᵢ [⋀^ιa ⊕ ιb]→ₗ[R'] N₁ ⊗[R'] N₂
AlternatingMap.domCoprod.comment:
Like `MultilinearMap.domCoprod`, but ensures the result is also alternating.

Note that this is usually defined (for instance, as used in Proposition 22.24 in [Gallier2011Notes])
over integer indices `ιa = Fin n` and `ιb = Fin m`, as
$$
(f \wedge g)(u_1, \ldots, u_{m+n}) =
  \sum_{\operatorname{shuffle}(m, n)} \operatorname{sign}(\sigma)
    f(u_{\sigma(1)}, \ldots, u_{\sigma(m)}) g(u_{\sigma(m+1)}, \ldots, u_{\sigma(m+n)}),
$$
where $\operatorname{shuffle}(m, n)$ consists of all permutations of $[1, m+n]$ such that
$\sigma(1) < \cdots < \sigma(m)$ and $\sigma(m+1) < \cdots < \sigma(m+n)$.

Here, we generalize this by replacing:
* the product in the sum with a tensor product
* the filtering of $[1, m+n]$ to shuffles with an isomorphic quotient
* the additions in the subscripts of $\sigma$ with an index of type `Sum`

The specialized version can be obtained by combining this definition with `finSumFinEquiv` and
`LinearMap.mul'`.

AlternatingMap.domCoprod.fullDefinition: def domCoprod (a : Mᵢ [⋀^ιa]→ₗ[R'] N₁) (b : Mᵢ [⋀^ιb]→ₗ[R'] N₂) :     Mᵢ [⋀^ιa ⊕ ιb]→ₗ[R'] (N₁ ⊗[R'] N₂) :=   { ∑ σ : Perm.ModSumCongr ιa ιb, domCoprod.summand a b σ with     toFun := fun v => (⇑(∑ σ : Perm.ModSumCongr ιa ιb, domCoprod.summand a b σ)) v     map_eq_zero_of_eq' := fun v i j hv hij => by       dsimp only       rw [MultilinearMap.sum_apply]       exact         Finset.sum_involution (fun σ _ => Equiv.swap i j • σ)           (fun σ _ => domCoprod.summand_add_swap_smul_eq_zero a b σ hv hij)           (fun σ _ => mt <| domCoprod.summand_eq_zero_of_smul_invariant a b σ hv hij)           (fun σ _ => Finset.mem_univ _) fun σ _ =>           Equiv.swap_smul_involutive i j σ }

explanatories.MultilinearMap.domCoprod'_apply: This theorem establishes the equality between two forms of combining multilinear maps through the coproduct and tensor product operations, confirming that applying the coproduct to the tensor product of two maps yields the same result as applying the defined coproduct operation directly to those maps.
explanatories.TensorProduct.add_tmul: This theorem proves that the tensor product distributes over addition in the first argument when combining elements from two modules.

explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear map commutes with scalar multiplication, meaning that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is the same as multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar.
explanatories.SMulCommClass.smul_comm: This theorem states that in the presence of a commutative scalar multiplication structure, the order of multiplying two elements with a third remains unchanged when using scalar multiplication.

MultilinearMap.domCoprod_alternization_coe.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6} {ιa : Type u_1} {ιb : Type u_2} [Fintype ιa]
  [Fintype ιb] {R' : Type u_3} {Mᵢ : Type u_4} {N₁ : Type u_5} {N₂ : Type u_6} [CommSemiring R'] [AddCommGroup N₁]
  [Module R' N₁] [AddCommGroup N₂] [Module R' N₂] [AddCommMonoid Mᵢ] [Module R' Mᵢ] [DecidableEq ιa] [DecidableEq ιb]
  (a : MultilinearMap R' (fun x => Mᵢ) N₁) (b : MultilinearMap R' (fun x => Mᵢ) N₂) :
  (↑(MultilinearMap.alternatization a)).domCoprod ↑(MultilinearMap.alternatization b) =
    ∑ σa : Perm ιa,
      ∑ σb : Perm ιb,
        Perm.sign σa • Perm.sign σb • (MultilinearMap.domDomCongr σa a).domCoprod (MultilinearMap.domDomCongr σb b)

Pi.basis.code:
Pi.basis.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {R : Type u_1} {η : Type u_2} {ιs : η → Type u_3} {Ms : η → Type u_4} [Semiring R]
  [(i : η) → AddCommMonoid (Ms i)] [(i : η) → Module R (Ms i)] [Fintype η] (s : (j : η) → Basis (ιs j) R (Ms j)) :
  Basis ((j : η) × ιs j) R ((j : η) → Ms j)
Pi.basis.comment:
`Pi.basis (s : ∀ j, Basis (ιs j) R (Ms j))` is the `Σ j, ιs j`-indexed basis on `Π j, Ms j`
given by `s j` on each component.

For the standard basis over `R` on the finite-dimensional space `η → R` see `Pi.basisFun`.

explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.Basis.ofRepr: This definition establishes a linear equivalence that maps a vector to its coordinates with respect to a given basis.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.piCongrRight: This definition combines a family of linear equivalences into a single linear equivalence for a product of type families.
explanatories.Basis.repr: This definition establishes a linear equivalence that maps a vector to its coordinates with respect to a given basis.
explanatories.Finsupp.sigmaFinsuppLEquivPiFinsupp: This definition establishes a linear equivalence between the space of finitely supported functions over a dependent sum type and the space of functions mapping indices to finitely supported functions over the corresponding types.

Pi.basis.fullDefinition: protected noncomputable def basis (s : ∀ j, Basis (ιs j) R (Ms j)) :     Basis (Σj, ιs j) R (∀ j, Ms j) :=   Basis.ofRepr     ((LinearEquiv.piCongrRight fun j => (s j).repr) ≪≫ₗ       (Finsupp.sigmaFinsuppLEquivPiFinsupp R).symm)   --  Porting note: was   -- -- The `AddCommMonoid (Π j, Ms j)` instance was hard to find.   -- -- Defining this in tactic mode seems to shake up instance search enough   -- -- that it works by itself.   -- refine Basis.ofRepr (?_ ≪≫ₗ (Finsupp.sigmaFinsuppLEquivPiFinsupp R).symm)   -- exact LinearEquiv.piCongrRight fun j => (s j).repr
Pi.basis.description: This definition specifies a basis for a product space, constructed from individual bases of component spaces, allowing for a structured representation of complex vector spaces.

Module.Free.constr.code:
Module.Free.constr.{u, v, z} (R : Type u) (M : Type v) (N : Type z) [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
  [Free R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] {S : Type z} [Semiring S] [Module S N] [SMulCommClass R S N] :
  (ChooseBasisIndex R M → N) ≃ₗ[S] M →ₗ[R] N
Module.Free.constr.comment:
The universal property of free modules: giving a function `(ChooseBasisIndex R M) → N`, for `N`
an `R`-module, is the same as giving an `R`-linear map `M →ₗ[R] N`.

This definition is parameterized over an extra `Semiring S`,
such that `SMulCommClass R S M'` holds.
If `R` is commutative, you can set `S := R`; if `R` is not commutative,
you can recover an `AddEquiv` by setting `S := ℕ`.
See library note [bundled maps over different rings].

explanatories.Basis.constr: This definition establishes a method to construct a linear map using the values assigned to a basis over an additional semiring, allowing for flexibility in the scalar multiplication structure.

Module.Free.constr.fullDefinition: noncomputable def constr {S : Type z} [Semiring S] [Module S N] [SMulCommClass R S N] :     (ChooseBasisIndex R M → N) ≃ₗ[S] M →ₗ[R] N :=   Basis.constr (chooseBasis R M) S
Module.Free.constr.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between providing a function from a basis index set to another module and giving a linear map from a free module to that second module, encapsulating the universal property of free modules.

Submodule.basis_of_pid_aux.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
  [IsPrincipalIdealRing R] [Finite ι] {O : Type u_4} [AddCommGroup O] [Module R O] (M N : Submodule R O)
  (b'M : Basis ι R ↥M) (N_bot : N ≠ ⊥) (N_le_M : N ≤ M) :
  ∃ y ∈ M,
    ∃ a,
      a • y ∈ N ∧
        ∃ M' ≤ M,
          ∃ N' ≤ N,
            N' ≤ M' ∧
              (∀ (c : R), ∀ z ∈ M', c • y + z = 0 → c = 0) ∧
                (∀ (c : R), ∀ z ∈ N', c • a • y + z = 0 → c = 0) ∧
                  ∀ (n' : ℕ) (bN' : Basis (Fin n') R ↥N'),
                    ∃ bN,
                      ∀ (m' : ℕ) (hn'm' : n' ≤ m') (bM' : Basis (Fin m') R ↥M'),
                        ∃ (hnm : n' + 1 ≤ m' + 1),
                          ∃ bM,
                            ∀ (as : Fin n' → R),
                              (∀ (i : Fin n'), ↑(bN' i) = as i • ↑(bM' (Fin.castLE hn'm' i))) →
                                ∃ as', ∀ (i : Fin (n' + 1)), ↑(bN i) = as' i • ↑(bM (Fin.castLE hnm i))
Submodule.basis_of_pid_aux.comment:
The induction hypothesis of `Submodule.basisOfPid` and `Submodule.smithNormalForm`.

Basically, it says: let `N ≤ M` be a pair of submodules, then we can find a pair of
submodules `N' ≤ M'` of strictly smaller rank, whose basis we can extend to get a basis
of `N` and `M`. Moreover, if the basis for `M'` is up to scalars a basis for `N'`,
then the basis we find for `M` is up to scalars a basis for `N`.

For `basis_of_pid` we only need the first half and can fix `M = ⊤`,
for `smith_normal_form` we need the full statement,
but must also feed in a basis for `M` using `basis_of_pid` to keep the induction going.

explanatories.Fin.castLE: A finite number is embedded into a larger finite number when there is a non-strict inequality between their respective upper limits.

submodule.basis_of_pid_aux.comment:
The induction hypothesis of `Submodule.basisOfPid` and `Submodule.smithNormalForm`.

Basically, it says: let `N ≤ M` be a pair of submodules, then we can find a pair of
submodules `N' ≤ M'` of strictly smaller rank, whose basis we can extend to get a basis
of `N` and `M`. Moreover, if the basis for `M'` is up to scalars a basis for `N'`,
then the basis we find for `M` is up to scalars a basis for `N`.

For `basis_of_pid` we only need the first half and can fix `M = ⊤`,
for `smith_normal_form` we need the full statement,
but must also feed in a basis for `M` using `basis_of_pid` to keep the induction going.

explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.

explanatories.MulAction.mul_smul: This theorem states that the action of multiplying two elements behaves associatively with respect to both multiplication and the action on another element.
explanatories.LinearMap.ker: The kernel of a linear map is defined as the set of elements in the domain that are mapped to zero in the codomain, and it forms a submodule of the domain.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm: This definition specifies the symmetry of linear equivalences, indicating that the inverse relationship between two modules can be expressed as a linear equivalence in the opposite direction.
explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.

explanatories.Set.mem_range_self: An element obtained by applying a function to an index is guaranteed to be part of the range of that function.

Module.basisOfFiniteTypeTorsionFree.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Module.basisOfFiniteTypeTorsionFree [Fintype ι] {s : ι → M}     (hs : span R (range s) = ⊤) [NoZeroSMulDivisors R M] : Σn : ℕ, Basis (Fin n) R M := by   classical     -- We define `N` as the submodule spanned by a maximal linear independent subfamily of `s`     have := exists_maximal_independent R s     let I : Set ι := this.choose     obtain       ⟨indepI : LinearIndependent R (s ∘ (fun x => x) : I → M), hI :         ∀ i ∉ I, ∃ a : R, a ≠ 0 ∧ a • s i ∈ span R (s '' I)⟩ :=       this.choose_spec     let N := span R (range <| (s ∘ (fun x => x) : I → M))     -- same as `span R (s '' I)` but more convenient     let _sI : I → N := fun i ↦ ⟨s i.1, subset_span (mem_range_self i)⟩     -- `s` restricted to `I` is a basis of `N`     let sI_basis : Basis I R N := Basis.span indepI     -- Our first goal is to build `A ≠ 0` such that `A • M ⊆ N`     have exists_a : ∀ i : ι, ∃ a : R, a ≠ 0 ∧ a • s i ∈ N := by       intro i       by_cases hi : i ∈ I       · use 1, zero_ne_one.symm         rw [one_smul]         exact subset_span (mem_range_self (⟨i, hi⟩ : I))       · simpa [image_eq_range s I] using hI i hi     choose a ha ha' using exists_a     let A := ∏ i, a i     have hA : A ≠ 0 := by       rw [Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff]       simpa using ha     -- `M ≃ A • M` because `M` is torsion free and `A ≠ 0`     let φ : M →ₗ[R] M := LinearMap.lsmul R M A     have : LinearMap.ker φ = ⊥ := @LinearMap.ker_lsmul R M _ _ _ _ _ hA     let ψ := LinearEquiv.ofInjective φ (LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mp this)     have : LinearMap.range φ ≤ N := by       -- as announced, `A • M ⊆ N`       suffices ∀ i, φ (s i) ∈ N by         rw [LinearMap.range_eq_map, ← hs, map_span_le]         rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩         apply this       intro i       calc         (∏ j, a j) • s i = (∏ j ∈ {i}ᶜ, a j) • a i • s i := by           rw [Fintype.prod_eq_prod_compl_mul i, mul_smul]         _ ∈ N := N.smul_mem _ (ha' i)

Submodule.exists_smith_normal_form_of_le.code:

  [IsPrincipalIdealRing R] {M : Type u_3} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Finite ι] (b : Basis ι R M)
  (N O : Submodule R M) (N_le_O : N ≤ O) :
  ∃ n o, ∃ (hno : n ≤ o), ∃ bO bN a, ∀ (i : Fin n), ↑(bN i) = a i • ↑(bO (Fin.castLE hno i))
Submodule.exists_smith_normal_form_of_le.comment:
If `M` is finite free over a PID `R`, then any submodule `N` is free
and we can find a basis for `M` and `N` such that the inclusion map is a diagonal matrix
in Smith normal form.

See `Submodule.smithNormalFormOfLE` for a version of this theorem that returns
a `Basis.SmithNormalForm`.

This is a strengthening of `Submodule.basisOfPidOfLE`.

explanatories.Fin.castLE: A finite number is embedded into a larger finite number when there is a non-strict inequality between their respective upper limits.
explanatories.Basis.SmithNormalForm.bN: This definition provides a method to obtain a basis for a submodule from its Smith normal form representation.
explanatories.Basis.SmithNormalForm.a: This definition establishes a function that retrieves the diagonal entries of a matrix associated with the Smith normal form of a submodule.

Submodule.exists_smith_normal_form_of_le.description: This theorem asserts that for a finite free module over a principal ideal domain, any submodule can be represented by a basis such that the inclusion map can be described by a diagonal matrix in Smith normal form.

Submodule.smithNormalForm.comment:
If `M` is finite free over a PID `R`, then any submodule `N` is free
and we can find a basis for `M` and `N` such that the inclusion map is a diagonal matrix
in Smith normal form.

This is a strengthening of `Submodule.basisOfPid`.

See also `Ideal.smithNormalForm`, which moreover proves that the dimension of
an ideal is the same as the dimension of the whole ring.

explanatories.Basis.SmithNormalForm: This definition provides a mapping from the finite index set of a Smith normal form basis to the original basis vectors of a submodule in a module over a commutative ring.

explanatories.Basis.SmithNormalForm.bM: This definition states the basis of a module in the context of the Smith normal form for a submodule, establishing the relationship between the original module and its basis vectors.
explanatories.Basis.SmithNormalForm.bN: This definition provides a method to obtain a basis for a submodule from its Smith normal form representation.
explanatories.Basis.SmithNormalForm.snf: This theorem establishes a relationship between the vectors of the bases in a Smith normal form, demonstrating how one vector in the submodule can be expressed as a scalar multiple of another vector in the module, linked through a specific mapping.
explanatories.Basis.SmithNormalForm.a: This definition establishes a function that retrieves the diagonal entries of a matrix associated with the Smith normal form of a submodule.
explanatories.Basis.map_apply: This theorem states that the application of a linear isomorphism to a basis vector can be computed by applying the isomorphism directly to the representation of that basis vector.
explanatories.Submodule.coe_smul_of_tower: This theorem asserts that when an element from a submodule is scaled by a scalar from a larger structure that acts as a scalar tower, the result remains consistent when viewed in both the submodule and the original module.
explanatories.Submodule.smithNormalFormOfLE: This definition asserts that for a finite free module over a principal ideal domain, any submodule can be expressed with a basis such that the inclusion map corresponds to a diagonal matrix in Smith normal form, given that one submodule is contained within another.
explanatories.Function.Embedding.trans: The composition of two embeddings results in a new embedding that maps elements from the first type to the third type through the intermediate type.
explanatories.Equiv.toEmbedding: An equivalence between two types is transformed into an embedding that retains the injective property of the original function.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ofTop_apply: This theorem states that when applying a linear equivalence from the top submodule to the module, an element from the submodule is represented identically in the module.
explanatories.Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe_apply_co: The theorem establishes an equality relating the elements of a preimage of a submodule through a subtype with the elements of the original preimage, given that one submodule is contained within the other.
explanatories.Basis.reindex_apply: This theorem asserts that applying a basis that has been reindexed corresponds to retrieving the original basis vector using the inverse of the reindexing function.
explanatories.Equiv.toEmbedding_apply: Applying an equivalence function to an element of its domain yields the same result as applying the corresponding embedding created from that equivalence.
explanatories.Function.Embedding.trans_apply: No theorem is presented, so there is nothing to summarize.
explanatories.Equiv.symm_apply_apply: This theorem shows that applying an equivalence and then its inverse will return the original element from the first type.

Submodule.smithNormalForm.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Submodule.smithNormalForm [Finite ι] (b : Basis ι R M) (N : Submodule R M) :     Σn : ℕ, Basis.SmithNormalForm N ι n :=   let ⟨m, n, bM, bN, f, a, snf⟩ := N.smithNormalFormOfLE b ⊤ le_top   let bM' := bM.map (LinearEquiv.ofTop _ rfl)   let e := bM'.indexEquiv b   ⟨n, bM'.reindex e, bN.map (comapSubtypeEquivOfLe le_top), f.trans e.toEmbedding, a, fun i ↦ by     simp only [bM', snf, Basis.map_apply, LinearEquiv.ofTop_apply, Submodule.coe_smul_of_tower,       Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe_apply_coe, Basis.reindex_apply,       Equiv.toEmbedding_apply, Function.Embedding.trans_apply, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]⟩
Submodule.smithNormalForm.description: This definition establishes that for a finite free module over a principal ideal domain, any submodule can be characterized by a basis and a corresponding Smith normal form, representing the structure of the inclusion map as a diagonal matrix.

submodule.smith_normal_form.code:
Submodule.smithNormalForm.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
  [IsPrincipalIdealRing R] {M : Type u_3} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Finite ι] (b : Basis ι R M)
  (N : Submodule R M) : (n : ℕ) × Basis.SmithNormalForm N ι n
submodule.smith_normal_form.comment:
If `M` is finite free over a PID `R`, then any submodule `N` is free
and we can find a basis for `M` and `N` such that the inclusion map is a diagonal matrix
in Smith normal form.

This is a strengthening of `Submodule.basisOfPid`.

See also `Ideal.smithNormalForm`, which moreover proves that the dimension of
an ideal is the same as the dimension of the whole ring.

  {S : Type u_4} [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra R S] [Fintype ι] (b : Basis ι R S) (I : Ideal S) (hI : I ≠ ⊥) :

Ideal.smithNormalForm.comment:
If `S` a finite-dimensional ring extension of a PID `R` which is free as an `R`-module,
then any nonzero `S`-ideal `I` is free as an `R`-submodule of `S`, and we can
find a basis for `S` and `I` such that the inclusion map is a square diagonal
matrix.

See `Ideal.exists_smith_normal_form` for a version of this theorem that doesn't
need to map `I` into a submodule of `R`.

This is a strengthening of `Submodule.basisOfPid`.

Ideal.smithNormalForm.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Ideal.smithNormalForm [Fintype ι] (b : Basis ι R S) (I : Ideal S) (hI : I ≠ ⊥) :     Basis.SmithNormalForm (I.restrictScalars R) ι (Fintype.card ι) :=   let ⟨n, bS, bI, f, a, snf⟩ := (I.restrictScalars R).smithNormalForm b   have eq := Ideal.rank_eq bS hI (bI.map ((restrictScalarsEquiv R S S I).restrictScalars R))   let e : Fin n ≃ Fin (Fintype.card ι) := Fintype.equivOfCardEq (by rw [eq, Fintype.card_fin])   ⟨bS, bI.reindex e, e.symm.toEmbedding.trans f, a ∘ e.symm, fun i ↦ by     simp only [snf, Basis.coe_reindex, Function.Embedding.trans_apply, Equiv.toEmbedding_apply,       (· ∘ ·)]⟩

Ideal.exists_smith_normal_form.code:
Ideal.exists_smith_normal_form.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
  [IsPrincipalIdealRing R] {S : Type u_4} [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra R S] [Finite ι] (b : Basis ι R S)
  (I : Ideal S) (hI : I ≠ ⊥) : ∃ b' a ab', ∀ (i : ι), ↑(ab' i) = a i • b' i
Ideal.exists_smith_normal_form.comment:
If `S` a finite-dimensional ring extension of a PID `R` which is free as an `R`-module,
then any nonzero `S`-ideal `I` is free as an `R`-submodule of `S`, and we can
find a basis for `S` and `I` such that the inclusion map is a square diagonal
matrix.

See also `Ideal.smithNormalForm` for a version of this theorem that returns
a `Basis.SmithNormalForm`.

The definitions `Ideal.ringBasis`, `Ideal.selfBasis`, `Ideal.smithCoeffs` are (noncomputable)
choices of values for this existential quantifier.

  {S : Type u_4} [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra R S] [Finite ι] (b : Basis ι R S) (I : Ideal S) (hI : I ≠ ⊥) :
  Basis ι R ↥I
Ideal.selfBasis.comment:
If `S` a finite-dimensional ring extension of a PID `R` which is free as an `R`-module,
then any nonzero `S`-ideal `I` is free as an `R`-submodule of `S`, and we can
find a basis for `S` and `I` such that the inclusion map is a square diagonal
matrix; this is the basis for `I`.
See `Ideal.ringBasis` for the basis on `S`,
see `Ideal.smithCoeffs` for the entries of the diagonal matrix
and `Ideal.selfBasis_def` for the proof that the inclusion map forms a square diagonal matrix.

explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Submodule.pi: This definition establishes a submodule consisting of dependent functions indexed by a set, where each function's value lies within a corresponding submodule for indices included in that set.
explanatories.Set.univ: This defines the universal set for a given type as the set that includes all elements of that type.
explanatories.Submodule.map: This definition describes the construction of a new submodule in a different module by applying a semilinear map to the elements of an existing submodule.
explanatories.Basis.equivFun: This definition states that a finite-dimensional module with a basis is linearly equivalent to the set of functions that map basis elements to scalars in the underlying field.

explanatories.Submodule.mem_map: This theorem characterizes an element in the image of a submodule under a semilinear map as being expressible as the image of some element from the original submodule under that map.
explanatories.Submodule.mem_pi: This theorem characterizes membership in the product of submodules by stating that an element belongs to the product if and only if its components are each within their respective submodules.
explanatories.Ideal.mem_span_singleton: An element belongs to the span generated by a singleton set if and only if it is divisible by the generator of that set in a commutative semiring.
explanatories.Set.mem_univ: Any element of a type belongs to the universal set of that type.

explanatories.smul_eq_mul: This theorem establishes that the scalar multiplication of two elements is equivalent to their multiplication in a type that has a multiplication operation.
explanatories.forall_true_left: This theorem states that for any property dependent on a true proposition, it is equivalent to asserting that the property holds for the specific instance of true.

explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.

haveI := Fintype.ofFinite ι   -- Choose `e : S ≃ₗ I` and a basis `b'` for `S` that turns the map   -- `f := ((Submodule.subtype I).restrictScalars R).comp e` into a diagonal matrix:   -- there is an `a : ι → ℤ` such that `f (b' i) = a i • b' i`.   let a := I.smithCoeffs b hI   let b' := I.ringBasis b hI   let ab := I.selfBasis b hI   have ab_eq := I.selfBasis_def b hI   have mem_I_iff : ∀ x, x ∈ I ↔ ∀ i, a i ∣ b'.repr x i := by     intro x     -- Porting note: these lines used to be `simp_rw [ab.mem_ideal_iff', ab_eq]`     rw [ab.mem_ideal_iff']     simp_rw [ab_eq]     have : ∀ (c : ι → R) (i), b'.repr (∑ j : ι, c j • a j • b' j) i = a i * c i := by       intro c i       simp only [← MulAction.mul_smul, b'.repr_sum_self, mul_comm]     constructor     · rintro ⟨c, rfl⟩ i       exact ⟨c i, this c i⟩     · rintro ha       choose c hc using ha       exact ⟨c, b'.ext_elem fun i => Eq.trans (hc i) (this c i).symm⟩   -- Now we map everything through the linear equiv `S ≃ₗ (ι → R)`,   -- which maps `I` to `I' := Π i, a i ℤ`.   let I' : Submodule R (ι → R) := Submodule.pi Set.univ fun i => span ({a i} : Set R)   have : Submodule.map (b'.equivFun : S →ₗ[R] ι → R) (I.restrictScalars R) = I' := by     ext x     simp only [I', Submodule.mem_map, Submodule.mem_pi, mem_span_singleton, Set.mem_univ,       Submodule.restrictScalars_mem, mem_I_iff, smul_eq_mul, forall_true_left, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,       Basis.equivFun_apply]     constructor     · rintro ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ i       exact hy i     · rintro hdvd       refine ⟨∑ i, x i • b' i, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩ <;> rw [b'.repr_sum_self]       · exact hdvd i   refine ((Submodule.Quotient.restrictScalarsEquiv R I).restrictScalars R).symm.trans     (σ₁₂ := RingHom.id R) (σ₃₂ := RingHom.id R) (re₂₃ := inferInstance) (re₃₂ := inferInstance) ?_   refine (Submodule.Quotient.equiv (I.restrictScalars R) I' b'.equivFun this).trans     (σ₁₂ := RingHom.id R) (σ₃₂ := RingHom.id R) (re₂₃ := inferInstance) (re₃₂ := inferInstance) ?_   classical     let this :=       Submodule.quotientPi (show _ → Submodule R R from fun i => span ({a i} : Set R))     exact this
