explanatories.Submodule.restrictScalars: This definition describes the process of forming an S-submodule from an R-submodule by restricting the scalar multiplication from the semiring R to the semiring S.
explanatories.Submodule.mem_map: This theorem characterizes an element in the image of a submodule under a semilinear map as being expressible as the image of some element from the original submodule under that map.
explanatories.Submodule.mem_pi: This theorem characterizes membership in the product of submodules by stating that an element belongs to the product if and only if its components are each within their respective submodules.
explanatories.Ideal.mem_span_singleton: An element belongs to the span generated by a singleton set if and only if it is divisible by the generator of that set in a commutative semiring.
explanatories.Set.mem_univ: Any element of a type belongs to the universal set of that type.
explanatories.Submodule.restrictScalars_mem: This theorem establishes that an element belongs to the S-submodule formed by restricting scalars if and only if it belongs to the original R-submodule.
explanatories.smul_eq_mul: This theorem establishes that the scalar multiplication of two elements is equivalent to their multiplication in a type that has a multiplication operation.
explanatories.forall_true_left: This theorem states that for any property dependent on a true proposition, it is equivalent to asserting that the property holds for the specific instance of true.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.coe_coe: This theorem states that the function obtained by coercing a linear equivalence to a linear map is equal to the function directly associated with that linear equivalence.
explanatories.Basis.equivFun_apply: This theorem states that the function associated with a basis applied to a vector is equal to the evaluation of that vector's representation in terms of the basis.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.Submodule.Quotient.restrictScalarsEquiv: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the quotient of a module by a submodule formed under one ring and the quotient of the same module by the same submodule considered under another ring, provided certain scalar multiplication conditions are met.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.restrictScalars: This definition states that an S-linear equivalence between two semimodules can also be regarded as an R-linear equivalence when the semimodules are structured by scalar actions from two related semirings.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.trans: This definition establishes that if there are two linear equivalences between three modules with corresponding ring homomorphisms, then there exists a direct linear equivalence between the first and last modules.
explanatories.Submodule.Quotient.equiv: This definition states that if there exists a linear equivalence between two modules that maps one submodule to another, then the quotient modules formed by their corresponding submodules are also linearly equivalent.
explanatories.Submodule.quotientPi: This definition asserts that there is an isomorphism between the quotient of a direct sum of modules and the direct sum of their respective quotients by corresponding submodules.

ideal.quotient_equiv_pi_span.fullDefinition: noncomputable def quotientEquivPiSpan (I : Ideal S) (b : Basis ι R S) (hI : I ≠ ⊥) :     (S ⧸ I) ≃ₗ[R] ∀ i, R ⧸ span ({I.smithCoeffs b hI i} : Set R) := by   haveI := Fintype.ofFinite ι   -- Choose `e : S ≃ₗ I` and a basis `b'` for `S` that turns the map   -- `f := ((Submodule.subtype I).restrictScalars R).comp e` into a diagonal matrix:   -- there is an `a : ι → ℤ` such that `f (b' i) = a i • b' i`.   let a := I.smithCoeffs b hI   let b' := I.ringBasis b hI   let ab := I.selfBasis b hI   have ab_eq := I.selfBasis_def b hI   have mem_I_iff : ∀ x, x ∈ I ↔ ∀ i, a i ∣ b'.repr x i := by     intro x     -- Porting note: these lines used to be `simp_rw [ab.mem_ideal_iff', ab_eq]`     rw [ab.mem_ideal_iff']     simp_rw [ab_eq]     have : ∀ (c : ι → R) (i), b'.repr (∑ j : ι, c j • a j • b' j) i = a i * c i := by       intro c i       simp only [← MulAction.mul_smul, b'.repr_sum_self, mul_comm]     constructor     · rintro ⟨c, rfl⟩ i       exact ⟨c i, this c i⟩     · rintro ha       choose c hc using ha       exact ⟨c, b'.ext_elem fun i => Eq.trans (hc i) (this c i).symm⟩   -- Now we map everything through the linear equiv `S ≃ₗ (ι → R)`,   -- which maps `I` to `I' := Π i, a i ℤ`.   let I' : Submodule R (ι → R) := Submodule.pi Set.univ fun i => span ({a i} : Set R)   have : Submodule.map (b'.equivFun : S →ₗ[R] ι → R) (I.restrictScalars R) = I' := by     ext x     simp only [I', Submodule.mem_map, Submodule.mem_pi, mem_span_singleton, Set.mem_univ,       Submodule.restrictScalars_mem, mem_I_iff, smul_eq_mul, forall_true_left, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,       Basis.equivFun_apply]     constructor     · rintro ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ i       exact hy i     · rintro hdvd       refine ⟨∑ i, x i • b' i, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩ <;> rw [b'.repr_sum_self]       · exact hdvd i   refine ((Submodule.Quotient.restrictScalarsEquiv R I).restrictScalars R).symm.trans     (σ₁₂ := RingHom.id R) (σ₃₂ := RingHom.id R) (re₂₃ := inferInstance) (re₃₂ := inferInstance) ?_   refine (Submodule.Quotient.equiv (I.restrictScalars R) I' b'.equivFun this).trans     (σ₁₂ := RingHom.id R) (σ₃₂ := RingHom.id R) (re₂₃ := inferInstance) (re₃₂ := inferInstance) ?_   classical     let this :=       Submodule.quotientPi (show _ → Submodule R R from fun i => span ({a i} : Set R))     exact this

TensorAlgebra.gradedAlgebra.fullDefinition: instance gradedAlgebra :     GradedAlgebra ((LinearMap.range (ι R : M →ₗ[R] TensorAlgebra R M) ^ ·) : ℕ → Submodule R _) :=   GradedAlgebra.ofAlgHom _ (lift R <| GradedAlgebra.ι R M)     (by       ext m       dsimp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply, AlgHom.comp_apply,         AlgHom.id_apply]       rw [lift_ι_apply, GradedAlgebra.ι_apply R M, DirectSum.coeAlgHom_of, Subtype.coe_mk])     fun i x => by     cases' x with x hx     dsimp only [Subtype.coe_mk, DirectSum.lof_eq_of]     -- Porting note: use new `induction using` support that failed in Lean 3     induction hx using Submodule.pow_induction_on_left' with     | algebraMap r =>       rw [AlgHom.commutes, DirectSum.algebraMap_apply]; rfl     | add x y i hx hy ihx ihy =>       -- Note: #8386 had to specialize `map_add` to avoid a timeout       -- (the extra typeclass search seems to have pushed this already slow proof over the edge)       rw [map_add, ihx, ihy, ← AddMonoidHom.map_add]       rfl     | mem_mul m hm i x hx ih =>       obtain ⟨_, rfl⟩ := hm       rw [map_mul, ih, lift_ι_apply, GradedAlgebra.ι_apply R M, DirectSum.of_mul_of]       exact DirectSum.of_eq_of_gradedMonoid_eq (Sigma.subtype_ext (add_comm _ _) rfl)

FiniteDimensional.basisSingleton.fullDefinition: noncomputable def basisSingleton (ι : Type*) [Unique ι] (h : finrank K V = 1) (v : V)     (hv : v ≠ 0) : Basis ι K V :=   let b := FiniteDimensional.basisUnique ι h   let h : b.repr v default ≠ 0 := mt FiniteDimensional.basisUnique_repr_eq_zero_iff.mp hv   Basis.ofRepr     { toFun := fun w => Finsupp.single default (b.repr w default / b.repr v default)       invFun := fun f => f default • v       map_add' := by simp [add_div]       map_smul' := by simp [mul_div]       left_inv := fun w => by         apply_fun b.repr using b.repr.toEquiv.injective         apply_fun Equiv.finsuppUnique         simp only [LinearEquiv.map_smulₛₗ, Finsupp.coe_smul, Finsupp.single_eq_same,           smul_eq_mul, Pi.smul_apply, Equiv.finsuppUnique_apply]         exact div_mul_cancel₀ _ h       right_inv := fun f => by         ext         simp only [LinearEquiv.map_smulₛₗ, Finsupp.coe_smul, Finsupp.single_eq_same,           RingHom.id_apply, smul_eq_mul, Pi.smul_apply]         exact mul_div_cancel_right₀ _ h }

explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.

explanatories.Finset.sup_induction: This theorem establishes that if a property holds for the supremum of a set of function values and the property is preserved under taking suprema, then it also holds for the overall supremum of those function values.
explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.

Module.End.eigenspace.comment:
The submodule `eigenspace f μ` for a linear map `f` and a scalar `μ` consists of all vectors `x`
such that `f x = μ • x`. (Def 5.36 of [axler2015])

explanatories.LinearMap.ker: The kernel of a linear map is defined as the set of elements in the domain that are mapped to zero in the codomain, and it forms a submodule of the domain.
explanatories.algebraMap: This definition provides a ring homomorphism that represents the embedding of a commutative semiring into an algebra defined over that semiring.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ker: The kernel of a linear equivalence is trivial, meaning it contains only the zero element.

Module.End.eigenspace.description: This definition describes the eigenspace associated with a linear map and a scalar, comprising all vectors that are scaled by the scalar when the map is applied to them.

Module.End.genEigenspace.code:
Module.End.genEigenspace.{v, w} {R : Type v} {M : Type w} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f : End R M)
  (μ : R) : ℕ →o Submodule R M
Module.End.genEigenspace.comment:
The generalized eigenspace for a linear map `f`, a scalar `μ`, and an exponent `k ∈ ℕ` is the
kernel of `(f - μ • id) ^ k`. (Def 8.10 of [axler2015]). Furthermore, a generalized eigenspace for
some exponent `k` is contained in the generalized eigenspace for exponents larger than `k`.

explanatories.LinearMap.ker: The kernel of a linear map is defined as the set of elements in the domain that are mapped to zero in the codomain, and it forms a submodule of the domain.
explanatories.algebraMap: This definition provides a ring homomorphism that represents the embedding of a commutative semiring into an algebra defined over that semiring.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ker: The kernel of a linear equivalence is trivial, meaning it contains only the zero element.
explanatories.pow_sub_mul_pow: In a monoid, if one exponent is less than or equal to another, the product of the term raised to the difference of the exponents and the term raised to the smaller exponent equals the term raised to the larger exponent.
explanatories.LinearMap.ker_le_ker_comp: The kernel of a linear map is a subset of the kernel of the composition of that map with another linear map.

Module.End.genEigenspace.fullDefinition: def genEigenspace (f : End R M) (μ : R) : ℕ →o Submodule R M where   toFun k := LinearMap.ker ((f - algebraMap R (End R M) μ) ^ k)   monotone' k m hm := by     simp only [← pow_sub_mul_pow _ hm]     exact       LinearMap.ker_le_ker_comp ((f - algebraMap R (End R M) μ) ^ k)         ((f - algebraMap R (End R M) μ) ^ (m - k))
Module.End.genEigenspace.description: This definition describes the generalized eigenspace associated with a linear map and a given scalar as the kernel of a matrix raised to a power, indicating a hierarchy of generalized eigenspaces based on their exponent.

explanatories.Module.Dual.eval: This definition describes a linear map that associates each element of a module to its corresponding dual of the dual, effectively recovering an evaluation map between the module and its double dual.
explanatories.Finsupp.sum.eq_1: The sum of a function evaluated at a finitely supported function is equal to the sum of that function evaluated at each element in the support of the finitely supported function, weighted by its values.
explanatories.FiniteDimensional.eq_1: The equality between two ways of representing finite dimensionality for a vector space over a division ring is established, showing that a vector space is finitely dimensional if and only if it can be expressed as a module that is also finitely generated.
explanatories.Submodule.comap: This definition introduces the pullback of a submodule through a semilinear map, producing a corresponding submodule in the original space.
explanatories.Module.DualBases.lc.eq_1: The linear combination of a set of elements from a module, scaled by coefficients, is equal to the sum of these scaled elements as described by a given finite support function.
explanatories.Module.DualBases.eval: The evaluation of a dual basis with respect to a module produces a Kronecker delta function, which is equal to one if the indices are the same and zero otherwise.
explanatories.Submodule.dualAnnihilator: The dual annihilator of a submodule consists of all linear maps that evaluate to zero on every element of that submodule.
explanatories.Ne.eq_1: This theorem states that the inequality of two elements is equivalent to the negation of their equality.

Submodule.dualCoannihilator.eq_1.description: The dual coannihilator of a submodule in the dual space is shown to be equal to the pullback of its dual annihilator through the evaluation map.

Subspace.dualLift.comment:
Given a subspace `W` of `V` and an element of its dual `φ`, `dualLift W φ` is
an arbitrary extension of `φ` to an element of the dual of `V`.
That is, `dualLift W φ` sends `w ∈ W` to `φ x` and `x` in a chosen complement of `W` to `0`.

explanatories.LinearEquiv.dualMap: This definition establishes a linear equivalence between the dual spaces of two modules that are related by a linear isomorphism, allowing for the transformation of linear functionals from one dual space to the other.
explanatories.Classical.choose: The existence of an element satisfying a property guarantees the ability to select one such element.
explanatories.LinearMap.exists_leftInverse_of_injectiv: If a linear map between two vector spaces is injective, then there exists a left inverse linear map that composes with it to yield the identity map.
explanatories.Submodule.ker_subtype: The kernel of the subtype map associated with a submodule is trivial, meaning it only contains the zero element.

Submodule.dualCopairing.comment:
Given a submodule, corestrict to the pairing on `M ⧸ W` by
simultaneously restricting to `W.dualAnnihilator`.

See `Subspace.dualCopairing_nondegenerate`.

explanatories.Module.dualPairing: The canonical pairing between a vector space and its algebraic dual is represented as a linear map from the dual space to the space of linear maps from that vector space back to the ring.
explanatories.LinearMap.flip: This definition describes a process that takes a bilinear map and rearranges the order of its variables to form a new linear map.
explanatories.LinearMap.ext: This theorem states that if two linear maps agree on all inputs, then they are equal as functions.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Basis.ext: This theorem asserts that two linear maps are identical if they produce the same output for every basis vector.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.
explanatories.Subsingleton.intro: A type is a subsingleton if it can be shown that all of its elements are equal to each other.
explanatories.Submodule.dualAnnihilator: The dual annihilator of a submodule consists of all linear maps that evaluate to zero on every element of that submodule.
explanatories.Submodule.mem_dualAnnihilator: An element of the dual module belongs to the dual annihilator of a submodule if and only if it evaluates to zero for all elements of that submodule.
explanatories.Submodule.liftQ: This definition describes a linear map from the quotient of a module by a submodule to another module, induced by a linear transformation that vanishes on the submodule.
explanatories.LinearMap.domRestrict: This definition describes a linear map that restricts a given linear transformation from a module to a submodule.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.TensorProduct.ext: This theorem establishes that if two linear maps from the tensor product of two modules to a third module are equal when restricted through a specific construction, then the linear maps themselves must be identical.

Submodule.dualCopairing.fullDefinition: def dualCopairing (W : Submodule R M) : W.dualAnnihilator →ₗ[R] M ⧸ W →ₗ[R] R :=   LinearMap.flip <|     W.liftQ ((Module.dualPairing R M).domRestrict W.dualAnnihilator).flip       (by         intro w hw         ext ⟨φ, hφ⟩         exact (mem_dualAnnihilator φ).mp hφ w hw)
Submodule.dualCopairing.description: This definition describes a linear map that pairs functionals from the dual annihilator of a submodule with equivalence classes in the quotient of a module by that submodule, facilitating the interaction between the dual and quotient structures.

  (W : Submodule R M) : Dual R M ⧸ W.dualAnnihilator →ₗ[R] ↥W →ₗ[R] R
Submodule.dualPairing.comment:
Given a submodule, restrict to the pairing on `W` by
simultaneously corestricting to `Module.Dual R M ⧸ W.dualAnnihilator`.
This is `Submodule.dualRestrict` factored through the quotient by its kernel (which
is `W.dualAnnihilator` by definition).

See `Subspace.dualPairing_nondegenerate`.

explanatories.Submodule.dualRestrict: This defines a linear map that restricts the dual space of a module to the dual space of a specified submodule.
explanatories.Submodule.dualAnnihilator: The dual annihilator of a submodule consists of all linear maps that evaluate to zero on every element of that submodule.
explanatories.Submodule.liftQ: This definition describes a linear map from the quotient of a module by a submodule to another module, induced by a linear transformation that vanishes on the submodule.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.

Submodule.dualPairing.fullDefinition: def dualPairing (W : Submodule R M) : Module.Dual R M ⧸ W.dualAnnihilator →ₗ[R] W →ₗ[R] R :=   W.dualAnnihilator.liftQ W.dualRestrict le_rfl
Submodule.dualPairing.description: The dual pairing for a submodule constructs a linear map from the quotient of the dual space by its dual annihilator to the submodule itself, facilitating the evaluation of linear functionals on that submodule.

submodule.dual_pairing.code:
Submodule.dualPairing.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
  (W : Submodule R M) : Dual R M ⧸ W.dualAnnihilator →ₗ[R] ↥W →ₗ[R] R
submodule.dual_pairing.comment:
Given a submodule, restrict to the pairing on `W` by
simultaneously corestricting to `Module.Dual R M ⧸ W.dualAnnihilator`.
This is `Submodule.dualRestrict` factored through the quotient by its kernel (which
is `W.dualAnnihilator` by definition).

See `Subspace.dualPairing_nondegenerate`.

Submodule.dualQuotEquivDualAnnihilator.code:
Submodule.dualQuotEquivDualAnnihilator.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M]
  [Module R M] (W : Submodule R M) : Dual R (M ⧸ W) ≃ₗ[R] ↥W.dualAnnihilator
Submodule.dualQuotEquivDualAnnihilator.comment:
Equivalence $(M/W)^* \cong \operatorname{ann}(W)$. That is, there is a one-to-one
correspondence between the dual of `M ⧸ W` and those elements of the dual of `M` that
vanish on `W`.

The inverse of this is `Submodule.dualCopairing`.

TensorProduct.dualDistribInvOfBasis.fullDefinition: noncomputable def dualDistribInvOfBasis (b : Basis ι R M) (c : Basis κ R N) :     Dual R (M ⊗[R] N) →ₗ[R] Dual R M ⊗[R] Dual R N :=   -- Porting note: ∑ (i) (j) does not seem to work; applyₗ needs a little help to unify   ∑ i, ∑ j,     (ringLmapEquivSelf R ℕ _).symm (b.dualBasis i ⊗ₜ c.dualBasis j) ∘ₗ       (applyₗ (R := R) (c j)) ∘ₗ (applyₗ (R := R) (b i)) ∘ₗ lcurry R M N R

LinearMap.detAux.comment:
The determinant of an endomorphism given a basis.

See `LinearMap.det` for a version that populates the basis non-computably.

Although the `Trunc (Basis ι A M)` parameter makes it slightly more convenient to switch bases,
there is no good way to generalize over universe parameters, so we can't fully state in `detAux`'s
type that it does not depend on the choice of basis. Instead you can use the `detAux_def''` lemma,
or avoid mentioning a basis at all using `LinearMap.det`.

LinearEquiv.ofIsUnitDet.fullDefinition: def LinearEquiv.ofIsUnitDet {f : M →ₗ[R] M'} {v : Basis ι R M} {v' : Basis ι R M'}     (h : IsUnit (LinearMap.toMatrix v v' f).det) : M ≃ₗ[R] M' where   toFun := f   map_add' := f.map_add   map_smul' := f.map_smul   invFun := toLin v' v (toMatrix v v' f)⁻¹   left_inv x :=     calc toLin v' v (toMatrix v v' f)⁻¹ (f x)       _ = toLin v v ((toMatrix v v' f)⁻¹ * toMatrix v v' f) x := by         rw [toLin_mul v v' v, toLin_toMatrix, LinearMap.comp_apply]       _ = x := by simp [h]   right_inv x :=     calc f (toLin v' v (toMatrix v v' f)⁻¹ x)       _ = toLin v' v' (toMatrix v v' f * (toMatrix v v' f)⁻¹) x := by         rw [toLin_mul v' v v', LinearMap.comp_apply, toLin_toMatrix v v']       _ = x := by simp [h]

explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm: This definition specifies the symmetry of linear equivalences, indicating that the inverse relationship between two modules can be expressed as a linear equivalence in the opposite direction.
explanatories.Matrix.det: This defines the determinant of a matrix using the Leibniz formula, which involves summing products of matrix entries corresponding to permutations of rows.
explanatories.LinearMap.toMatrix: This definition specifies a linear equivalence between linear maps from one module to another and matrices formed over a commutative ring, given specific bases for the modules.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.LinearMap.det: This definition introduces a function that calculates the determinant of a linear endomorphism, yielding a value that is independent of the choice of basis and defaults to one when there is no finite basis available.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear equivalence preserves scalar multiplication when applied to elements of two modules over the same semiring.
explanatories.MulEquiv.symm: The inverse of a multiplicative isomorphism is itself a multiplicative isomorphism between the two types.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.det: This definition describes a method for calculating the determinant of a linear equivalence, resulting in a unit in the underlying ring.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear map commutes with scalar multiplication, meaning that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is the same as multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar.
explanatories.Basis.toMatrix: The definition constructs a matrix whose columns are composed of vectors expressed in terms of a given basis.
explanatories.Subsingleton.elim: In a subsingleton type, any two elements are equal, demonstrating the uniqueness of elements in such types.
explanatories.Basis.toMatrix_update: This theorem states that updating a vector in a basis results in a corresponding update to the matrix representation of that vector by modifying a specific column with the representation of the new value.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.map_add: This theorem states that a linear equivalence preserves the addition of elements from one module when mapped to another module.
explanatories.Finsupp.coe_add: This theorem states that the function corresponding to the sum of two finitely supported functions is equal to the sum of the functions corresponding to each individual finitely supported function.
explanatories.Matrix.det_updateColumn_add: This theorem establishes that the determinant of a matrix, when a column is updated with the sum of two vectors, is equal to the sum of the determinants obtained by updating the same column with each vector separately.
explanatories.Basis.repr: This definition establishes a linear equivalence that maps a vector to its coordinates with respect to a given basis.
explanatories.Algebra.id.smul_eq_mul: This theorem establishes that scalar multiplication by an element in a commutative semiring is equivalent to the usual multiplication of that element with another element from the same semiring.
explanatories.Matrix.det_updateColumn_smul: This theorem states that when a column of a matrix is multiplied by a scalar and updated, the determinant of the resulting matrix is equal to that scalar multiplied by the determinant of the matrix with the original column updated.
explanatories.Function.update_eq_self: This is an empty statement with no content to convey.
explanatories.Matrix.det_transpose: This theorem states that the determinant of a matrix remains unchanged when the matrix is transposed.
explanatories.Matrix.updateRow_transpose: This theorem states that updating a specific row of a transposed matrix is equivalent to transposing the result of updating the corresponding column in the original matrix.
explanatories.Basis.toMatrix_transpose_apply: This theorem asserts that the transpose of a matrix constructed from a basis and a set of vectors evaluates at a specific index to the representation of the corresponding vector in that basis.
explanatories.Matrix.det_zero_of_row_eq: This theorem asserts that the determinant of a matrix is zero if it has two equal rows.
explanatories.Matrix.updateRow_ne: This theorem asserts that updating a specified row of a matrix with a new vector does not affect other rows when the updated row is different from the specified one.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.Matrix.updateRow_self: This theorem states that updating a specific row of a matrix with a new vector at that same row index results in the new vector itself.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.

Basis.det.fullDefinition: nonrec def Basis.det : M [⋀^ι]→ₗ[R] R where   toFun v := det (e.toMatrix v)   map_add' := by     intro inst v i x y     cases Subsingleton.elim inst ‹_›     simp only [e.toMatrix_update, LinearEquiv.map_add, Finsupp.coe_add]     -- Porting note: was `exact det_update_column_add _ _ _ _`     convert det_updateColumn_add (e.toMatrix v) i (e.repr x) (e.repr y)   map_smul' := by     intro inst u i c x     cases Subsingleton.elim inst ‹_›     simp only [e.toMatrix_update, Algebra.id.smul_eq_mul, LinearEquiv.map_smul]     -- Porting note: was `apply det_update_column_smul`     convert det_updateColumn_smul (e.toMatrix u) i c (e.repr x)   map_eq_zero_of_eq' := by     intro v i j h hij     -- Porting note: added     simp only     rw [← Function.update_eq_self i v, h, ← det_transpose, e.toMatrix_update, ← updateRow_transpose,       ← e.toMatrix_transpose_apply]     apply det_zero_of_row_eq hij     rw [updateRow_ne hij.symm, updateRow_self]

Module.preReflection.code:
Module.preReflection.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (x : M)
  (f : Dual R M) : End R M
Module.preReflection.comment:
Given an element `x` in a module `M` and a linear form `f` on `M`, we define the endomorphism
of `M` for which `y ↦ y - (f y) • x`.

One is typically interested in this endomorphism when `f x = 2`; this definition exists to allow the
user defer discharging this proof obligation. See also `Module.reflection`.

explanatories.Module.End: This definition describes the type of linear endomorphisms of a module that have an associated ring structure.
explanatories.LinearMap.id: This definition specifies the identity linear map for a module over a semiring that maps each element to itself.
explanatories.LinearMap.smulRight: This definition specifies how to construct a new linear map by taking an existing linear map and associating it with a fixed element, such that the output of the new map scales with that element's scalar multiplication.
explanatories.RingHom.id: This definition describes the identity ring homomorphism that maps each element of a semiring to itself.

Module.preReflection.fullDefinition: def preReflection : End R M :=   LinearMap.id - f.smulRight x
Module.preReflection.description: This defines an endomorphism of a module that adjusts elements by subtracting the product of a linear form evaluated at the element and a specified vector.

Module.preReflection_apply.code:
Module.preReflection_apply.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (x : M)
  (f : Dual R M) (y : M) : (preReflection x f) y = y - f y • x

explanatories.Module.Dual: The dual space of an R-module is defined as the set of all linear maps from that module to the ring R, forming an R-module itself.

Module.preReflection_apply.description: The application of the defined endomorphism to any element results in that element being decreased by the product of the linear form applied to it and a specified vector.

  {x : M} {f : Dual R M} (h : f x = 2) : Involutive ⇑(preReflection x f)

explanatories.Module.Dual: The dual space of an R-module is defined as the set of all linear maps from that module to the ring R, forming an R-module itself.
explanatories.Function.Involutive: A function is considered involutive if applying it twice yields the identity function, effectively reverting to the original input.

Module.involutive_preReflection.description: The defined endomorphism is involutive when the linear form applied to a specified vector equals two.

Module.reflection.code:
Module.reflection.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {x : M}
  {f : Dual R M} (h : f x = 2) : M ≃ₗ[R] M
Module.reflection.comment:
Given an element `x` in a module `M` and a linear form `f` on `M` for which `f x = 2`, we define
the endomorphism of `M` for which `y ↦ y - (f y) • x`.

It is an involutive endomorphism of `M` fixing the kernel of `f` for which `x ↦ -x`.

explanatories.Module.preReflection: This defines an endomorphism of a module that adjusts elements by subtracting the product of a linear form evaluated at the element and a specified vector.
explanatories.Module.involutive_preReflection: The defined endomorphism is involutive when the linear form applied to a specified vector equals two.
explanatories.Function.Involutive.toPerm: This definition describes a method to convert an involutive function into a permutation that has the function itself as both the forward and inverse mappings.

Module.reflection.fullDefinition: def reflection (h : f x = 2) : M ≃ₗ[R] M :=   { preReflection x f, (involutive_preReflection h).toPerm with }
Module.reflection.description: This defines a linear isomorphism on a module that represents an involutive transformation with respect to a specific vector and linear form, while fixing the elements where the linear form evaluates to zero.

Module.Dual.eq_of_preReflection_mapsTo.comment:
See also `Module.Dual.eq_of_preReflection_mapsTo'` for a variant of this lemma which
applies when `Φ` does not span.

This rather technical-looking lemma exists because it is exactly what is needed to establish various
uniqueness results for root data / systems. One might regard this lemma as lying at the boundary of
linear algebra and combinatorics since the finiteness assumption is the key.

explanatories.LinearMap.coe_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the function corresponding to the composition of two linear maps is equivalent to the composition of their respective functions.

explanatories.TensorProduct.mk_apply: This theorem asserts that the application of the tensor product to two elements from distinct modules corresponds to their associated representation in a specific tensor product construction.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear map commutes with scalar multiplication, meaning that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is the same as multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ofLinear: This definition states that a pair of linear maps that are inverses of each other form a linear equivalence between two modules over different semirings.
explanatories.TensorProduct.mk: This definition describes a canonical bilinear map that takes an element from one module and another from a second module and produces an element in their tensor product.

explanatories.LinearMap.coeFn_sum: This theorem asserts that the function associated with the sum of a set of linear maps applied to a module element is equivalent to the sum of the functions applied individually to that element.
explanatories.LinearMap.id_coe: This theorem shows that the identity linear map is equivalent to the usual identity function when viewed as a function from a module over a semiring.

explanatories.Fintype.sum_apply: The sum of a function's values over a finite type is equal to the sum obtained by evaluating the function for a specific argument across the same finite type.

explanatories.TensorProduct.smul_tmul': This theorem demonstrates that scaling an element from one module before taking its tensor product with an element from another module is equivalent to taking the tensor product first and then scaling, provided both modules are appropriately structured.
explanatories.TensorProduct.sum_tmul: This theorem establishes that the tensor product of a sum of elements from a module with an element from another module is equal to the sum of the tensor products of each individual element with that element.

RootPairing.root.fullDefinition: root : ι ↪ M   /-- A parametrized family of dual vectors, called coroots. -/   coroot : ι ↪ N   root_coroot_two : ∀ i, toLin (root i) (coroot i) = 2   /-- A parametrized family of permutations, induced by reflection. -/   reflection_perm : ι → (ι ≃ ι)   reflection_perm_root : ∀ i j,     root j - toLin (root j) (coroot i) • root i = root (reflection_perm i j)   reflection_perm_coroot : ∀ i j,     coroot j - toLin (root i) (coroot j) • coroot i = coroot (reflection_perm i j)
RootPairing.root.description: This definition establishes a collection of vectors, referred to as roots, that are associated with a given parameter.

RootPairing.injOn_dualMap_subtype_span_r.code:
RootPairing.injOn_dualMap_subtype_span_root_coroot.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3}
  {N : Type u_4} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [_root_.Finite ι]
  (P : RootPairing ι R M N) [NoZeroSMulDivisors ℤ M] :
  InjOn (⇑((span R (range ⇑P.root)).subtype.dualMap ∘ₗ P.toLin.flip)) (range ⇑P.coroot)
RootPairing.injOn_dualMap_subtype_span_r.comment:
Even though the roots may not span, coroots are distinguished by their pairing with the
roots. The proof depends crucially on the fact that there are finitely-many roots.

Modulo trivial generalisations, this statement is exactly Lemma 1.1.4 on page 87 of SGA 3 XXI.

explanatories.RootPairing.root_coroot_two: The theorem states that the linear transformation of the root vector associated with a parameter, when applied to the corresponding coroot vector, equals two.
explanatories.RootPairing.reflection_perm: This definition introduces a collection of permutations that are parameterized and induced by reflection.
explanatories.LinearMap.flip_apply: This theorem establishes that applying a flipped linear map to a pair of inputs yields the same result as first applying the original map to one input and then the result to the other input.
explanatories.Module.preReflection_apply: The application of the defined endomorphism to any element results in that element being decreased by the product of the linear form applied to it and a specified vector.
explanatories.RootPairing.equiv_of_mapsTo: This definition establishes a bijective correspondence on the indexing set that arises from the reflection process associated with a perfect pairing.
explanatories.RootPairing.equiv_of_mapsTo_apply: This theorem demonstrates the application of a bijection derived from reflection to establish a specific relationship between elements in the indexing set, represented by a chosen index.
explanatories._private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli: This theorem establishes that if a specific relation holds for roots under a bilinear pairing, then a corresponding relation holds for coroots under a dual transformation.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.

RootPairing.mk'.fullDefinition: def mk' [Finite ι] [CharZero R] [NoZeroSMulDivisors R M]     (p : PerfectPairing R M N)     (root : ι ↪ M)     (coroot : ι ↪ N)     (hp : ∀ i, p.toLin (root i) (coroot i) = 2)     (hr : ∀ i, MapsTo (preReflection (root i) (p.toLin.flip (coroot i))) (range root) (range root))     (hc : ∀ i, MapsTo (preReflection (coroot i) (p.toLin (root i))) (range coroot) (range coroot)) :     RootPairing ι R M N where   toPerfectPairing := p   root := root   coroot := coroot   root_coroot_two := hp   reflection_perm i := RootPairing.equiv_of_mapsTo p root coroot i hr hp   reflection_perm_root i j := by     rw [equiv_of_mapsTo_apply, (exist_eq_reflection_of_mapsTo p root coroot i j hr).choose_spec,       preReflection_apply, LinearMap.flip_apply]   reflection_perm_coroot i j := by     refine (coroot_eq_coreflection_of_root_eq' p root coroot hp hr hc ?_).symm     rw [equiv_of_mapsTo_apply, (exist_eq_reflection_of_mapsTo p root coroot i j hr).choose_spec]
RootPairing.mk'.description: This definition specifies a structure for a root pairing given certain stability conditions under reflections for finite collections of roots and coroots in a module context over a commutative ring.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.code:
RootSystem.coroot_eq_coreflection_of_root_eq_of_span_eq_top.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2}
  {M : Type u_3} {N : Type u_4} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
  [_root_.Finite ι] [CharZero R] [NoZeroSMulDivisors R M] (p : PerfectPairing R M N) (root : ι ↪ M) (coroot : ι ↪ N)
  (hp : ∀ (i : ι), (p.toLin (root i)) (coroot i) = 2)
  (hs : ∀ (i : ι), MapsTo (⇑(preReflection (root i) (p.toLin.flip (coroot i)))) (range ⇑root) (range ⇑root))
  (hsp : span R (range ⇑root) = ⊤) {i j k : ι}
  (hk : root k = (preReflection (root i) (p.toLin.flip (coroot i))) (root j)) :
  coroot k = (preReflection (coroot i) (p.toLin (root i))) (coroot j)

coevaluation.code:
coevaluation.{u, v} (K : Type u) [Field K] (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] :
  K →ₗ[K] V ⊗[K] Module.Dual K V
coevaluation.comment:
The coevaluation map is a linear map from a field `K` to a finite dimensional
vector space `V`.

explanatories.Module.Dual: The dual space of an R-module is defined as the set of all linear maps from that module to the ring R, forming an R-module itself.
explanatories.Basis.ofVectorSpace: Every vector space has a basis consisting of linearly independent vectors indexed by a specific construction.
explanatories.Basis.singleton: This definition describes a basis that maps a unique element of a type to the scalar one in a specified semiring.
explanatories.Unit: This defines a type that contains exactly one value, used to indicate the absence of meaningful information.
explanatories.Basis.constr: This definition establishes a method to construct a linear map using the values assigned to a basis over an additional semiring, allowing for flexibility in the scalar multiplication structure.
explanatories.Basis.ofVectorSpaceIndex: A set is defined to serve as an index for the basis of a vector space.
explanatories.Basis.coord: This definition describes a linear function that returns the coordinate of a vector corresponding to a specific index in a given basis.

coevaluation.fullDefinition: def coevaluation : K →ₗ[K] V ⊗[K] Module.Dual K V :=   let bV := Basis.ofVectorSpace K V   (Basis.singleton Unit K).constr K fun _ =>     ∑ i : Basis.ofVectorSpaceIndex K V, bV i ⊗ₜ[K] bV.coord i
coevaluation.description: This definition introduces a linear map that connects elements of a field to a finite-dimensional vector space and its dual, constructed using the tensor product.

coevaluation_apply_one.code:
coevaluation_apply_one.{u, v} (K : Type u) [Field K] (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
  [FiniteDimensional K V] :
  (coevaluation K V) 1 =
    let bV := Basis.ofVectorSpace K V;
    ∑ i : ↑(Basis.ofVectorSpaceIndex K V), bV i ⊗ₜ[K] bV.coord i

explanatories.FiniteDimensional: This definition characterizes vector spaces as finite-dimensional if they can be understood as finite modules over a division ring.

explanatories.Basis.ofVectorSpaceIndex: A set is defined to serve as an index for the basis of a vector space.
explanatories.Basis.coord: This definition describes a linear function that returns the coordinate of a vector corresponding to a specific index in a given basis.

coevaluation_apply_one.description: This theorem asserts that applying the coevaluation map to the scalar one yields a sum involving the basis of the vector space and its corresponding coordinates.

contractLeft_assoc_coevaluation.code:
contractLeft_assoc_coevaluation.{u, v} (K : Type u) [Field K] (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
  [FiniteDimensional K V] :
  LinearMap.rTensor (Module.Dual K V) (contractLeft K V) ∘ₗ
      ↑(TensorProduct.assoc K (Module.Dual K V) V (Module.Dual K V)).symm ∘ₗ
        LinearMap.lTensor (Module.Dual K V) (coevaluation K V) =
    ↑(TensorProduct.lid K (Module.Dual K V)).symm ∘ₗ ↑(TensorProduct.rid K (Module.Dual K V))
contractLeft_assoc_coevaluation.comment:
This lemma corresponds to one of the coherence laws for duals in rigid categories, see
`CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Rigid`.

explanatories.FiniteDimensional: This definition characterizes vector spaces as finite-dimensional if they can be understood as finite modules over a division ring.
explanatories.Module.Dual: The dual space of an R-module is defined as the set of all linear maps from that module to the ring R, forming an R-module itself.
explanatories.LinearMap.rTensor: This definition describes a natural linear map that extends a linear transformation from one module to a tensor product with another module.
explanatories.TensorProduct.assoc: This definition asserts a linear equivalence between the tensor product of two tensor products and the tensor product of all three given modules, reflecting the associative property in the context of module operations.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm: This definition specifies the symmetry of linear equivalences, indicating that the inverse relationship between two modules can be expressed as a linear equivalence in the opposite direction.
explanatories.LinearMap.lTensor: This definition describes a natural linear map that takes a tensor product of one module with another and produces a tensor product with a third module, guided by a specified linear map.
explanatories.TensorProduct.lid: This definition establishes that the tensor product of the base ring with a module is linearly equivalent to the module itself, effectively treating the base ring as a left identity in this context.
explanatories.TensorProduct.rid: This definition establishes a linear isomorphism that identifies the tensor product of a module with the base ring as being equivalent to the original module itself.

contractLeft_assoc_coevaluation.description: This theorem establishes a relationship between various linear maps and tensor product identities within the context of finite-dimensional vector spaces and their duals, reflecting coherence in rigid categories.

Lagrange.basisDivisor.code: Lagrange.basisDivisor.{u_1} {F : Type u_1} [Field F] (x y : F) : F[X]
Lagrange.basisDivisor.comment:
`basisDivisor x y` is the unique linear or constant polynomial such that
when evaluated at `x` it gives `1` and `y` it gives `0` (where when `x = y` it is identically `0`).
Such polynomials are the building blocks for the Lagrange interpolants.

explanatories.Polynomial.C: This definition specifies a ring homomorphism that maps a constant from a semiring to the corresponding constant polynomial in a polynomial ring.
explanatories.Polynomial.X: This definition introduces the polynomial variable, also known as the indeterminate, for polynomials over a semiring.

Lagrange.basisDivisor.fullDefinition: def basisDivisor (x y : F) : F[X] :=   C (x - y)⁻¹ * (X - C y)
Lagrange.basisDivisor.description: The basis divisor is the unique linear or constant polynomial that equals one at a specific point and zero at another, serving as a fundamental component for constructing Lagrange interpolants.

  {s : Finset ι} {i j : ι} {v : ι → F} (r : ι → F) (hvs : Set.InjOn v ↑s) (hi : i ∈ s) (hj : j ∈ s) (hij : i ≠ j) :

Lagrange.nodal.code: Lagrange.nodal.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] {ι : Type u_2} (s : Finset ι) (v : ι → R) : R[X]
Lagrange.nodal.comment:
`nodal s v` is the unique monic polynomial whose roots are the nodes defined by `v` and `s`.

That is, the roots of `nodal s v` are exactly the image of `v` on `s`,
with appropriate multiplicity.

We can use `nodal` to define the barycentric forms of the evaluated interpolant.

lagrange.nodal.comment:
`nodal s v` is the unique monic polynomial whose roots are the nodes defined by `v` and `s`.

That is, the roots of `nodal s v` are exactly the image of `v` on `s`,
with appropriate multiplicity.

We can use `nodal` to define the barycentric forms of the evaluated interpolant.

Submodule.LinearDisjoint.linearIndepende.code:

  {m : κ → ↥M} {n : ι → ↥N} (hm : LinearIndependent R m) (hn : LinearIndependent R n) :
  LinearIndependent R fun i => ↑(m i.1) * ↑(n i.2)
Submodule.LinearDisjoint.linearIndepende.comment:
If `M` and `N` are linearly disjoint, if `M` is flat, then for any family of
`R`-linearly independent elements `{ m_i }` of `M`, and any family of
`R`-linearly independent elements `{ n_j }` of `N`, the family `{ m_i * n_j }` in `S` is
also `R`-linearly independent.

explanatories.LinearIndependent: This definition characterizes a family of vectors as linearly independent over a specified ring if no vector in the family can be expressed as a linear combination of the others.

Submodule.LinearDisjoint.linearIndepende.description: If two submodules are linearly disjoint and one is flat, then the product of any families of linearly independent elements from each submodule is also linearly independent.

Submodule.LinearDisjoint.of_basis_mul'.description: If two submodules each have a basis such that the products of their basis elements form a linearly independent family, then the submodules are linearly disjoint.

QuadraticMap.polar.code: QuadraticMap.polar.{u_4, u_5} {M : Type u_4} {N : Type u_5} [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N] (f : M → N) (x y : M) : N
QuadraticMap.polar.comment:
Up to a factor 2, `Q.polar` is the associated bilinear map for a quadratic map `Q`.

Source of this name: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadratic_form#Generalization
QuadraticMap.polar.fullDefinition: def polar (f : M → N) (x y : M) :=   f (x + y) - f x - f y

explanatories.QuadraticMap.polar: This definition describes a bilinear map associated with a quadratic map, which takes two elements from one additive group and produces an element in another additive group.
explanatories.sub_sub: In a commutative subtraction monoid, subtracting a second element and then a third from a first element is the same as subtracting the sum of the second and third elements from the first element.
explanatories.QuadraticMap.polar_comm: This theorem establishes that the bilinear map associated with a function is symmetric, meaning it produces the same result regardless of the order of its two arguments.
explanatories.QuadraticMap.toFun: This definition describes a function that converts a quadratic map into a regular mapping from one module to another over a commutative semiring.
explanatories.CoeFun.mk: A function that facilitates the conversion of types into a function type is established within a specific type construction tailored for coerced functions.

QuadraticMap.associatedHom.comment:
`associatedHom` is the map that sends a quadratic map on a module `M` over `R` to its
associated symmetric bilinear map.  As provided here, this has the structure of an `S`-linear map
where `S` is a commutative subring of `R`.

Over a commutative ring, use `QuadraticMap.associated`, which gives an `R`-linear map.  Over a
general ring with no nontrivial distinguished commutative subring, use `QuadraticMap.associated'`,
which gives an additive homomorphism (or more precisely a `ℤ`-linear map.)

explanatories.QuadraticMap.polar_smul: This theorem shows that scaling the function by a scalar results in scaling the associated bilinear map by the same scalar.

explanatories.LinearMap.ext₂: This theorem states that if two linear maps yield the same output for all input pairs, then they are equal as maps.
explanatories.Submonoid.center: The center of a multiplicative monoid is defined as the subset of elements that commute with every element in that monoid.

(⟨⅟2, Set.invOf_mem_center (Set.ofNat_mem_center _ _)⟩ : Submonoid.center R) •     { toFun := polarBilin       map_add' := fun _x _y => LinearMap.ext₂ <| polar_add _ _       map_smul' := fun _c _x => LinearMap.ext₂ <| polar_smul _ _ }

QuadraticForm.tensorDistrib.description: This definition establishes a linear map from the tensor product of two quadratic forms into a quadratic form defined on the tensor product of their respective modules, allowing for a larger coefficient ring on one side of the operation.

explanatories.SignType.sign: This definition establishes a function that assigns a sign value of one for positive elements, negative one for negative elements, and zero for all other values.

explanatories.QuadraticMap.basisRepr_apply: This theorem states that the representation of a quadratic map in terms of a basis applied to a weighted sum of basis elements is equal to the quadratic map applied to that same sum.
explanatories.Basis.unitsSMul_apply: This theorem demonstrates that applying a scalar multiplication from a unit in the ring to the basis vector results in the same value as using the corresponding entry from the unit function multiplied by the basis vector.
explanatories.sq: This theorem asserts that squaring an element in a monoid is equivalent to multiplying the element by itself.
explanatories.mul_pow: In a commutative monoid, the power of a product of two elements equals the product of their individual powers.
explanatories.Finset.sum_congr: If two finite sets are equal and their corresponding functions yield the same values for all elements, then the sums of those function values over the sets are also equal.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.

QuadraticForm.isometryEquivSignWeightedS.fullDefinition: noncomputable def isometryEquivSignWeightedSumSquares (w : ι → ℝ) :     IsometryEquiv (weightedSumSquares ℝ w)       (weightedSumSquares ℝ (fun i ↦ (sign (w i) : ℝ))) := by   let u i := if h : w i = 0 then (1 : ℝˣ) else Units.mk0 (w i) h   have hu : ∀ i : ι, 1 / √|(u i : ℝ)| ≠ 0 := fun i ↦     have : (u i : ℝ) ≠ 0 := (u i).ne_zero     by positivity   have hwu : ∀ i, w i / |(u i : ℝ)| = sign (w i) := fun i ↦ by     by_cases hi : w i = 0 <;> field_simp [hi, u]   convert QuadraticForm.isometryEquivBasisRepr (weightedSumSquares ℝ w)     ((Pi.basisFun ℝ ι).unitsSMul fun i => .mk0 _ (hu i))   ext1 v   classical   suffices ∑ i, (w i / |(u i : ℝ)|) * v i ^ 2 = ∑ i, w i * (v i ^ 2 * |(u i : ℝ)|⁻¹) by     simpa [basisRepr_apply, Basis.unitsSMul_apply, ← _root_.sq, mul_pow, ← hwu]   exact sum_congr rfl fun j _ ↦ by ring
QuadraticForm.isometryEquivSignWeightedS.description: This definition establishes an isometry between the weighted sum of squares based on a set of weights and the weighted sum of squares based on the signs of those weights.

QuadraticForm.isometryEquivSumSquares.fullDefinition: noncomputable def isometryEquivSumSquares (w' : ι → ℂ) :     IsometryEquiv (weightedSumSquares ℂ w')       (weightedSumSquares ℂ (fun i => if w' i = 0 then 0 else 1 : ι → ℂ)) := by   let w i := if h : w' i = 0 then (1 : Units ℂ) else Units.mk0 (w' i) h   have hw' : ∀ i : ι, (w i : ℂ) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℂ)) ≠ 0 := by     intro i hi     exact (w i).ne_zero ((Complex.cpow_eq_zero_iff _ _).1 hi).1   convert QuadraticForm.isometryEquivBasisRepr (weightedSumSquares ℂ w')     ((Pi.basisFun ℂ ι).unitsSMul fun i => (isUnit_iff_ne_zero.2 <| hw' i).unit)   ext1 v   erw [basisRepr_apply, weightedSumSquares_apply, weightedSumSquares_apply]   refine sum_congr rfl fun j hj => ?_   have hsum : (∑ i : ι, v i • ((isUnit_iff_ne_zero.2 <| hw' i).unit : ℂ) • (Pi.basisFun ℂ ι) i) j =       v j • w j ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℂ)) := by     classical     rw [Finset.sum_apply, sum_eq_single j, Pi.basisFun_apply, IsUnit.unit_spec,       LinearMap.stdBasis_apply, Pi.smul_apply, Pi.smul_apply, Function.update_same, smul_eq_mul,       smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]     · intro i _ hij       rw [Pi.basisFun_apply, LinearMap.stdBasis_apply, Pi.smul_apply, Pi.smul_apply,         Function.update_noteq hij.symm, Pi.zero_apply, smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul,         mul_zero, mul_zero]     intro hj'; exact False.elim (hj' hj)   simp_rw [Basis.unitsSMul_apply]   erw [hsum, smul_eq_mul]   split_ifs with h   · simp only [h, zero_smul, zero_mul]   have hww' : w' j = w j := by simp only [w, dif_neg h, Units.val_mk0]   simp (config := {zeta := false}) only [one_mul, Units.val_mk0, smul_eq_mul]   rw [hww']   suffices v j * v j = w j ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℂ)) * w j ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℂ)) * w j * v j * v j by     rw [this]; ring   rw [← Complex.cpow_add _ _ (w j).ne_zero, show -(1 / 2 : ℂ) + -(1 / 2) = -1 by simp [← two_mul],     Complex.cpow_neg_one, inv_mul_cancel (w j).ne_zero, one_mul]

explanatories.zero_smul: This theorem confirms that scalar multiplication of any element by zero yields zero within a structure that supports scalar multiplication with zero.

explanatories.two_mul: This theorem demonstrates that multiplying an element by two in a non-associative semiring is equivalent to adding the element to itself.
explanatories.Complex.cpow_neg_one: The theorem asserts that raising a complex number to the power of negative one is equivalent to taking its reciprocal.
explanatories.inv_mul_cancel: This theorem asserts that in a group with zero, the product of a nonzero element and its inverse equals one.

quadratic_form.isometry_sum_squares.fullDefinition: noncomputable def isometryEquivSumSquares (w' : ι → ℂ) :     IsometryEquiv (weightedSumSquares ℂ w')       (weightedSumSquares ℂ (fun i => if w' i = 0 then 0 else 1 : ι → ℂ)) := by   let w i := if h : w' i = 0 then (1 : Units ℂ) else Units.mk0 (w' i) h   have hw' : ∀ i : ι, (w i : ℂ) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℂ)) ≠ 0 := by     intro i hi     exact (w i).ne_zero ((Complex.cpow_eq_zero_iff _ _).1 hi).1   convert QuadraticForm.isometryEquivBasisRepr (weightedSumSquares ℂ w')     ((Pi.basisFun ℂ ι).unitsSMul fun i => (isUnit_iff_ne_zero.2 <| hw' i).unit)   ext1 v   erw [basisRepr_apply, weightedSumSquares_apply, weightedSumSquares_apply]   refine sum_congr rfl fun j hj => ?_   have hsum : (∑ i : ι, v i • ((isUnit_iff_ne_zero.2 <| hw' i).unit : ℂ) • (Pi.basisFun ℂ ι) i) j =       v j • w j ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℂ)) := by     classical     rw [Finset.sum_apply, sum_eq_single j, Pi.basisFun_apply, IsUnit.unit_spec,       LinearMap.stdBasis_apply, Pi.smul_apply, Pi.smul_apply, Function.update_same, smul_eq_mul,       smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul, mul_one]     · intro i _ hij       rw [Pi.basisFun_apply, LinearMap.stdBasis_apply, Pi.smul_apply, Pi.smul_apply,         Function.update_noteq hij.symm, Pi.zero_apply, smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul,         mul_zero, mul_zero]     intro hj'; exact False.elim (hj' hj)   simp_rw [Basis.unitsSMul_apply]   erw [hsum, smul_eq_mul]   split_ifs with h   · simp only [h, zero_smul, zero_mul]   have hww' : w' j = w j := by simp only [w, dif_neg h, Units.val_mk0]   simp (config := {zeta := false}) only [one_mul, Units.val_mk0, smul_eq_mul]   rw [hww']   suffices v j * v j = w j ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℂ)) * w j ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℂ)) * w j * v j * v j by     rw [this]; ring   rw [← Complex.cpow_add _ _ (w j).ne_zero, show -(1 / 2 : ℂ) + -(1 / 2) = -1 by simp [← two_mul],     Complex.cpow_neg_one, inv_mul_cancel (w j).ne_zero, one_mul]

clifford_algebra.lift.code:
CliffordAlgebra.lift.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] {M : Type u_2} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
  (Q : QuadraticForm R M) {A : Type u_3} [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] :
  { f // ∀ (m : M), f m * f m = (algebraMap R A) (Q m) } ≃ (CliffordAlgebra Q →ₐ[R] A)
clifford_algebra.lift.comment:
Given a linear map `f : M →ₗ[R] A` into an `R`-algebra `A`, which satisfies the condition:
`cond : ∀ m : M, f m * f m = Q(m)`, this is the canonical lift of `f` to a morphism of `R`-algebras
from `CliffordAlgebra Q` to `A`.

explanatories.DirectSum.coeAlgHom_of: This theorem asserts that the canonical homomorphism associated with a graded structure and a specific index acts as the identity on elements of the graded component at that index.

CliffordAlgebra.gradedAlgebra.fullDefinition: instance gradedAlgebra : GradedAlgebra (evenOdd Q) :=   GradedAlgebra.ofAlgHom (evenOdd Q)     -- while not necessary, the `by apply` makes this elaborate faster     (lift Q ⟨by apply GradedAlgebra.ι Q, by apply GradedAlgebra.ι_sq_scalar Q⟩)     -- the proof from here onward is mostly similar to the `TensorAlgebra` case, with some extra     -- handling for the `iSup` in `evenOdd`.   (Q : QuadraticForm R M) (n : ZMod 2) {motive : (x : CliffordAlgebra Q) → x ∈ evenOdd Q n → Prop}
  (range_ι_pow : ∀ (v : CliffordAlgebra Q) (h : v ∈ LinearMap.range (ι Q) ^ n.val), motive v ⋯)
  (add :
    ∀ (x y : CliffordAlgebra Q) (hx : x ∈ evenOdd Q n) (hy : y ∈ evenOdd Q n),
      motive x hx → motive y hy → motive (x + y) ⋯)
  (ι_mul_ι_mul :
    ∀ (m₁ m₂ : M) (x : CliffordAlgebra Q) (hx : x ∈ evenOdd Q n), motive x hx → motive ((ι Q) m₁ * (ι Q) m₂ * x) ⋯)
  (x : CliffordAlgebra Q) (hx : x ∈ evenOdd Q n) : motive x hx
CliffordAlgebra.evenOdd_induction.comment:

CliffordAlgebra.ofProd.fullDefinition: def ofProd : CliffordAlgebra (Q₁.prod Q₂) →ₐ[R] (evenOdd Q₁ ᵍ⊗[R] evenOdd Q₂) :=   lift _ ⟨     LinearMap.coprod       ((GradedTensorProduct.includeLeft (evenOdd Q₁) (evenOdd Q₂)).toLinearMap           ∘ₗ (evenOdd Q₁ 1).subtype ∘ₗ (ι Q₁).codRestrict _ (ι_mem_evenOdd_one Q₁))       ((GradedTensorProduct.includeRight (evenOdd Q₁) (evenOdd Q₂)).toLinearMap           ∘ₗ (evenOdd Q₂ 1).subtype ∘ₗ (ι Q₂).codRestrict _ (ι_mem_evenOdd_one Q₂)),     fun m => by       simp_rw [LinearMap.coprod_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply,         AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply, QuadraticForm.prod_apply, Submodule.coeSubtype,         GradedTensorProduct.includeLeft_apply, GradedTensorProduct.includeRight_apply, map_add,         add_mul, mul_add, GradedTensorProduct.algebraMap_def,         GradedTensorProduct.tmul_one_mul_one_tmul, GradedTensorProduct.tmul_one_mul_coe_tmul,         GradedTensorProduct.tmul_coe_mul_one_tmul, GradedTensorProduct.tmul_coe_mul_coe_tmul,         LinearMap.codRestrict_apply, one_mul, uzpow_one, Units.neg_smul, one_smul, ι_sq_scalar,         mul_one, ← GradedTensorProduct.algebraMap_def, ← GradedTensorProduct.algebraMap_def']       abel⟩

              (evenOdd Q₁ 1).subtype ∘ₗ LinearMap.codRestrict (evenOdd Q₁ 1) (ι Q₁) ⋯).coprod
          ((GradedTensorProduct.includeRight (evenOdd Q₁) (evenOdd Q₂)).toLinearMap ∘ₗ
            (evenOdd Q₂ 1).subtype ∘ₗ LinearMap.codRestrict (evenOdd Q₂ 1) (ι Q₂) ⋯),
        ⋯⟩

explanatories.QuadraticForm.Isometry.inl: The definition characterizes the inclusion of a quadratic form into the product of two modules as an isometry related to the first component of the product.
explanatories.QuadraticForm.Isometry.inr: An isometry between a quadratic form and the product of another quadratic form with a second module can be defined through the second component's inclusion into their product.

CliffordAlgebra.toProd.eq_1.description: This theorem asserts that the canonical structure of the Clifford algebra associated with the product of two quadratic forms can be represented as a specific lift of their even components, incorporating the maps defined by the isometries of each form.

CliffordAlgebra.foldr.code:
CliffordAlgebra.foldr.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M]
  [AddCommGroup N] [Module R M] [Module R N] (Q : QuadraticForm R M) (f : M →ₗ[R] N →ₗ[R] N)
  (hf : ∀ (m : M) (x : N), (f m) ((f m) x) = Q m • x) : N →ₗ[R] CliffordAlgebra Q →ₗ[R] N
CliffordAlgebra.foldr.comment:
Fold a bilinear map along the generators of a term of the clifford algebra, with the rule
given by `foldr Q f hf n (ι Q m * x) = f m (foldr Q f hf n x)`.

For example, `foldr f hf n (r • ι R u + ι R v * ι R w) = r • f u n + f v (f w n)`.

explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.lift: This definition establishes a correspondence between a specific type of linear map satisfying a quadratic form condition and the morphisms of algebras from the Clifford algebra associated with that quadratic form to any given algebra.
explanatories.LinearMap.ext: This theorem states that if two linear maps agree on all inputs, then they are equal as functions.
explanatories.LinearMap.flip: This definition describes a process that takes a bilinear map and rearranges the order of its variables to form a new linear map.
explanatories.List.foldr: This definition describes a function that recursively processes the elements of a list from right to left, applying a specified binary function and accumulating a result starting from a given initial value.
explanatories.Prod.ext: If two pairs of elements have equal first components and equal second components, then the pairs themselves are equal.

CliffordAlgebra.foldr.description: This definition describes a way to fold a bilinear map through the generators of a Clifford algebra using a specified rule and a quadratic form.

CliffordAlgebra.foldl.comment:
Fold a bilinear map along the generators of a term of the clifford algebra, with the rule
given by `foldl Q f hf n (ι Q m * x) = f m (foldl Q f hf n x)`.

For example, `foldl f hf n (r • ι R u + ι R v * ι R w) = r • f u n + f v (f w n)`.

explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.reverse: This definition represents a linear map that performs grade reversion by inverting the multiplication order of the basis vectors in the Clifford algebra.
explanatories.List.foldl: This defines a function that iteratively applies a binary operation to elements of a list, accumulating a result by processing the list from left to right, starting with an initial value.

CliffordAlgebra.foldr'Aux.fullDefinition: def foldr'Aux (f : M →ₗ[R] CliffordAlgebra Q × N →ₗ[R] N) :     M →ₗ[R] Module.End R (CliffordAlgebra Q × N) := by   have v_mul := (Algebra.lmul R (CliffordAlgebra Q)).toLinearMap ∘ₗ ι Q   have l := v_mul.compl₂ (LinearMap.fst _ _ N)   exact     { toFun := fun m => (l m).prod (f m)       map_add' := fun v₂ v₂ =>         LinearMap.ext fun x =>           Prod.ext (LinearMap.congr_fun (l.map_add _ _) x) (LinearMap.congr_fun (f.map_add _ _) x)       map_smul' := fun c v =>         LinearMap.ext fun x =>           Prod.ext (LinearMap.congr_fun (l.map_smul _ _) x)             (LinearMap.congr_fun (f.map_smul _ _) x) }
CliffordAlgebra.foldr'Aux.description: This definition describes an auxiliary function that maps elements from a module, combined with a quadratic form and a linear function, to a linear endomorphism on the product of a Clifford algebra and another module.

  (hf : ∀ (m : M) (x : CliffordAlgebra Q) (fx : N), (f m) ((ι Q) m * x, (f m) (x, fx)) = Q m • fx) (n : N) :
  CliffordAlgebra Q →ₗ[R] N
CliffordAlgebra.foldr'.comment:
Fold a bilinear map along the generators of a term of the clifford algebra, with the rule
given by `foldr' Q f hf n (ι Q m * x) = f m (x, foldr' Q f hf n x)`.
Note this is like `CliffordAlgebra.foldr`, but with an extra `x` argument.
Implement the recursion scheme `F[n0](m * x) = f(m, (x, F[n0](x)))`.

explanatories.QuadraticForm: A quadratic form is defined as a mathematical structure that specifies a polynomial of degree two associated with a module over a commutative semiring.
explanatories.QuadraticForm.baseChange: This definition introduces a quadratic form defined over a larger ring obtained by base changing a given quadratic form from one commutative ring to another, while extending the module structure to accommodate this change.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.lift: This definition establishes a correspondence between a specific type of linear map satisfying a quadratic form condition and the morphisms of algebras from the Clifford algebra associated with that quadratic form to any given algebra.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This theorem states that for any element and a property it satisfies, one can construct a subtype consisting of elements that possess that property.
explanatories.LinearMap.restrictScalars: This definition specifies the process of restricting an S-linear map between two modules to an R-linear map when both modules are compatible with their respective scalar actions.
explanatories.TensorProduct.mk: This definition describes a canonical bilinear map that takes an element from one module and another from a second module and produces an element in their tensor product.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.ι_sq_scalar: This theorem shows that the image of a vector under the inclusion map in the Clifford algebra squared is equal to the image of that vector's quadratic form through the algebra map from the commutative ring to the Clifford algebra.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.one_mul: This theorem asserts that multiplying any element by the identity element in a multiplicative structure results in the element itself.
explanatories.Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one: This theorem shows that the image of a scalar under the algebra map from a commutative semiring to its algebra structure is equivalent to the scalar multiplied by the identity element of the algebra.
explanatories.IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply: This theorem shows that in a scalar tower involving two commutative semirings and an algebra, applying the algebra map from the first semiring to the algebra equals applying the algebra map from the second semiring to the algebra after first applying the algebra map from the first semiring to the second semiring.
explanatories.Algebra.TensorProduct.lift: This definition establishes a construction for a unique algebra homomorphism from the tensor product of two algebras to a third algebra, given two commuting algebra homomorphisms from each factor to the third algebra.

CliffordAlgebra.ofBaseChangeAux.fullDefinition: noncomputable def ofBaseChangeAux (Q : QuadraticForm R V) :     CliffordAlgebra Q →ₐ[R] CliffordAlgebra (Q.baseChange A) :=   CliffordAlgebra.lift Q <| by     refine ⟨(ι (Q.baseChange A)).restrictScalars R ∘ₗ TensorProduct.mk R A V 1, fun v => ?_⟩     refine (CliffordAlgebra.ι_sq_scalar (Q.baseChange A) (1 ⊗ₜ v)).trans ?_     rw [QuadraticForm.baseChange_tmul, one_mul, ← Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one,       ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply]
CliffordAlgebra.ofBaseChangeAux.description: This definition gives a construction that relates the Clifford algebra of a quadratic form to the Clifford algebra of its base change over another commutative ring.

CliffordAlgebra.toBaseChange.fullDefinition: noncomputable def toBaseChange (Q : QuadraticForm R V) :     CliffordAlgebra (Q.baseChange A) →ₐ[A] A ⊗[R] CliffordAlgebra Q :=   CliffordAlgebra.lift _ <| by     refine ⟨TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.map (LinearMap.id : A →ₗ[A] A) (ι Q), ?_⟩     letI : Invertible (2 : A) := (Invertible.map (algebraMap R A) 2).copy 2 (map_ofNat _ _).symm     letI : Invertible (2 : A ⊗[R] CliffordAlgebra Q) :=       (Invertible.map (algebraMap R _) 2).copy 2 (map_ofNat _ _).symm     suffices hpure_tensor : ∀ v w, (1 * 1) ⊗ₜ[R] (ι Q v * ι Q w) + (1 * 1) ⊗ₜ[R] (ι Q w * ι Q v) =         QuadraticMap.polarBilin (Q.baseChange A) (1 ⊗ₜ[R] v) (1 ⊗ₜ[R] w) ⊗ₜ[R] 1 by       -- the crux is that by converting to a statement about linear maps instead of quadratic forms,       -- we then have access to all the partially-applied `ext` lemmas.       rw [CliffordAlgebra.forall_mul_self_eq_iff (isUnit_of_invertible _)]       refine TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.curry_injective ?_       ext v w       dsimp       exact hpure_tensor v w     intros v w     rw [← TensorProduct.tmul_add, CliffordAlgebra.ι_mul_ι_add_swap,       QuadraticForm.polarBilin_baseChange, LinearMap.BilinMap.baseChange_tmul, one_mul,       TensorProduct.smul_tmul, Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one, QuadraticMap.polarBilin_apply_apply]

explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.ι_sq_scalar: This theorem shows that the image of a vector under the inclusion map in the Clifford algebra squared is equal to the image of that vector's quadratic form through the algebra map from the commutative ring to the Clifford algebra.

explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.ι_mul_ι_add_swap: This theorem states that the product of two images from a quadratic form's embedding, when added in the reverse order, equals the algebraic map of the quadratic form's polar associated with those two vectors.
explanatories.QuadraticMap.polar: This definition describes a bilinear map associated with a quadratic map, which takes two elements from one additive group and produces an element in another additive group.

CliffordAlgebraQuaternion.quaternionBasi.fullDefinition: def quaternionBasis : QuaternionAlgebra.Basis (CliffordAlgebra (Q c₁ c₂)) c₁ c₂ where   i := ι (Q c₁ c₂) (1, 0)   j := ι (Q c₁ c₂) (0, 1)   k := ι (Q c₁ c₂) (1, 0) * ι (Q c₁ c₂) (0, 1)   i_mul_i := by     rw [ι_sq_scalar, Q_apply, ← Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one]     simp   j_mul_j := by     rw [ι_sq_scalar, Q_apply, ← Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one]     simp   i_mul_j := rfl   j_mul_i := by     rw [eq_neg_iff_add_eq_zero, ι_mul_ι_add_swap, QuadraticMap.polar]     simp
CliffordAlgebraQuaternion.quaternionBasi.description: This definition describes the basis vectors of a quaternion algebra within the context of a specific Clifford algebra determined by two coefficients from a commutative ring.

CliffordAlgebraQuaternion.ofQuaternion_m.code:

explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.ι: This definition describes a canonical linear map from a module associated with a quadratic form to its corresponding Clifford algebra.
explanatories.QuadraticForm: A quadratic form is defined as a mathematical structure that specifies a polynomial of degree two associated with a module over a commutative semiring.
explanatories.Algebra.commutes: This theorem asserts that in an algebra over a commutative semiring, the multiplication of a scalar from the semiring and an element from the algebra is commutative.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.reverse.commutes: This theorem asserts that the reversal operation in the Clifford algebra leaves the images of scalars from the base ring unchanged.
explanatories.LinearMap.zero_apply: This theorem asserts that applying a linear map to the zero element of a module yields the zero element in the codomain.
explanatories.LinearMap.ext: This theorem states that if two linear maps agree on all inputs, then they are equal as functions.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom: This definition asserts that if there exists an algebra homomorphism between two algebras and its inverse, then the two algebras are isomorphic as algebras over the given commutative semiring.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.lift: This definition establishes a correspondence between a specific type of linear map satisfying a quadratic form condition and the morphisms of algebras from the Clifford algebra associated with that quadratic form to any given algebra.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Algebra.ofId: This definition describes a function that represents the algebra map from a commutative semiring to an algebra over that semiring.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebraRing.equiv: This definition establishes an algebraic isomorphism between the Clifford algebra over a zero-dimensional vector space and the underlying scalar field.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.lift_ι_apply: This theorem states that the application of the lift of a quadratic form to the image of an element under an injective map equals the result of applying that map to the element itself.
explanatories.Complex.lift: This definition introduces a unique isomorphism that associates each element in a ring with a square of negative one to a homomorphism from the complex numbers to any real algebra containing that element.
explanatories.AlgHom.comp_apply: This theorem states that the composition of two algebra homomorphisms applied to an element from the source algebra yields the same result as applying the two homomorphisms sequentially to that element.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp_apply: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of two linear maps applied to an element yields the same result as applying each map sequentially to that element.
explanatories.AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply: This theorem asserts that applying an algebra homomorphism to an element yields the same result as applying the corresponding linear map derived from the homomorphism.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebraComplex.equiv: This definition asserts that the Clifford algebra associated with a specific quadratic form is isomorphic to the complex numbers as a real algebra.
explanatories.AlgHom.commutes: This theorem demonstrates that an algebra homomorphism commutes with the algebra maps from a commutative semiring to its algebras.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebraQuaternion.equiv: This definition establishes that the Clifford algebra associated with a specific quadratic form is isomorphic to the quaternion algebra over a given commutative ring.
explanatories.QuadraticMap.zero_apply: This theorem states that the application of the zero quadratic map to any input results in zero.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebraDualNumber.ι_mul_ι: This theorem states that the product of two elements represented as the image of zero under a specific embedding in the Clifford algebra results in zero.
explanatories.TrivSqZeroExt.inr_mul_inr: This theorem asserts that the product of two elements, each injected into the trivial square-zero extension, is equal to zero.
explanatories.DualNumber.lift: This definition establishes an isomorphism between a certain structure involving a commutative semiring and its dual numbers, ensuring a unique algebra homomorphism for every map between two algebras given specific commutativity and nilpotence conditions.
explanatories.AlgHom.coe_comp: This theorem establishes that the composition of two algebra homomorphisms corresponds to the composition of their underlying functions.
explanatories.Function.comp_apply: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.
explanatories.DualNumber.lift_apply_eps: This theorem shows that when the lifting operation is applied to the unit element of the dual numbers, it yields the unique element in the target that squares to zero.
explanatories.AlgHom.coe_id: This theorem asserts that the identity algebra homomorphism is equivalent to the identity function on the corresponding algebra.
explanatories.id_eq: The identity function returns each element unchanged, establishing that applying it to any element results in that same element.
explanatories.AlgHom.comp_toLinearMap: This theorem states that the composition of two algebra homomorphisms can be expressed as the composition of their corresponding linear maps.
explanatories.LinearMap.coe_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the function corresponding to the composition of two linear maps is equivalent to the composition of their respective functions.
explanatories.AlgHom.toLinearMap_id: This theorem states that the identity algebra homomorphism from an algebra to itself corresponds to the identity linear map on that algebra.
explanatories.LinearMap.id_comp: This theorem confirms that the composition of an identity linear map with any linear map results in the original linear map unchanged.
