explanatories.Module.Dual: The dual space of an R-module is defined as the set of all linear maps from that module to the ring R, forming an R-module itself.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.contractLeftAux: This definition describes an auxiliary function that facilitates the contraction of elements in a Clifford algebra by mapping a vector to a bilinear map involving pairs of Clifford algebra elements.
explanatories.mul_smul_comm: This theorem demonstrates that in the presence of a commutativity condition for scalar multiplication, the operation of multiplying an element by a scalar and then scaling another element is equivalent to first scaling the second element and then multiplying the two results.
explanatories.zero_add: This theorem establishes that adding zero to any element in an additive structure results in that same element.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.contractLeftAux_contract: This theorem establishes a relationship between the contraction of two Clifford algebra elements and a quadratic form evaluated at a vector, demonstrating how the contraction operation acts on this algebraic structure.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.foldr': This definition outlines a process for folding a bilinear map across the generators of a Clifford algebra using a specified rule that incorporates an additional argument from the algebra.
explanatories.LinearMap.ext: This theorem states that if two linear maps agree on all inputs, then they are equal as functions.
explanatories.LinearMap.add_apply: This theorem states that the sum of two linear maps applied to an element of their domain equals the sum of the results obtained by applying each individual map to that element.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.left_induction: This theorem provides a technique to prove a property for all elements of a Clifford algebra by showing that it holds for scalars, is closed under addition, and is preserved under multiplication by elements of the associated module.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.foldr'_algebraMap: This theorem establishes that applying a specific bilinear map in conjunction with a quadratic form to a scalar value in the Clifford algebra yields a linear combination with the original scalar multiplied by a given element.
explanatories.map_add: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.add_add_add_comm: The sum of four elements can be rearranged by grouping them in different ways within a commutative additive semigroup.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.foldr'_ι_mul: This theorem shows that when applying a specific folding operation on a bilinear map and a quadratic form, multiplying an element from the Clifford algebra by a vector leads to an equality involving the transformation of the vector and the output from the folding operation.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.contractLeftAux_apply_ap: This theorem establishes an equation that relates the result of applying an auxiliary contraction function to a vector and a pair of Clifford algebra elements to the scaled first component and the product involving the second component of the pair.
explanatories.sub_add_sub_comm: In a commutative subtraction monoid, the expression of subtraction and addition can be rearranged without altering the result.
explanatories.mul_add: This theorem states that in a structure where multiplication is left distributive over addition, the product of an element and the sum of two other elements equals the sum of the products of the first element with each of the other two elements.
explanatories.add_smul: This theorem states that the operation of scalar multiplication distributes over the addition of scalars in a module.
explanatories.LinearMap.smul_apply: This theorem states that applying a scalar multiplication to a linear map and then to a vector results in the same output as applying the scalar multiplication directly to the image of the vector under the linear map.
explanatories.RingHom.id_apply: This theorem states that the identity ring homomorphism returns any element from the semiring unchanged.
explanatories.smul_assoc: This theorem states that in a scalar tower structure involving multiple scalar multiplications, applying the scalars in succession produces the same result as applying the first scalar and then multiplying the outcome by the second scalar.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul': This theorem asserts that a specific linear map interacts with scalar multiplication in such a way that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is equivalent to multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar's image under a specified semiring homomorphism.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.ext: This theorem establishes that if two linear equivalences agree on their action for all elements, then they are identical.

CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft.fullDefinition: def contractLeft : Module.Dual R M →ₗ[R] CliffordAlgebra Q →ₗ[R] CliffordAlgebra Q where   toFun d := foldr' Q (contractLeftAux Q d) (contractLeftAux_contractLeftAux Q d) 0   map_add' d₁ d₂ :=     LinearMap.ext fun x => by       dsimp only       rw [LinearMap.add_apply]       induction' x using CliffordAlgebra.left_induction with r x y hx hy m x hx       · simp_rw [foldr'_algebraMap, smul_zero, zero_add]       · rw [map_add, map_add, map_add, add_add_add_comm, hx, hy]       · rw [foldr'_ι_mul, foldr'_ι_mul, foldr'_ι_mul, hx]         dsimp only [contractLeftAux_apply_apply]         rw [sub_add_sub_comm, mul_add, LinearMap.add_apply, add_smul]   map_smul' c d :=     LinearMap.ext fun x => by       dsimp only       rw [LinearMap.smul_apply, RingHom.id_apply]       induction' x using CliffordAlgebra.left_induction with r x y hx hy m x hx       · simp_rw [foldr'_algebraMap, smul_zero]       · rw [map_add, map_add, smul_add, hx, hy]       · rw [foldr'_ι_mul, foldr'_ι_mul, hx]         dsimp only [contractLeftAux_apply_apply]         rw [LinearMap.smul_apply, smul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, smul_sub]

explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft: This definition describes a linear operation that permits the contraction of elements in a Clifford algebra with a dual module element from the left side.

  CliffordAlgebra Q ≃ₗ[R] CliffordAlgebra Q'
CliffordAlgebra.changeFormEquiv.comment:
Any two algebras whose quadratic forms differ by a bilinear form are isomorphic as modules.

This is $\bar \lambda_B$ from [bourbaki2007][] $9 Proposition 3.

explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.changeForm.neg_proof: This theorem asserts that negating a bilinear map leads to a quadratic map that represents the difference between two quadratic forms in reverse order.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.changeForm_self_apply: This theorem states that applying a change of form operation to an element of a Clifford algebra based on a given quadratic form results in the same element, indicating that the operation is an identity on that element.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.changeForm_changeForm: This theorem shows that the operation of changing forms twice, under certain conditions on quadratic forms and bilinear maps, results in a single equivalent change of form.
explanatories.add_neg_self: This theorem establishes that the sum of any element and its additive inverse in an additive group equals the identity element, which is zero.
explanatories.add_left_neg: This theorem asserts that in an additive group, the sum of an element and its additive inverse equals the zero element.

clifford_algebra.even_hom.compr₂.fullDefinition: def EvenHom.compr₂ (g : EvenHom Q A) (f : A →ₐ[R] B) : EvenHom Q B where   bilin := g.bilin.compr₂ f.toLinearMap   contract _m := (f.congr_arg <| g.contract _).trans <| f.commutes _   contract_mid _m₁ _m₂ _m₃ :=     (map_mul f _ _).symm.trans <| (f.congr_arg <| g.contract_mid _ _ _).trans <| map_smul f _ _

CliffordAlgebra.even.ι.fullDefinition: nonrec def even.ι : EvenHom Q (even Q) where   bilin :=     LinearMap.mk₂ R (fun m₁ m₂ => ⟨ι Q m₁ * ι Q m₂, ι_mul_ι_mem_evenOdd_zero Q _ _⟩)       (fun _ _ _ => by simp only [LinearMap.map_add, add_mul]; rfl)       (fun _ _ _ => by simp only [LinearMap.map_smul, smul_mul_assoc]; rfl)       (fun _ _ _ => by simp only [LinearMap.map_add, mul_add]; rfl) fun _ _ _ => by       simp only [LinearMap.map_smul, mul_smul_comm]; rfl   contract m := Subtype.ext <| ι_sq_scalar Q m   contract_mid m₁ m₂ m₃ :=     Subtype.ext <|       calc         ι Q m₁ * ι Q m₂ * (ι Q m₂ * ι Q m₃) = ι Q m₁ * (ι Q m₂ * ι Q m₂ * ι Q m₃) := by           simp only [mul_assoc]         _ = Q m₂ • (ι Q m₁ * ι Q m₃) := by rw [Algebra.smul_def, ι_sq_scalar, Algebra.left_comm]

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.comment:
An auxiliary submodule used to store the half-applied values of `f`.
This is the span of elements `f'` such that `∃ x m₂, ∀ m₁, f' m₁ = f m₁ m₂ * x`.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.fullDefinition: private def S : Submodule R (M →ₗ[R] A) :=   Submodule.span R     {f' | ∃ x m₂, f' = LinearMap.lcomp R _ (f.bilin.flip m₂) (LinearMap.mulRight R x)}

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.fullDefinition: private def fFold : M →ₗ[R] A × S f →ₗ[R] A × S f :=   LinearMap.mk₂ R     (fun m acc =>       /- We could write this `snd` term in a point-free style as follows, but it wouldn't help as we         don't have any prod or subtype combinators to deal with n-linear maps of this degree.         ```lean         (LinearMap.lcomp R _ (Algebra.lmul R A).to_linear_map.flip).comp <|           (LinearMap.llcomp R M A A).flip.comp f.flip : M →ₗ[R] A →ₗ[R] M →ₗ[R] A)         ```         -/       (acc.2.val m,         ⟨(LinearMap.mulRight R acc.1).comp (f.bilin.flip m), Submodule.subset_span <| ⟨_, _, rfl⟩⟩))     (fun m₁ m₂ a =>       Prod.ext (LinearMap.map_add _ m₁ m₂)         (Subtype.ext <|           LinearMap.ext fun m₃ =>             show f.bilin m₃ (m₁ + m₂) * a.1 = f.bilin m₃ m₁ * a.1 + f.bilin m₃ m₂ * a.1 by               rw [map_add, add_mul]))     (fun c m a =>       Prod.ext (LinearMap.map_smul _ c m)         (Subtype.ext <|           LinearMap.ext fun m₃ =>             show f.bilin m₃ (c • m) * a.1 = c • (f.bilin m₃ m * a.1) by               rw [LinearMap.map_smul, smul_mul_assoc]))     (fun m a₁ a₂ => Prod.ext rfl (Subtype.ext <| LinearMap.ext fun m₃ => mul_add _ _ _))     fun c m a => Prod.ext rfl (Subtype.ext <| LinearMap.ext fun m₃ => mul_smul_comm _ _ _)

explanatories.LinearMap.comp: This definition states that the composition of two linear maps, each between different modules over semirings, results in another linear map that connects the first and last modules directly.

explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.EquivEven.v_sq_scalar: This theorem states that the square of the embedding of a vector from a module associated with a quadratic form equals the image of the quadratic form evaluated at that vector under the algebra map into the corresponding Clifford algebra.

explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.even: This definition identifies the even submodule of the Clifford algebra corresponding to a quadratic form as a subalgebra over the base ring.

explanatories.LinearMap.codRestrict: This definition describes a linear map that restricts the codomain of a given linear map to a specified submodule, ensuring that all outputs lie within that submodule.
explanatories.Submodule.mem_iSup_of_mem: This theorem states that if an element belongs to a specific submodule within a family of submodules, then it also belongs to the least upper bound of that family.
explanatories.LinearMap.mulLeft: This definition specifies a linear map that represents left multiplication by a fixed element in a non-unital algebra.
explanatories.Subtype.coe_mk: This theorem shows that the value of an element formed by a subtype is equal to the underlying value itself when the property is satisfied.
explanatories.pow_two: This theorem states that in a monoid, the square of an element is equal to the element multiplied by itself.
explanatories.Submodule.mul_mem_mul: This theorem states that the product of two elements from two submodules is contained in the submodule generated by their product within a commutative semiring.
explanatories.LinearMap.mem_range_self: This theorem states that the image of an element under a linear map is always contained in the range of that linear map.
explanatories.Subalgebra.coe_mul: The product of two elements in a subalgebra, when viewed in the larger algebra, is equal to the product of their respective images in that algebra.
explanatories.LinearMap.codRestrict_apply: This theorem establishes that applying the restricted linear map to an element produces the same result as applying the original linear map to that element, confirming that the restriction operation preserves values in the specified submodule.
explanatories.LinearMap.mulLeft_apply: This theorem demonstrates that applying the linear map for left multiplication by an element in a non-unital algebra results in the same outcome as directly multiplying that element by another element.
explanatories.Subalgebra.coe_algebraMap: The image of an element under the algebra map from a larger commutative semiring to a subalgebra is equal to its image under the algebra map to the entire algebra.

explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.even.lift: This definition establishes a bijective correspondence between even homomorphisms associated with a quadratic form and algebra morphisms from its even subalgebra to another algebra.
explanatories.AlgHom.comp: This definition describes how to construct a new algebra homomorphism by composing two existing algebra homomorphisms that connect three algebras over a common commutative semiring.
explanatories.AlgHom.comp_apply: This theorem states that the composition of two algebra homomorphisms applied to an element from the source algebra yields the same result as applying the two homomorphisms sequentially to that element.

CliffordAlgebra.toEven.fullDefinition: def toEven : CliffordAlgebra Q →ₐ[R] CliffordAlgebra.even (Q' Q) := by   refine CliffordAlgebra.lift Q ⟨?_, fun m => ?_⟩   · refine LinearMap.codRestrict _ ?_ fun m => Submodule.mem_iSup_of_mem ⟨2, rfl⟩ ?_     · exact (LinearMap.mulLeft R <| e0 Q).comp (v Q)     rw [Subtype.coe_mk, pow_two]     exact Submodule.mul_mem_mul (LinearMap.mem_range_self _ _) (LinearMap.mem_range_self _ _)   · ext1     rw [Subalgebra.coe_mul]  -- Porting note: was part of the `dsimp only` below     erw [LinearMap.codRestrict_apply] -- Porting note: was part of the `dsimp only` below     dsimp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, Subalgebra.coe_algebraMap]     rw [← mul_assoc, e0_mul_v_mul_e0, v_sq_scalar]
CliffordAlgebra.toEven.description: This definition describes a specific algebraic embedding from a Clifford algebra associated with a quadratic form into a larger algebra that consists of even elements from the corresponding quadratic form.

CliffordAlgebra.ofEven.fullDefinition: def ofEven : CliffordAlgebra.even (Q' Q) →ₐ[R] CliffordAlgebra Q := by   /-     Recall that we need:      * `f ⟨0,1⟩ ⟨x,0⟩ = ι x`      * `f ⟨x,0⟩ ⟨0,1⟩ = -ι x`      * `f ⟨x,0⟩ ⟨y,0⟩ = ι x * ι y`      * `f ⟨0,1⟩ ⟨0,1⟩ = -1`     -/   let f : M × R →ₗ[R] M × R →ₗ[R] CliffordAlgebra Q :=     ((Algebra.lmul R (CliffordAlgebra Q)).toLinearMap.comp <|           (ι Q).comp (LinearMap.fst _ _ _) +             (Algebra.linearMap R _).comp (LinearMap.snd _ _ _)).compl₂       ((ι Q).comp (LinearMap.fst _ _ _) - (Algebra.linearMap R _).comp (LinearMap.snd _ _ _))   haveI f_apply : ∀ x y, f x y = (ι Q x.1 + algebraMap R _ x.2) * (ι Q y.1 - algebraMap R _ y.2) :=     fun x y => by rfl   haveI hc : ∀ (r : R) (x : CliffordAlgebra Q), Commute (algebraMap _ _ r) x := Algebra.commutes   haveI hm :     ∀ m : M × R,       ι Q m.1 * ι Q m.1 - algebraMap R _ m.2 * algebraMap R _ m.2 = algebraMap R _ (Q' Q m) := by     intro m     rw [ι_sq_scalar, ← RingHom.map_mul, ← RingHom.map_sub, sub_eq_add_neg, Q'_apply, sub_eq_add_neg]   refine even.lift (Q' Q) ⟨f, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> simp_rw [f_apply]   · intro m     rw [← (hc _ _).symm.mul_self_sub_mul_self_eq, hm]   · intro m₁ m₂ m₃     rw [← mul_smul_comm, ← mul_assoc, mul_assoc (_ + _), ← (hc _ _).symm.mul_self_sub_mul_self_eq',       Algebra.smul_def, ← mul_assoc, hm]

CliffordAlgebra.ofEven_ι.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
  (Q : QuadraticForm R M) (x y : M × R) :
  (ofEven Q) (((even.ι (Q' Q)).bilin x) y) =

CliffordAlgebra.evenEquivEvenNeg.comment:

ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti.fullDefinition: def ιMulti (n : ℕ) : M [⋀^Fin n]→ₗ[R] ExteriorAlgebra R M :=   let F := (MultilinearMap.mkPiAlgebraFin R n (ExteriorAlgebra R M)).compLinearMap fun _ => ι R   { F with     map_eq_zero_of_eq' := fun f x y hfxy hxy => by       dsimp [F]       clear F       wlog h : x < y       · exact this R (A := A) n f y x hfxy.symm hxy.symm (hxy.lt_or_lt.resolve_left h)       clear hxy       induction' n with n hn       · exact x.elim0       · rw [List.ofFn_succ, List.prod_cons]         by_cases hx : x = 0         -- one of the repeated terms is on the left         · rw [hx] at hfxy h           rw [hfxy, ← Fin.succ_pred y (ne_of_lt h).symm]           exact ι_mul_prod_list (f ∘ Fin.succ) _         -- ignore the left-most term and induct on the remaining ones, decrementing indices         · convert mul_zero (ι R (f 0))           refine             hn               (fun i => f <| Fin.succ i) (x.pred hx)               (y.pred (ne_of_lt <| lt_of_le_of_lt x.zero_le h).symm) ?_               (Fin.pred_lt_pred_iff.mpr h)           simp only [Fin.succ_pred]           exact hfxy     toFun := F }

exterior_algebra.ι_multi.fullDefinition: def ιMulti (n : ℕ) : M [⋀^Fin n]→ₗ[R] ExteriorAlgebra R M :=   let F := (MultilinearMap.mkPiAlgebraFin R n (ExteriorAlgebra R M)).compLinearMap fun _ => ι R   { F with     map_eq_zero_of_eq' := fun f x y hfxy hxy => by       dsimp [F]       clear F       wlog h : x < y       · exact this R (A := A) n f y x hfxy.symm hxy.symm (hxy.lt_or_lt.resolve_left h)       clear hxy       induction' n with n hn       · exact x.elim0       · rw [List.ofFn_succ, List.prod_cons]         by_cases hx : x = 0         -- one of the repeated terms is on the left         · rw [hx] at hfxy h           rw [hfxy, ← Fin.succ_pred y (ne_of_lt h).symm]           exact ι_mul_prod_list (f ∘ Fin.succ) _         -- ignore the left-most term and induct on the remaining ones, decrementing indices         · convert mul_zero (ι R (f 0))           refine             hn               (fun i => f <| Fin.succ i) (x.pred hx)               (y.pred (ne_of_lt <| lt_of_le_of_lt x.zero_le h).symm) ?_               (Fin.pred_lt_pred_iff.mpr h)           simp only [Fin.succ_pred]           exact hfxy     toFun := F }

ExteriorAlgebra.map.comment: The morphism of exterior algebras induced by a linear map.

explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.map: This definition describes how any linear map that maintains a quadratic form can be extended to a homomorphism between the corresponding Clifford algebras.
explanatories.Submodule.map: This definition describes the construction of a new submodule in a different module by applying a semilinear map to the elements of an existing submodule.
explanatories.TrivSqZeroExt.map: This definition establishes a method for creating an algebra homomorphism from the trivial square-zero extension of one module to that of another, using a linear map between the two modules when the underlying ring is commutative.

ExteriorAlgebra.map.description: This definition describes the process of constructing a morphism between exterior algebras that is induced by a linear map between two modules.

ExteriorAlgebra.map_apply_ι.description: This theorem states that the application of a linear map to the image of a module element under the inclusion map into the exterior algebra corresponds to the image of that element under the linear map, also mapped through the inclusion into the exterior algebra.

explanatories.LinearMap.comp: This definition states that the composition of two linear maps, each between different modules over semirings, results in another linear map that connects the first and last modules directly.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.map: This definition describes how any linear map that maintains a quadratic form can be extended to a homomorphism between the corresponding Clifford algebras.
explanatories.ExteriorAlgebra.map: This definition describes the process of constructing a morphism between exterior algebras that is induced by a linear map between two modules.
explanatories.AlgHom.comp: This definition describes how to construct a new algebra homomorphism by composing two existing algebra homomorphisms that connect three algebras over a common commutative semiring.
explanatories.Submodule.map: This definition describes the construction of a new submodule in a different module by applying a semilinear map to the elements of an existing submodule.
explanatories.TrivSqZeroExt.map: This definition establishes a method for creating an algebra homomorphism from the trivial square-zero extension of one module to that of another, using a linear map between the two modules when the underlying ring is commutative.

ExteriorAlgebra.toTrivSqZeroExt_comp_map.description: This theorem asserts that the composition of a trivial square zero extension with a linear map in the context of exterior algebras is equivalent to the composition of a map of those extensions with the original trivial square zero extension.

ExteriorAlgebra.leftInverse_map_iff.comment:
For a linear map `f` from `M` to `N`,
`ExteriorAlgebra.map g` is a retraction of `ExteriorAlgebra.map f` iff
`g` is a retraction of `f`.

explanatories.Function.LeftInverse: This definition establishes the concept of a function being a left inverse, indicating that when one function is applied after another, the result is the identity function.

ExteriorAlgebra.leftInverse_map_iff.description: This theorem states that a linear map from one module to another induces a left inverse relationship between their corresponding exterior algebra maps if and only if the original maps themselves have a left inverse relationship.

ExteriorAlgebra.ιInv_comp_map.description: This theorem asserts that the composition of the inverse inclusion map with a linear map applied to the exterior algebra is equivalent to applying the linear map to the inverse inclusion map directly.

ExteriorAlgebra.map_injective.description: This theorem states that if a module homomorphism has a linear retraction, then the corresponding induced map on the exterior algebra is injective.

explanatories.LinearMap.compr₂: This defines a bilinear map created by composing a linear map from one module to another with a bilinear map from a third module to the first two modules.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.toLinearMap: This definition constructs a linear map from one module to another using a linear equivalence that relates the two modules through compatible ring homomorphisms.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp: This definition states that the composition of two linear maps, each between different modules over semirings, results in another linear map that connects the first and last modules directly.
explanatories.LinearMap.proj: This definition introduces a linear map that extracts a specific component from a family of modules indexed by a set.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm: This definition specifies the symmetry of linear equivalences, indicating that the inverse relationship between two modules can be expressed as a linear equivalence in the opposite direction.
explanatories.CliffordAlgebra.foldl: This definition describes a method for folding a bilinear map along generators of a Clifford algebra using a specified rule that incorporates a quadratic form and a bilinear function.
explanatories.LinearMap.mk₂: This definition establishes a method for constructing a bilinear map from a function that exhibits linear behavior separately in each of its two input components.
explanatories.Nat.succ: This states the successor function for natural numbers, which yields the next integer by adding one to a given natural number.
explanatories.AlternatingMap.curryLeft: This definition describes a process for transforming an alternating map that takes one more variable into a linear map that produces alternating maps with one fewer variable by fixing the first input.
explanatories.map_smul: This theorem states that a morphism that is equivariant with respect to the actions of a monoid preserves the action when applied to the product of an element from the monoid and an element from the type.
explanatories.map_add: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.Pi.add_apply: This theorem examines the behavior of function composition involving a constant function that returns the "one" value.

explanatories.AlternatingMap.curryLeft_add: Theorem states that the left curry operation is distributive over the addition of alternating maps.
explanatories.AlternatingMap.curryLeft_smul: This theorem states that scaling an alternating map by a scalar on the left does not affect its left currying operation.
explanatories.LinearMap.add_apply: This theorem states that the sum of two linear maps applied to an element of their domain equals the sum of the results obtained by applying each individual map to that element.
explanatories.LinearMap.smul_apply: This theorem states that applying a scalar multiplication to a linear map and then to a vector results in the same output as applying the scalar multiplication directly to the image of the vector under the linear map.
explanatories.AlternatingMap.ext: This theorem states that if two alternating maps produce the same output for all inputs, then the maps themselves are equal.

ExteriorAlgebra.liftAlternating.fullDefinition: def liftAlternating : (∀ i, M [⋀^Fin i]→ₗ[R] N) →ₗ[R] ExteriorAlgebra R M →ₗ[R] N := by   suffices     (∀ i, M [⋀^Fin i]→ₗ[R] N) →ₗ[R]       ExteriorAlgebra R M →ₗ[R] ∀ i, M [⋀^Fin i]→ₗ[R] N by     refine LinearMap.compr₂ this ?_     refine (LinearEquiv.toLinearMap ?_).comp (LinearMap.proj 0)     exact AlternatingMap.constLinearEquivOfIsEmpty.symm   refine CliffordAlgebra.foldl _ ?_ ?_   · refine       LinearMap.mk₂ R (fun m f i => (f i.succ).curryLeft m) (fun m₁ m₂ f => ?_) (fun c m f => ?_)         (fun m f₁ f₂ => ?_) fun c m f => ?_     all_goals       ext i : 1       simp only [map_smul, map_add, Pi.add_apply, Pi.smul_apply, AlternatingMap.curryLeft_add,         AlternatingMap.curryLeft_smul, map_add, map_smul, LinearMap.add_apply, LinearMap.smul_apply]   · -- when applied twice with the same `m`, this recursive step produces 0     intro m x     ext     simp

Polynomial.annIdeal.code:
Polynomial.annIdeal.{u_1, u_2} (R : Type u_1) {A : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] (a : A) :
  Ideal R[X]
Polynomial.annIdeal.comment:
`annIdeal R a` is the *annihilating ideal* of all `p : R[X]` such that `p(a) = 0`.

The informal notation `p(a)` stand for `Polynomial.aeval a p`.
Again informally, the annihilating ideal of `a` is
`{ p ∈ R[X] | p(a) = 0 }`. This is an ideal in `R[X]`.
The formal definition uses the kernel of the aeval map.

explanatories.RingHom.ker: The kernel of a ring homomorphism is defined as an ideal in the domain of that homomorphism.
explanatories.AlgHom.toRingHom: This definition provides a way to interpret an algebra homomorphism as a ring homomorphism, preserving the algebraic structures involved.

Polynomial.annIdeal.fullDefinition: noncomputable def annIdeal (a : A) : Ideal R[X] :=   RingHom.ker ((aeval a).toRingHom : R[X] →+* A)
Polynomial.annIdeal.description: This defines the annihilating ideal of a given element in a polynomial ring, consisting of all polynomials that evaluate to zero when applied to that element.

Polynomial.annIdealGenerator.code: Polynomial.annIdealGenerator.{u_1, u_2} (𝕜 : Type u_1) {A : Type u_2} [Field 𝕜] [Ring A] [Algebra 𝕜 A] (a : A) : 𝕜[X]
Polynomial.annIdealGenerator.comment:
`annIdealGenerator 𝕜 a` is the monic generator of `annIdeal 𝕜 a`
if one exists, otherwise `0`.

Since `𝕜[X]` is a principal ideal domain there is a polynomial `g` such that
 `span 𝕜 {g} = annIdeal a`. This picks some generator.
 We prefer the monic generator of the ideal.

explanatories.Submodule.IsPrincipal.generator: The generator of a principal submodule is an element in the module such that the submodule is equal to the span of that element.
explanatories.Polynomial.C: This definition specifies a ring homomorphism that maps a constant from a semiring to the corresponding constant polynomial in a polynomial ring.

LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix.comment: `charpoly f` is the characteristic polynomial of the matrix of `f` in any basis.

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.Matrix.charpoly: This definition establishes the characteristic polynomial of a square matrix as the determinant of the difference between a scalar multiple of the identity matrix and the matrix itself.

LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix.description: This theorem states that the characteristic polynomial of a linear map is equal to the characteristic polynomial of its matrix representation in any basis of the vector space.

Module.End.IsSemisimple.code:
Module.End.IsSemisimple.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
  (f : End R M) : Prop
Module.End.IsSemisimple.comment:
A linear endomorphism of an `R`-module `M` is called *semisimple* if the induced `R[X]`-module
structure on `M` is semisimple. This is equivalent to saying that every `f`-invariant `R`-submodule
of `M` has an `f`-invariant complement: see `Module.End.isSemisimple_iff`.

explanatories.IsSemisimpleModule: A module is categorized as semisimple if every submodule has a complementary submodule, meaning it can be expressed as a direct sum of simple modules.
explanatories.Polynomial.X: This definition introduces the polynomial variable, also known as the indeterminate, for polynomials over a semiring.

Module.End.IsSemisimple.description: A linear endomorphism of an R-module is considered semisimple if the induced module structure on the module is semisimple, meaning every invariant submodule has an invariant complement.

Module.End.isSemisimple_iff.code:
Module.End.isSemisimple_iff.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
  {f : End R M} : f.IsSemisimple ↔ ∀ p ≤ Submodule.comap f p, ∃ q ≤ Submodule.comap f q, IsCompl p q

explanatories.Module.End.IsSemisimple: A linear endomorphism of an R-module is considered semisimple if the induced module structure on the module is semisimple, meaning every invariant submodule has an invariant complement.
explanatories.Submodule.comap: This definition introduces the pullback of a submodule through a semilinear map, producing a corresponding submodule in the original space.

Module.End.isSemisimple_iff.description: A linear endomorphism of an R-module is semisimple if and only if for every submodule, there exists a complementary submodule such that both can be expressed with respect to the endomorphism.

Module.End.IsSemisimple_smul_iff.code:
Module.End.IsSemisimple_smul_iff.{u_2, u_3} {M : Type u_2} [AddCommGroup M] {K : Type u_3} [Field K] [Module K M]
  {f : End K M} {t : K} (ht : t ≠ 0) : (t • f).IsSemisimple ↔ f.IsSemisimple
Module.End.IsSemisimple_smul_iff.description: A scalar multiplication of a linear endomorphism by a non-zero element preserves the semisimplicity of the endomorphism.

Module.IsTorsionBy.eq_1.code:
Module.IsTorsionBy.eq_1.{u_1, u_2} (R : Type u_1) (M : Type u_2) [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
  (a : R) : IsTorsionBy R M a = ∀ ⦃x : M⦄, a • x = 0

explanatories.Ideal.span.eq_1: The span of a set in a semiring is equivalent to the submodule span generated by that set.

Module.IsTorsionBy.eq_1.description: An element of an R-module is considered torsion by a scalar if it is annihilated by that scalar, meaning multiplying it by the scalar yields zero for all elements in the module.

  [Module K M] {f : End K M} {p : K[X]} (hp : Squarefree p) (hpf : (aeval f) p = 0) : f.IsSemisimple

Module.End.isSemisimple_of_squarefree_ae.description: A linear endomorphism of an K-module is semisimple if the polynomial associated with it is squarefree and its evaluation at the endomorphism equals zero.

Module.End.IsSemisimple.aeval.description: If a linear endomorphism of a finite-dimensional module is semisimple, then the evaluation of a polynomial at that endomorphism is also semisimple.

explanatories.FiniteDimensional: This definition characterizes vector spaces as finite-dimensional if they can be understood as finite modules over a division ring.
explanatories.Algebra.adjoin: The adjoin operation defines the smallest subalgebra containing a given set of elements from an algebra over a commutative semiring.

Module.End.IsSemisimple.of_mem_adjoin_si.description: If a linear endomorphism is semisimple and another endomorphism is in the algebraic span of it, then that second endomorphism is also semisimple.

  [Module K M] {f : End K M} [FiniteDimensional K M] (hf : f.IsSemisimple) : Squarefree (minpoly K f)
Module.End.IsSemisimple.minpoly_squarefr.comment: The minimal polynomial of a semisimple endomorphism is square free

Module.End.IsSemisimple.minpoly_squarefr.description: The minimal polynomial of a semisimple linear endomorphism in a finite-dimensional module is square-free, indicating that it has no repeated roots.

Module.End.IsSemisimple.of_mem_adjoin_pa.code:
Module.End.IsSemisimple.of_mem_adjoin_pair.{u_2, u_3} {M : Type u_2} [AddCommGroup M] {K : Type u_3} [Field K]
  [Module K M] {f g : End K M} [FiniteDimensional K M] [PerfectField K] (comm : Commute f g) (hf : f.IsSemisimple)
  (hg : g.IsSemisimple) {a : End K M} (ha : a ∈ Algebra.adjoin K {f, g}) : a.IsSemisimple

explanatories.FiniteDimensional: This definition characterizes vector spaces as finite-dimensional if they can be understood as finite modules over a division ring.
explanatories.Algebra.adjoin: The adjoin operation defines the smallest subalgebra containing a given set of elements from an algebra over a commutative semiring.
explanatories.Commute: This definition states that two elements are said to commute if their multiplication is independent of the order in which they are combined.

Module.End.IsSemisimple.of_mem_adjoin_pa.description: If two semisimple linear endomorphisms commute and a third endomorphism belongs to the algebra generated by them, then that third endomorphism is also semisimple.

Module.End.exists_isNilpotent_isSemisimp.code:
Module.End.exists_isNilpotent_isSemisimple_of_separable_of_dvd_pow.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [Field K]
  [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {f : End K V} {P : K[X]} {k : ℕ} (sep : P.Separable) (nil : minpoly K f ∣ P ^ k) :
  ∃ n ∈ adjoin K {f}, ∃ s ∈ adjoin K {f}, IsNilpotent n ∧ s.IsSemisimple ∧ f = n + s

explanatories.minpoly: The minimal polynomial of an element in an algebra is a monic polynomial with coefficients in the base ring that has the smallest degree among those that have the element as a root, if it exists, or zero otherwise.
explanatories.Algebra.adjoin: The adjoin operation defines the smallest subalgebra containing a given set of elements from an algebra over a commutative semiring.
explanatories.IsNilpotent: An element is defined as nilpotent if there exists a power of that element which equals zero in the given algebraic structure.
explanatories.Module.End.IsSemisimple: A linear endomorphism of an R-module is considered semisimple if the induced module structure on the module is semisimple, meaning every invariant submodule has an invariant complement.

Module.End.exists_isNilpotent_isSemisimp.description: This theorem asserts that for a separable polynomial and a linear endomorphism whose minimal polynomial divides a power of that polynomial, there exist a nilpotent element and a semisimple element in the extension such that their sum equals the endomorphism.
